1.121.s:
sanātana uvāca
atha vratāni dvādaśyāḥ kathayāmi tavānagha /
yāni kṛtvā naro loke viṣṇoḥ priyataro bhavet //
1.121.d:
सनातन उवाच
अथ व्रतानि द्वादश्याः कथयामि तवानघ ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो लोके विष्णोः प्रियतरो भवेत् ॥
1.121.m: Sanātana said: / Now I shall tell you, O sinless one, the vows of the twelfth [day], / by performing which a man becomes very dear to Viṣṇu in the world.

1.121.s:
caitrasya śukladvādaśyāṃ madanavratamācaret /
sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kuṃbhaṃ sitatandulapūritam //
1.121.d:
चैत्रस्य शुक्लद्वादश्यां मदनव्रतमाचरेत् ।
स्थापयेदव्रणं कुंभं सिततन्दुलपूरितम् ॥
1.121.m: On the bright twelfth [day] of Caitra, one should observe the vow of Madana. / One should set up an unblemished jar filled with white rice,

1.121.s:
nānāphalayutaṃ tadvadikṣudaṇḍasamanvitam /
sitavastrayugacchannaṃ sitacandanacarccitam //
1.121.d:
नानाफलयुतं तद्वदिक्षुदण्डसमन्वितम् ।
सितवस्त्रयुगच्छन्नं सितचन्दनचर्च्चितम् ॥
1.121.m: provided with various fruits, likewise accompanied by sugarcane stalks, / covered with a pair of white cloths, and smeared with white sandalwood paste.

1.121.s:
nānābhakṣyasamopetaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ svaśaktitaḥ /
tāmrapātraṃ guḍopetaṃ tasyopari niveśayet //
1.121.d:
नानाभक्ष्यसमोपेतं सहिरण्यं स्वशक्तितः ।
ताम्रपात्रं गुडोपेतं तस्योपरि निवेशयेत् ॥
1.121.m: Furnished with various edibles, accompanied by gold according to one's means, / one should place upon it a copper vessel provided with jaggery.

1.121.s:
tatra saṃpūjayeddevaṃ kāmarūpiṇamacyutam /
gandhādyairupacāraistu sopavāso pare 'hani //
1.121.d:
तत्र संपूजयेद्देवं कामरूपिणमच्युतम् ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैस्तु सोपवासो परे ऽहनि ॥
1.121.m: There one should worship the god Acyuta, who assumes any desired form, / with offerings such as fragrant pastes; fasting, on the following day,

1.121.s:
punaḥ prātaḥ samabhyarcya brāhmaṇāya nivedayet /
brahmaṇānbhojayeccaiva tebhyo dadyācca dakṣiṇām //
1.121.d:
पुनः प्रातः समभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् ।
ब्रह्मणान्भोजयेच्चैव तेभ्यो दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.121.m: having worshipped again in the morning, one should present it to a Brahmin. / One should also feed Brahmins and give them a priestly gift.

1.121.s:
varṣamevaṃ vrataṃ kṛtvā ghṛtadhenusamanvitām /
śayyāṃ tu dadyādgurave sarvopaskarasaṃyutām //
1.121.d:
वर्षमेवं व्रतं कृत्वा घृतधेनुसमन्विताम् ।
शय्यां तु दद्याद्गुरवे सर्वोपस्करसंयुताम् ॥
1.121.m: Having observed the vow in this way for a year, one should give a bed / provided with a clarified-butter cow and equipped with all utensils to the guru,

1.121.s:
kāñcanaṃ kāmadevaṃ ca śuktāṃ gāṃ ca payasvinīm /
vāsobhirdvijadāṃpatyaṃ pūjayitvā samarpayet //
1.121.d:
काञ्चनं कामदेवं च शुक्तां गां च पयस्विनीम् ।
वासोभिर्द्विजदांपत्यं पूजयित्वा समर्पयेत् ॥
1.121.m: and a golden Kāmadeva, and a white milch cow; / having honoured a Brahmin couple with garments, one should present [these],

1.121.s:
prīyatāṃ kāmarūpī me harirityevamuccaran /
yaḥ kuryādvidhinānena madanadvādaśīvratam //
1.121.d:
प्रीयतां कामरूपी मे हरिरित्येवमुच्चरन् ।
यः कुर्याद्विधिनानेन मदनद्वादशीव्रतम् ॥
1.121.m: saying: "May Hari, who assumes any desired form, be pleased with me." / He who observes the vow of Madanadvādaśī according to this rule

1.121.s:
sa sarvapāpanirbhuktaḥ prāpnoti harisāmyatām /
asyāmeva samuddiṣṭaṃ bhartṛdvādaśikāvratam //
1.121.d:
स सर्वपापनिर्भुक्तः प्राप्नोति हरिसाम्यताम् ।
अस्यामेव समुद्दिष्टं भर्तृद्वादशिकाव्रतम् ॥
1.121.m: is freed from all sins and attains equality with Hari. / On this very [day], the vow of Bhartṛdvādaśī is prescribed.

1.121.s:
svāstṛtāṃ tatra śayyāṃ tu kṛtvātra śrīyutaṃ harim /
saṃsthāpya maṇḍapaṃ puṣpaistaduparpyupakalpayet //
1.121.d:
स्वास्तृतां तत्र शय्यां तु कृत्वात्र श्रीयुतं हरिम् ।
संस्थाप्य मण्डपं पुष्पैस्तदुपर्प्युपकल्पयेत् ॥
1.121.m: Having made a well-spread bed there, placing Hari together with Śrī upon it, / one should construct a pavilion above it with flowers.

1.121.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjya gandhādyairvratī jāgaraṇaṃ niśi /
nṛtyavāditragītādyaistataḥ prātaḥ pare 'hani //
1.121.d:
ततः संपूज्य गन्धाद्यैर्व्रती जागरणं निशि ।
नृत्यवादित्रगीताद्यैस्ततः प्रातः परे ऽहनि ॥
1.121.m: Then, having worshipped with fragrant pastes and other [offerings], the vow-keeper [spends] the night keeping vigil / with dances, musical instruments, songs, and the like; then in the morning on the following day,

1.121.s:
saśayyaṃ śrīhariṃ haimaṃ dvijagryāya nivedayet /
dvijānsaṃbhojya visṛjaddakṣiṇābhiḥ pratoṣitān //
1.121.d:
सशय्यं श्रीहरिं हैमं द्विजग्र्याय निवेदयेत् ।
द्विजान्संभोज्य विसृजद्दक्षिणाभिः प्रतोषितान् ॥
1.121.m: he should present the golden Śrīhari together with the bed to an eminent twice-born one. / Having fed the twice-born ones, he should dismiss [them], gratified with priestly gifts.

1.121.s:
evaṃ kṛtavratasyāpi dāṃpatyaṃ jāyate sthiram /
saptajanmasu bhuṅkte ca bhogān lokadvayepsitān //
1.121.d:
एवं कृतव्रतस्यापि दांपत्यं जायते स्थिरम् ।
सप्तजन्मसु भुङ्क्ते च भोगान् लोकद्वयेप्सितान् ॥
1.121.m: Even so, the marital union of one who has observed this vow becomes enduring, / and for seven births he enjoys the desired pleasures of both worlds.

1.121.s:
vaiśākhaśukladvādaśyāṃ sopavāso jitendriyaḥ /
saṃpūjya mādhavaṃ bhaktyā gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ //
1.121.d:
वैशाखशुक्लद्वादश्यां सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
संपूज्य माधवं भक्त्या गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ॥
1.121.m: On the bright twelfth [day] of Vaiśākha, fasting, with senses subdued, / having worshipped Mādhava with devotion through offerings such as fragrant pastes,

1.121.s:
pakkānnaṃ tṛptijanakaṃ madhuraṃ sodakuṃbhakam /
viprāya dadyādvidhivanmādhavaḥ prīyatāmiti //
1.121.d:
पक्कान्नं तृप्तिजनकं मधुरं सोदकुंभकम् ।
विप्राय दद्याद्विधिवन्माधवः प्रीयतामिति ॥
1.121.m: one should duly give cooked food that produces satisfaction, sweet, accompanied by a water-jar, / to a Brahmin, saying: "May Mādhava be pleased."

1.121.s:
dvādaśyāṃ jyeṣṭhaśuklāyāṃ pūjayitvā trivikramam /
gandhādyairmadhurānnāḍhyaṃ karaka vinivedayet //
1.121.d:
द्वादश्यां ज्येष्ठशुक्लायां पूजयित्वा त्रिविक्रमम् ।
गन्धाद्यैर्मधुरान्नाढ्यं करक विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.121.m: On the bright twelfth [day] of Jyeṣṭha, having worshipped Trivikrama / with fragrant pastes and other [offerings], one should present a water pot filled with sweet food.

1.121.s:
vratī dvijāya tatpaścādekabhaktaṃ samācaret /
vratenānena saṃtuṣṭo devadevastrivikramaḥ //
1.121.d:
व्रती द्विजाय तत्पश्चादेकभक्तं समाचरेत् ।
व्रतेनानेन संतुष्टो देवदेवस्त्रिविक्रमः ॥
1.121.m: After that, the vow-keeper should take a single meal. / Pleased by this vow, the god of gods Trivikrama

1.121.s:
dadāti vipulānbhogānante mokṣaṃ ca nārada /
āṣāḍhaśukladvādaśyāṃ dvijāndvādaśa bhojayet //
1.121.d:
ददाति विपुलान्भोगानन्ते मोक्षं च नारद ।
आषाढशुक्लद्वादश्यां द्विजान्द्वादश भोजयेत् ॥
1.121.m: bestows abundant pleasures and liberation at the end, O Nārada. / On the bright twelfth [day] of Āṣāḍha, one should feed twelve twice-born ones.

1.121.s:
madhurānnena tānpūjya pṛthaggandhādikaiḥ kramāt /
tabhyo vāsāṃsi daṇḍāṃśca brahmasūtrāṇi mudrikāḥ //
1.121.d:
मधुरान्नेन तान्पूज्य पृथग्गन्धादिकैः क्रमात् ।
तभ्यो वासांसि दण्डांश्च ब्रह्मसूत्राणि मुद्रिकाः ॥
1.121.m: Having honoured them with sweet food and individually with fragrant pastes and other [offerings] in order, / [one should give] them garments, staffs, sacred threads, signet rings,

1.121.s:
pātrāṇi ca dadedbhaktyā viṣṇumeṃ prīyatāmiti /
dvādaśyāṃ tu nabhaḥśukle śrīdharaṃ pūjayedvratī //
1.121.d:
पात्राणि च ददेद्भक्त्या विष्णुमें प्रीयतामिति ।
द्वादश्यां तु नभःशुक्ले श्रीधरं पूजयेद्व्रती ॥
1.121.m: and vessels with devotion, saying: "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me." / On the bright twelfth [day] of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), the vow-keeper should worship Śrīdhara

1.121.s:
gandhādyaistatparo bhaktyā dadhibhaktairdvijottamān /
saṃbhojya dakṣiṇā raupyāṃ datvā natvā visarjjayet //
1.121.d:
गन्धाद्यैस्तत्परो भक्त्या दधिभक्तैर्द्विजोत्तमान् ।
संभोज्य दक्षिणा रौप्यां दत्वा नत्वा विसर्ज्जयेत् ॥
1.121.m: with fragrant pastes and other [offerings], devoted to him; with curd-rice, having fed / the best of the twice-born and given a silver priestly gift, he should bow and dismiss them,

1.121.s:
vratenānena deveśaḥ śrīdharaḥ prīyatāmiti /
dvādaśyāṃ nabhasyaśukle vratī saṃpūjya vāmanam //
1.121.d:
व्रतेनानेन देवेशः श्रीधरः प्रीयतामिति ।
द्वादश्यां नभस्यशुक्ले व्रती संपूज्य वामनम् ॥
1.121.m: [saying:] "May Śrīdhara, the lord of gods, be pleased by this vow." / On the bright twelfth [day] of Nabhasya (Bhādrapada), the vow-keeper, having worshipped Vāmana,

1.121.s:
tadagre bhojayedviprānpāyasairdvādaśaiva ca /
sauvarṇī dakṣiṇāṃ datvā viṣṇuprītikaro bhavet //
1.121.d:
तदग्रे भोजयेद्विप्रान्पायसैर्द्वादशैव च ।
सौवर्णी दक्षिणां दत्वा विष्णुप्रीतिकरो भवेत् ॥
1.121.m: should feed precisely twelve Brahmins in front of him with milk-rice; / giving a golden priestly gift, he becomes one who pleases Viṣṇu.

1.121.s:
dvādaśyāmiṣaśuklāyāṃ padmanābhaṃ samarcayet /
gandhādyairupacāraistu tadagre bhojayeddvijān //
1.121.d:
द्वादश्यामिषशुक्लायां पद्मनाभं समर्चयेत् ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैस्तु तदग्रे भोजयेद्द्विजान् ॥
1.121.m: On the bright twelfth [day] of Iṣa (Āśvina), one should worship Padmanābha / with offerings such as fragrant pastes; in front of him one should feed twice-born ones

1.121.s:
madhurānnena vastrāḍhyāṃ sauvarṇīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadet /
vratenaitena saṃtuṣṭaḥ padmanābho dvijottama //
1.121.d:
मधुरान्नेन वस्त्राढ्यां सौवर्णीं दक्षिणां ददेत् ।
व्रतेनैतेन संतुष्टः पद्मनाभो द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.121.m: with sweet food, and should give a golden priestly gift along with garments. / Pleased by this vow, Padmanābha, O best of the twice-born,

1.121.s:
śvetadvīpagatiṃ dadyāddehabhogāṃśca vāñchitān /
kārtike kṛṣṇapakṣe tu govatsadvādaśīvratam //
1.121.d:
श्वेतद्वीपगतिं दद्याद्देहभोगांश्च वाञ्छितान् ।
कार्तिके कृष्णपक्षे तु गोवत्सद्वादशीव्रतम् ॥
1.121.m: bestows going to Śvetadvīpa and desired bodily pleasures. / In Kārttika, in the dark fortnight, however, [there is] the Govatsadvādaśī vow.

1.121.s:
tatra vatsayutāṃ gāṃ tu samālikhya sugandhibhiḥ /
candanādyaistathā puṣpamālābhiḥ prārcya tāmrake //
1.121.d:
तत्र वत्सयुतां गां तु समालिख्य सुगन्धिभिः ।
चन्दनाद्यैस्तथा पुष्पमालाभिः प्रार्च्य ताम्रके ॥
1.121.m: There, having depicted a cow together with a calf, worshipping it with fragrant / sandalwood pastes and other [unguents] and flower garlands, in a copper

1.121.s:
pātre puṣpākṣatatilairarghyaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ /
pradadyātpādamūle 'syā mantreṇānena nārada //
1.121.d:
पात्रे पुष्पाक्षततिलैरर्घ्यं कृत्वा विधानतः ।
प्रदद्यात्पादमूले ऽस्या मन्त्रेणानेन नारद ॥
1.121.m: vessel having duly prepared an arghya offering with flowers, unbroken grains, and sesame seeds, / one should present it at her feet with this mantra, O Nārada:

1.121.s:
kṣīrodārṇavasaṃbhūte surāsuranamaskṛte /
sarvadevamaye devi sarvadevairalaṅkṛte //
1.121.d:
क्षीरोदार्णवसंभूते सुरासुरनमस्कृते ।
सर्वदेवमये देवि सर्वदेवैरलङ्कृते ॥
1.121.m: "O goddess born from the ocean of milk, bowed to by gods and asuras, / comprising all gods, adorned with all gods,

1.121.s:
mātarmātargavāṃ mātargṛhāṇārghyaṃ namo 'stu te /
tato māṣādisaṃsiddhānvaṭakāṃśca nivedayet //
1.121.d:
मातर्मातर्गवां मातर्गृहाणार्घ्यं नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
ततो माषादिसंसिद्धान्वटकांश्च निवेदयेत् ॥
1.121.m: O mother, O mother, mother of cows, accept the arghya offering; homage to you!" / Then one should offer fried cakes prepared with black gram and other ingredients,

1.121.s:
evaṃ pañca daśaikaṃ vā yathāvibhavamātmanaḥ /
surabhi tvaṃ jaganmātā nityaṃ viṣṇupade sthitā //
1.121.d:
एवं पञ्च दशैकं वा यथाविभवमात्मनः ।
सुरभि त्वं जगन्माता नित्यं विष्णुपदे स्थिता ॥
1.121.m: five, ten, or one, according to one's own means, [saying:] / "O Surabhi, you are the mother of the universe, eternally abiding in the abode of Viṣṇu!

1.121.s:
sarvadevamaye grāsaṃ mayā dattamimaṃ grasa /
sarvadevamaye devi sarvadevairalaṅkṛte //
1.121.d:
सर्वदेवमये ग्रासं मया दत्तमिमं ग्रस ।
सर्वदेवमये देवि सर्वदेवैरलङ्कृते ॥
1.121.m: O you who comprise all gods, swallow this morsel given by me! / O goddess comprising all gods, adorned with all gods!"

1.121.s:
mātarmamābhilaṣitaṃ saphalaṃ kuru nandinī /
taddine tailapakvaṃ ca sthālīpakvaṃ dvijottama //
1.121.d:
मातर्ममाभिलषितं सफलं कुरु नन्दिनी ।
तद्दिने तैलपक्वं च स्थालीपक्वं द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.121.m:
"O Mother, bringer of joy, fulfill my desire!"
On that day, O best of the twice-born, [food] fried in oil and cooked in a pot,

1.121.s:
gokṣīraṃ goghṛtaṃ caiva dadhi takraṃ ca varjayet /
dvādaśyāmūrjaśuklāyāṃ devaṃ dāmodaraṃ dvija //
1.121.d:
गोक्षीरं गोघृतं चैव दधि तक्रं च वर्जयेत् ।
द्वादश्यामूर्जशुक्लायां देवं दामोदरं द्विज ॥
1.121.m:
Cow's milk, cow's ghee, curds, and buttermilk are to be avoided.
On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Ūrja, O twice-born,

1.121.s:
samabhyarcyopacāraistu gandhādyaiḥ susamāhitaḥ /
tadagre bhojayedviprānpakvānnenārkasaṃkhyakān //
1.121.d:
समभ्यर्च्योपचारैस्तु गन्धाद्यैः सुसमाहितः ।
तदग्रे भोजयेद्विप्रान्पक्वान्नेनार्कसंख्यकान् ॥
1.121.m:
Having worshipped the god Dāmodara with services, beginning with perfumes, highly concentrated,
One should feed twelve brāhmaṇas in front of him with cooked food.

1.121.s:
tataḥ kuṃbhānapāṃpūrṇānvastrācchannānsamarcitān /
sapūgamodakasvarṇāṃstebhyaḥ prītyā samarpayet //
1.121.d:
ततः कुंभानपांपूर्णान्वस्त्राच्छन्नान्समर्चितान् ।
सपूगमोदकस्वर्णांस्तेभ्यः प्रीत्या समर्पयेत् ॥
1.121.m:
Then, jars filled with water, covered with garments, and worshipped,
Together with betel-nuts, sweetmeats, and gold, he should lovingly offer to them.

1.121.s:
evaṃ kṛte priyo viṣṇorjāyate 'khilabhogabhuk /
dehānte viṣṇusāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.121.d:
एवं कृते प्रियो विष्णोर्जायते ऽखिलभोगभुक् ।
देहान्ते विष्णुसायुज्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.121.m:
When this is done, he becomes dear to Viṣṇu, enjoys all pleasures,
And at the end of his body attains union with Viṣṇu; there is no doubt about this.

1.121.s:
nīrājanavrataṃ cātra gaditaṃ tannibodha me /
suptotthitaṃ jagannāthamalaṅkṛtya niśāgame //
1.121.d:
नीराजनव्रतं चात्र गदितं तन्निबोध मे ।
सुप्तोत्थितं जगन्नाथमलङ्कृत्य निशागमे ॥
1.121.m:
The rite of waving lights (nīrājana) is also declared here; learn it from me.
At the arrival of night, having adorned the Lord of the World who has awakened from sleep,

1.121.s:
alaṅkṛto navaṃ vahnimutpādyābhyarcya mantrataḥ /
hutvā tatra samuddīpte raupya dīpikayā mune //
1.121.d:
अलङ्कृतो नवं वह्निमुत्पाद्याभ्यर्च्य मन्त्रतः ।
हुत्वा तत्र समुद्दीप्ते रौप्य दीपिकया मुने ॥
1.121.m:
He himself adorned, producing fresh fire, worshipping it with mantras,
And having made fire oblations there when it is brightly kindled, O sage, with a silver lamp,

1.121.s:
gandhapuṣpādyarcitayā janairnīrājayeddharim /
tatraivānugatāṃ lakṣmīṃ brahmāṇīṃ caṇḍikāṃ tathā //
1.121.d:
गन्धपुष्पाद्यर्चितया जनैर्नीराजयेद्धरिम् ।
तत्रैवानुगतां लक्ष्मीं ब्रह्माणीं चण्डिकां तथा ॥
1.121.m:
Worshipped with perfume, flowers, and the like, people should wave lights before Hari,
And in the very same place, to Lakṣmī who attends him, as well as to Brahmāṇī and Caṇḍikā,

1.121.s:
ādityaṃ śaṅkaraṃ gaurīṃ yakṣaṃ gaṇapatiṃ grahān /
mātṝḥ pitṝnnagānnāgānsarvānnīrājayetkramāt //
1.121.d:
आदित्यं शङ्करं गौरीं यक्षं गणपतिं ग्रहान् ।
मातॄः पितॄन्नगान्नागान्सर्वान्नीराजयेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.121.m:
To the Sun, Śaṅkara, Gaurī, the yakṣa, Gaṇapati, the planets,
The mothers, the ancestors, the mountains, and the serpents—he should wave lights before them all in order.

1.121.s:
gavāṃ nīrājanaṃ kuryānmahiṣyādeśca maṇḍalam /
namo jayeti śabdaiśca ghaṇṭāśaṅkhā diniḥsvanaiḥ //
1.121.d:
गवां नीराजनं कुर्यान्महिष्यादेश्च मण्डलम् ।
नमो जयेति शब्दैश्च घण्टाशङ्खा दिनिःस्वनैः ॥
1.121.m:
He should perform the waving of lights for cows, and for the herd of buffaloes and the like,
With the shouts of 'Salutations!' and 'Victory!', and with the sounds of bells, conches, and other instruments.

1.121.s:
siṃdūrāliptaśṛṅgāṇāṃ citrāṅgāṇāṃ ca varṇakaiḥ /
gavāṃ kolāhale vṛtte nīrājanamahotsave //
1.121.d:
सिंदूरालिप्तशृङ्गाणां चित्राङ्गाणां च वर्णकैः ।
गवां कोलाहले वृत्ते नीराजनमहोत्सवे ॥
1.121.m:
Their horns smeared with vermilion and their bodies painted with diverse colors,
While the tumult of the cows goes on during the great festival of waving lights,

1.121.s:
turagāṃllakṣaṇopetām gajāṃśca madaviplutān /
rājacihnāni sarvāṇi cchatrādīni ca nārada //
1.121.d:
तुरगांल्लक्षणोपेताम् गजांश्च मदविप्लुतान् ।
राजचिह्नानि सर्वाणि च्छत्रादीनि च नारद ॥
1.121.m:
To horses endowed with auspicious marks and to elephants dripping with rut,
To all the royal emblems, umbrellas, and the rest, O Nārada,

1.121.s:
rājā purodhasā sārdhaṃ mantribhṛtyaparaḥ saraḥ /
pūjayitvā yathānyāyaṃ nīrajya svayamādarāt //
1.121.d:
राजा पुरोधसा सार्धं मन्त्रिभृत्यपरः सरः ।
पूजयित्वा यथान्यायं नीरज्य स्वयमादरात् ॥
1.121.m:
The king, together with his royal priest, preceded by his ministers and attendants,
Having duly worshipped and himself waved lights with reverence,

1.121.s:
śaṅkhatūryādighoṣaiśca nānāratnavinirmite /
siṃhāsane nave kḷpte tiṣṭhetsamyagalaṅkṛtaḥ //
1.121.d:
शङ्खतूर्यादिघोषैश्च नानारत्नविनिर्मिते ।
सिंहासने नवे कॢप्ते तिष्ठेत्सम्यगलङ्कृतः ॥
1.121.m:
Amidst the sounds of conches, horns, and other instruments, should sit well adorned
Upon a newly fashioned throne made of various jewels.

1.121.s:
tataḥ sulakṣaṇairyuktā veśyā vātha kulāṅganā /
śīrṣopari naredrasya tayā nīrājayecchanaiḥ //
1.121.d:
ततः सुलक्षणैर्युक्ता वेश्या वाथ कुलाङ्गना ।
शीर्षोपरि नरेद्रस्य तया नीराजयेच्छनैः ॥
1.121.m:
Then, endowed with auspicious marks, either a courtesan or a woman of noble family,
Through her, one should slowly wave lights over the head of the king.

1.121.s:
evameṣā mahāsāṃtiḥ kartavyā prativatsaram /
rājñā vittavatānyena varṣamārogyamicchatā //
1.121.d:
एवमेषा महासांतिः कर्तव्या प्रतिवत्सरम् ।
राज्ञा वित्तवतान्येन वर्षमारोग्यमिच्छता ॥
1.121.m:
In this way, this great pacification rite should be performed every year
By a king or by another wealthy person desiring good health for a year.

1.121.s:
yeṣāṃ rāṣṭre pure grāme kriyate śāntiruttamā /
nīrājanābhidhā vipra tadrogā yānti saṃkṣayam //
1.121.d:
येषां राष्ट्रे पुरे ग्रामे क्रियते शान्तिरुत्तमा ।
नीराजनाभिधा विप्र तद्रोगा यान्ति संक्षयम् ॥
1.121.m:
In whose realm, city, or village this excellent pacification rite
Named nīrājana is performed, O twice-born, their diseases come to an end.

1.121.s:
dvādaśyāṃ mārgaśuklāyāṃ sādhyavratamanuttamam /
manobhavastathā prāṇo naro yātaśca vīryavān //
1.121.d:
द्वादश्यां मार्गशुक्लायां साध्यव्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
मनोभवस्तथा प्राणो नरो यातश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
1.121.m:
On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, there is the unsurpassed rite of the Sādhyas.
Manobhava, Prāṇa, Nara, Yāta, the powerful [Vīryavān],

1.121.s:
citirhayo nṛpaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā /
vibhuścāpi prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ //
1.121.d:
चितिर्हयो नृपश्चैव हंसो नारायणस्तथा ।
विभुश्चापि प्रभुश्चैव साध्या द्वादश कीर्तिताः ॥
1.121.m:
Citi, Haya, Nṛpa, Haṃsa, Nārāyaṇa,
Vibhu, and Prabhu—these are celebrated as the twelve Sādhyas.

1.121.s:
pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyairetāṃstandulakalpitān /
tato dvijāgryānsaṃbhojya dvādaśātra sudakṣiṇāḥ //
1.121.d:
पूजयेद्गन्धपुष्पाद्यैरेतांस्तन्दुलकल्पितान् ।
ततो द्विजाग्र्यान्संभोज्य द्वादशात्र सुदक्षिणाः ॥
1.121.m:
He should worship them, fashioned out of raw rice, with perfumes, flowers, and the rest;
Then, having fed the foremost twice-born, twelve in number here, and generous priestly gifts

1.121.s:
datvā tebhyastu visṛjetprīyānnārayaṇastviti /
etasyāmeva viditaṃ dvādaśādityasaṃjñitam //
1.121.d:
दत्वा तेभ्यस्तु विसृजेत्प्रीयान्नारयणस्त्विति ।
एतस्यामेव विदितं द्वादशादित्यसंज्ञितम् ॥
1.121.m:
Having given to them, he should dismiss them with the thought: 'May Nārāyaṇa be pleased.'
On this very [day], the vow known as the Twelve Ādityas is prescribed.

1.121.s:
vrataṃ tatrārcayeddhīmānādityāndvādaśāpi ca /
dhātāmitror'yamā pūṣā śakroṃ'śo varuṇo bhagaḥ //
1.121.d:
व्रतं तत्रार्चयेद्धीमानादित्यान्द्वादशापि च ।
धातामित्रोर्ऽयमा पूषा शक्रोंऽशो वरुणो भगः ॥
1.121.m:
In that rite, the wise man should worship all the twelve Ādityas:
Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aryaman, Pūṣan, Śakra, Aṃśa, Varuṇa, Bhaga,

1.121.s:
tvaṣṭā vivasvānsavitā viṣṇurdvādaśa īritāḥ /
pratimāsaṃ tu śuklāyāṃ dvādaśyāmarcya yatnataḥ //
1.121.d:
त्वष्टा विवस्वान्सविता विष्णुर्द्वादश ईरिताः ।
प्रतिमासं तु शुक्लायां द्वादश्यामर्च्य यत्नतः ॥
1.121.m:
Tvaṣṭṛ, Vivasvat, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu are declared as the twelve.
Worshipping them diligently on the bright twelfth day each month,

1.121.s:
varṣaṃ nayedvratānte tu pratimā dvādaśāpi ca /
haimīḥ saṃpūjya vidhinā bhojayitvā dvijottamān //
1.121.d:
वर्षं नयेद्व्रतान्ते तु प्रतिमा द्वादशापि च ।
हैमीः संपूज्य विधिना भोजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.121.m:
He should spend a year. At the conclusion of the vow, having worshipped according to rule
Twelve golden images, and having fed the best of the twice-born,

1.121.s:
madhurānnaiḥ susatkṛtya pratyekaṃ cārpayedvratī /
eva vrataṃ naraḥ kṛtvā dvādaśādityasaṃjñakam //
1.121.d:
मधुरान्नैः सुसत्कृत्य प्रत्येकं चार्पयेद्व्रती ।
एव व्रतं नरः कृत्वा द्वादशादित्यसंज्ञकम् ॥
1.121.m:
Having honored them well with sweet dishes, the observer of the vow should offer [an image] to each one.
Having performed this vow named the Twelve Ādityas, a man

1.121.s:
sūryalokaṃ samāsādya bhuktvā bhogāṃścaraṃ tataḥ /
jāyate bhuvi dharmātmā mānuṣye rogavarjitaḥ //
1.121.d:
सूर्यलोकं समासाद्य भुक्त्वा भोगांश्चरं ततः ।
जायते भुवि धर्मात्मा मानुष्ये रोगवर्जितः ॥
1.121.m:
Reaches the world of the Sun and enjoys pleasures for a long time; then
He is born on earth as a righteous person in a human form, free from disease.

1.121.s:
tato vratasya puṇyena punareva labhedvratam /
tatpuṇyena ravenbhitvā maṇḍalaṃ dvijasattama //
1.121.d:
ततो व्रतस्य पुण्येन पुनरेव लभेद्व्रतम् ।
तत्पुण्येन रवेन्भित्वा मण्डलं द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.121.m:
Then, through the merit of the vow, he attains the vow once again;
By its merit, having pierced the orb of the sun, O best of the twice-born,

1.121.s:
nirañjanaṃ nirā kāraṃ nirdvandvaṃ brahma cāpnuyāt /
atraivākhaṇḍasaṃjñaṃ ca vratamukta dvijottama //
1.121.d:
निरञ्जनं निरा कारं निर्द्वन्द्वं ब्रह्म चाप्नुयात् ।
अत्रैवाखण्डसंज्ञं च व्रतमुक्त द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.121.m:
He attains Brahman, stainless, formless, and free from dualities.
Right here, the vow named Akhaṇḍa is declared, O best of the twice-born.

1.121.s:
mūrtiṃ nirmāya sauvarṇīṃ janārdanasamāhvayām /
abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyaistadagre bhojayeddvijān //
1.121.d:
मूर्तिं निर्माय सौवर्णीं जनार्दनसमाह्वयाम् ।
अभ्यर्च्य गन्धपुष्पाद्यैस्तदग्रे भोजयेद्द्विजान् ॥
1.121.m:
Having fashioned a golden image named Janārdana,
And having worshipped it with perfume, flowers, and the rest, he should feed brāhmaṇas before it.

1.121.s:
dvādaśa pratimāsaṃ tu naktāśīḥ syājjitendriyaḥ /
tataḥ samānte tāṃ mūrtiṃ samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ //
1.121.d:
द्वादश प्रतिमासं तु नक्ताशीः स्याज्जितेन्द्रियः ।
ततः समान्ते तां मूर्तिं समभ्यर्च्य विधानतः ॥
1.121.m:
Twelve [in number] each month, he should eat only at night, with controlled senses.
Then, at the end of the year, having worshipped that image according to rule,

1.121.s:
gurave dhenusahitāṃ dadyātsaṃprārthayettathā /
śatajanmasu yatkiñcinmayākhaṇḍavrataṃ kṛtam //
1.121.d:
गुरवे धेनुसहितां दद्यात्संप्रार्थयेत्तथा ।
शतजन्मसु यत्किञ्चिन्मयाखण्डव्रतं कृतम् ॥
1.121.m:
He should give it to the guru together with a cow, and he should pray thus:
'Whatever unbroken vow (akhaṇḍavrata) has been performed by me across a hundred births,

1.121.s:
bhagavaṃstvatprasādena tadakhaṇḍamihāstu me /
tataḥ saṃbhojya viprāgryānsakhaṇḍāḍhyaistu pāyasaiḥ //
1.121.d:
भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन तदखण्डमिहास्तु मे ।
ततः संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यान्सखण्डाढ्यैस्तु पायसैः ॥
1.121.m:
O Lord, by your grace, let it be whole (akhaṇḍa) for me in this world.'
Then, having fed the foremost brāhmaṇas with milk-rice enriched with sugar candy,

1.121.s:
dvādaśaiva hi sauvarṇīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ pradadennamet /
iti kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra prīṇayitvā janārdanam //
1.121.d:
द्वादशैव हि सौवर्णीं दक्षिणां प्रददेन्नमेत् ।
इति कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र प्रीणयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥
1.121.m:
He should give a gift of gold to the twelve, and bow.
Having performed this vow in this manner, O twice-born, having pleased Janārdana,

1.121.s:
sauvarṇena vimānena yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam /
pauṣasya kṛṣṇadvādaśyāṃ rūpavratamudīritam //
1.121.d:
सौवर्णेन विमानेन याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ।
पौषस्य कृष्णद्वादश्यां रूपव्रतमुदीरितम् ॥
1.121.m:
He goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu by means of a golden celestial chariot.
On the dark twelfth day of Pauṣa, the Rūpavrata is declared.

1.121.s:
daśamyāṃ vidhivatsnātvā gṛhṇīyādgomayaṃ vratī /
śvetāyā vaikavarṇāyā antarikṣagataṃ dvija //
1.121.d:
दशम्यां विधिवत्स्नात्वा गृह्णीयाद्गोमयं व्रती ।
श्वेताया वैकवर्णाया अन्तरिक्षगतं द्विज ॥
1.121.m:
Having bathed according to rule on the tenth day, the observer of the vow should take cow dung
From a white or monochrome cow that has been caught in mid-air, O twice-born.

1.121.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ tena piṇḍikāḥ kalpya nārada /
śoṣayedātape dhṛtvā pātre tāmre 'tha mṛnmaye //
1.121.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं तेन पिण्डिकाः कल्प्य नारद ।
शोषयेदातपे धृत्वा पात्रे ताम्रे ऽथ मृन्मये ॥
1.121.m:
Having fashioned one hundred and eight balls from it, O Nārada,
Placing them in a copper or earthen vessel, he should dry them in the sun.

1.121.s:
ekādaśyāṃ sopavāsaḥ samabhyarcya vidhānataḥ /
sauvarṇīṃ pratimāṃ viṣṇorniśāyāṃ jāgaraṃ caret //
1.121.d:
एकादश्यां सोपवासः समभ्यर्च्य विधानतः ।
सौवर्णीं प्रतिमां विष्णोर्निशायां जागरं चरेत् ॥
1.121.m:
Fasting on the eleventh day, having worshipped according to rule
A golden image of Viṣṇu, he should observe a vigil at night,

1.121.s:
sumaṅgalairgītavādyaiḥ stotrapāṭhairjapādibhiḥ /
tataḥ prabhāte dvādaśyāṃ tilapātropari sthitām //
1.121.d:
सुमङ्गलैर्गीतवाद्यैः स्तोत्रपाठैर्जपादिभिः ।
ततः प्रभाते द्वादश्यां तिलपात्रोपरि स्थिताम् ॥
1.121.m:
With auspicious songs and instruments, recitation of hymns, japa, and the like.
Then, at dawn on the twelfth day, [placing] it on a vessel of sesame,

1.121.s:
aṃbupūrṇe ghaṭe nyasya pūjayedupacārakaiḥ /
tato 'gniṃ navamutpādya kāṣṭhasaṃgharṣaṇādibhiḥ //
1.121.d:
अंबुपूर्णे घटे न्यस्य पूजयेदुपचारकैः ।
ततो ऽग्निं नवमुत्पाद्य काष्ठसंघर्षणादिभिः ॥
1.121.m:
Setting it upon a water-filled pot, he should worship it with offerings of service.
Then, producing fresh fire by rubbing pieces of wood and the like,

1.121.s:
taṃ samabhyarcya vidhivadekaikāṃ piṇḍikāṃ sudhīḥ /
homayetsatilājyāṃ ca dvādaśākṣaravidyayā //
1.121.d:
तं समभ्यर्च्य विधिवदेकैकां पिण्डिकां सुधीः ।
होमयेत्सतिलाज्यां च द्वादशाक्षरविद्यया ॥
1.121.m:
Having worshipped it according to rule, the wise man should offer each ball into the fire,
Together with sesame and ghee, with the twelve-syllable mantra,

1.121.s:
vaiṣṇavyātha ca pūraṇāṃ ca śatamaṣṭottara tataḥ /
bhojayetpāyasairviprānprītyā susnigdhamānasaḥ //
1.121.d:
वैष्णव्याथ च पूरणां च शतमष्टोत्तर ततः ।
भोजयेत्पायसैर्विप्रान्प्रीत्या सुस्निग्धमानसः ॥
1.121.m:
Or with the Vaiṣṇava [mantra], performing the full offering one hundred and eight times. Then,
With a tender and loving mind, he should lovingly feed brāhmaṇas with milk-rice.

1.121.s:
sahitāṃ ca ghaṭenaiva pratimāṃ gurava'peyet /
viprebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā datvā natvā visarjayet /
naro vā yadi vā nārī vrataṃ kṛtvaivamādarāt //
1.121.d:
सहितां च घटेनैव प्रतिमां गुरवऽपेयेत् ।
विप्रेभ्यो दक्षिणां शक्त्या दत्वा नत्वा विसर्जयेत् ।
नरो वा यदि वा नारी व्रतं कृत्वैवमादरात् ॥
1.121.m:
He should offer the image together with the pot to the guru.
Having given priestly gifts according to his means to the brāhmaṇas and bowed, he should dismiss them.
Whether a man or a woman, having performed the vow in this manner with reverence,

1.121.s:
labhate rūpasaubhāgyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
sahasye śuklapakṣe tu sujanmadvādaśīvratam //
1.121.d:
लभते रूपसौभाग्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
सहस्ये शुक्लपक्षे तु सुजन्मद्वादशीव्रतम् ॥
1.121.m:
Attains beauty and good fortune; no doubt should be entertained on this point.
In the bright fortnight of Sahasya (Pauṣa), however, is the Sujanmadvādaśī vow.

1.121.s:
snātvā vidhānena gṛhṇoyādvārṣikavratam /
pītvā gaśṛṅgavāryādau tāṃ ca kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam //
1.121.d:
स्नात्वा विधानेन गृह्णोयाद्वार्षिकव्रतम् ।
पीत्वा गशृङ्गवार्यादौ तां च कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
1.121.m:
Having bathed according to rule, one should undertake the year-long vow.
Having first drunk water from the cow's horns and having circumambulated her,

1.121.s:
pratimāsaṃ tataḥ śukledvādaśyāṃ dānamācaret /
ghṛtaprasthaṃ taccatuṣkaṃ kramādvīheryavasya ca //
1.121.d:
प्रतिमासं ततः शुक्लेद्वादश्यां दानमाचरेत् ।
घृतप्रस्थं तच्चतुष्कं क्रमाद्वीहेर्यवस्य च ॥
1.121.m:
He should then make gifts on the bright twelfth day each month:
A prastha of ghee, four of that in succession of rice and of barley,

1.121.s:
dviraktikaṃ hema tilāḍhakārddhaṃ payasāṃ ghaṭam /
raupyasya māṣamekaṃ ca tṛptikṛnmiṣṭapakvakam //
1.121.d:
द्विरक्तिकं हेम तिलाढकार्द्धं पयसां घटम् ।
रौप्यस्य माषमेकं च तृप्तिकृन्मिष्टपक्वकम् ॥
1.121.m:
Two raktikās of gold, half an āḍhaka of sesame, a pot of milk,
A māṣa of silver, satisfying sweet cooked food,

1.121.s:
chatraṃ māṣārdhahemnaśca prasthaṃ phaāṇitamuttamam /
candanaṃ palikaṃ vastraṃ pañcahastonmitaṃ tanum //
1.121.d:
छत्रं माषार्धहेम्नश्च प्रस्थं फआणितमुत्तमम् ।
चन्दनं पलिकं वस्त्रं पञ्चहस्तोन्मितं तनुम् ॥
1.121.m:
An umbrella, half a māṣa of gold, an excellent prastha of boiled sugarcane juice,
A pala of sandalwood, and fine cloth measuring five cubits.

1.121.s:
evaṃ tu māsikaṃ dānaṃ kṛtvā prāśya yathākramam /
gomūtraṃ jalamājyaṃ vā paktvā śākaṃ caturvidham //
1.121.d:
एवं तु मासिकं दानं कृत्वा प्राश्य यथाक्रमम् ।
गोमूत्रं जलमाज्यं वा पक्त्वा शाकं चतुर्विधम् ॥
1.121.m: Having made this monthly gift in this manner, and having consumed in order / cow urine, water, or ghee, and having cooked the fourfold greens,

1.121.s:
dadhiyuktaṃ ca yāvānnaṃ tilājyaṃ śarkarānvitām /
darbhāṃbukṣīramuditaṃ prāśanaṃ pratimāsikam //
1.121.d:
दधियुक्तं च यावान्नं तिलाज्यं शर्करान्विताम् ।
दर्भांबुक्षीरमुदितं प्राशनं प्रतिमासिकम् ॥
1.121.m: and barley gruel mixed with curd, sesame seeds with ghee, and sugar, / the consumption of kuśa grass water and milk is prescribed month by month.

1.121.s:
evaṃ kṛtavrato varṣaṃ sauvarṇīṃ pratimāṃ raveḥ /
kṛtvā vai tāmrapātrasthāṃ nyasyābhyarcya vidhānataḥ //
1.121.d:
एवं कृतव्रतो वर्षं सौवर्णीं प्रतिमां रवेः ।
कृत्वा वै ताम्रपात्रस्थां न्यस्याभ्यर्च्य विधानतः ॥
1.121.m: One who has observed the vow for a year in this manner, having fashioned a golden image of the Sun, / placed it in a copper vessel, and worshipped it according to rule,

1.121.s:
gurave dhenusahitāṃ pratyarpya praṇametpuraḥ /
viprāndrādaśa saṃbhojya tebhyo dadyācca dakṣiṇām //
1.121.d:
गुरवे धेनुसहितां प्रत्यर्प्य प्रणमेत्पुरः ।
विप्रान्द्रादश संभोज्य तेभ्यो दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.121.m: having offered it to the guru together with a cow, should bow before him. / Having fed twelve brāhmaṇas, he should give them a dakṣiṇā.

1.121.s:
evaṃ kṛtavrato vipra janmāpnotyuttame kule /
nirogo dhanadhānyāḍhyo bhaveccāvikaledriyaḥ //
1.121.d:
एवं कृतव्रतो विप्र जन्माप्नोत्युत्तमे कुले ।
निरोगो धनधान्याढ्यो भवेच्चाविकलेद्रियः ॥
1.121.m: O brāhmaṇa, one who has observed the vow in this manner takes birth in an excellent family; / he becomes free from disease, rich in wealth and grain, and with his senses unimpaired.

1.121.s:
māghasya śukladvādaśyāṃ śālagrāmaśilāṃ dvija /
abhyacya vidhivadbhaktyā suvarṇaṃ tanmukhe nyaset //
1.121.d:
माघस्य शुक्लद्वादश्यां शालग्रामशिलां द्विज ।
अभ्यच्य विधिवद्भक्त्या सुवर्णं तन्मुखे न्यसेत् ॥
1.121.m: On the bright twelfth day of Māgha, O twice-born, / having worshipped the Śālagrāma stone properly with devotion, one should place gold on its mouth.

1.121.s:
tāṃ sthāpya raupyapātre tu sitavastrayugāvṛtām /
pradadyādvedaviduṣe taṃ hi saṃbhojayettataḥ //
1.121.d:
तां स्थाप्य रौप्यपात्रे तु सितवस्त्रयुगावृताम् ।
प्रदद्याद्वेदविदुषे तं हि संभोजयेत्ततः ॥
1.121.m: Having placed it in a silver vessel and covered it with a pair of white garments, / one should give it to a knower of the Vedas; one should then feed him

1.121.s:
pāyasānnena khaṇḍājyasahitena hitena ca /
evaṃ kṛtvaikabhaktaḥ sanviṣṇu cintanatatparaḥ //
1.121.d:
पायसान्नेन खण्डाज्यसहितेन हितेन च ।
एवं कृत्वैकभक्तः सन्विष्णु चिन्तनतत्परः ॥
1.121.m: with rice-milk pudding accompanied by sugar and ghee, wholesome [and delicious]. / Having acted thus, taking a single meal, intent on meditation upon Viṣṇu,

1.121.s:
vaiṣṇavaṃ labhate dhāma bhuktvā bhogānihepsitān /
antye sitāyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ sauvarṇīṃ pratimāṃ hareḥ //
1.121.d:
वैष्णवं लभते धाम भुक्त्वा भोगानिहेप्सितान् ।
अन्त्ये सितायां द्वादश्यां सौवर्णीं प्रतिमां हरेः ॥
1.121.m: after enjoying the desired pleasures here, he attains the abode of Viṣṇu. / On the final bright twelfth day, [making] a golden image of Hari,

1.121.s:
abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyairdadyādvedavide dvija /
dviṣaṭkasaṃkhyānviprāṃśca bhojayitvā ca dakṣiṇām //
1.121.d:
अभ्यर्च्य गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर्दद्याद्वेदविदे द्विज ।
द्विषट्कसंख्यान्विप्रांश्च भोजयित्वा च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.121.m: having worshipped it with fragrant scents, flowers, and the like, O twice-born, one should give it to a knower of the Vedas. / And having fed brāhmaṇas numbering twelve, and given dakṣiṇā,

1.121.s:
datvā visarjayetpaścātsvayaṃ bhuñjīta bāndhavaiḥ /
trispṛśonmīlinī pakṣavarddhinī vañjulī tathā //
1.121.d:
दत्वा विसर्जयेत्पश्चात्स्वयं भुञ्जीत बान्धवैः ।
त्रिस्पृशोन्मीलिनी पक्षवर्द्धिनी वञ्जुली तथा ॥
1.121.m: and dismissed them thereafter, one should eat oneself with relatives. / Trispṛśā, Unmīlinī, Pakṣavarddhinī, and Vañjulī,

1.121.s:
jayā ca vijayā caiva jayantī cāparājitā /
etā aṣṭau sadopoṣyā dvādaśyaḥ pāpahārikāḥ //
1.121.d:
जया च विजया चैव जयन्ती चापराजिता ।
एता अष्टौ सदोपोष्या द्वादश्यः पापहारिकाः ॥
1.121.m: and Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Aparājitā— / on these eight twelfth lunar days, which remove sins, one should always fast.

1.121.s:
śrīnārada uvāca
kīdṛśaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brahmannetāsāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ tathā /
tatsarvaṃ me samācakṣva yāścanyāḥ puṇyadāyukāḥ //
1.121.d:
श्रीनारद उवाच
कीदृशं लक्षणं ब्रह्मन्नेतासां किं फलं तथा ।
तत्सर्वं मे समाचक्ष्व याश्चन्याः पुण्यदायुकाः ॥
1.121.m: Śrī Nārada said: / What is the characteristic of these, O holy one? What is their fruit? / Tell me all that, and whatever others bestow merit.

1.121.s:
sūta uvāca
itthaṃ sanātanaḥ pṛṣṭo nāradena dvijottamaḥ /
praśasya bhrātaraṃ prāha mahābhāgavataṃ muniḥ //
1.121.d:
सूत उवाच
इत्थं सनातनः पृष्टो नारदेन द्विजोत्तमः ।
प्रशस्य भ्रातरं प्राह महाभागवतं मुनिः ॥
1.121.m: Sūta said: / Questioned thus by Nārada, the sage Sanātana, best of the twice-born, / praised his brother, the great devotee of the Lord, and said:

1.121.s:
sanātana uvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā bhrātaḥ sādhūnāṃ saṃśayacchidā /
vakṣye mahādvādaśīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca phalaṃ pṛthak //
1.121.d:
सनातन उवाच
साधु पृष्टं त्वया भ्रातः साधूनां संशयच्छिदा ।
वक्ष्ये महाद्वादशीनां लक्षणं च फलं पृथक् ॥
1.121.m: Sanātana said: / Well asked by you, brother, who cuts away the doubts of the virtuous! / I shall declare the characteristic and separate fruit of the great twelfth lunar days.

1.121.s:
ekādaśī nivṛttā cetsūryasyodayataḥ purā /
tadā tu trispṛśā nāma dvādaśī sā mahāphalā //
1.121.d:
एकादशी निवृत्ता चेत्सूर्यस्योदयतः पुरा ।
तदा तु त्रिस्पृशा नाम द्वादशी सा महाफला ॥
1.121.m: If the eleventh lunar day terminates before sunrise, / then that twelfth lunar day is named Trispṛśā, and bears great fruit.

1.121.s:
asyāmupoṣya govindaṃ yaḥ pūjayati nārada /
aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ labhate dhruvam //
1.121.d:
अस्यामुपोष्य गोविन्दं यः पूजयति नारद ।
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं लभते ध्रुवम् ॥
1.121.m: Fasting on this and worshipping Govinda, O Nārada, / one surely attains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.

1.121.s:
yadāruṇodaye viddhā daśamyaikādaśī tithiḥ /
tadā tāṃ saṃparityajya dvādaśīṃ samupoṣayet //
1.121.d:
यदारुणोदये विद्धा दशम्यैकादशी तिथिः ।
तदा तां संपरित्यज्य द्वादशीं समुपोषयेत् ॥
1.121.m: When the eleventh lunar day is penetrated by the tenth at dawn, / then, abandoning it, one should fast on the twelfth.

1.121.s:
tatreṣṭvā vāsudevākhyaṃ samyakpūjāvidhānataḥ /
rājasūyasahasrasya phalamunmīlite labhet //
1.121.d:
तत्रेष्ट्वा वासुदेवाख्यं सम्यक्पूजाविधानतः ।
राजसूयसहस्रस्य फलमुन्मीलिते लभेत् ॥
1.121.m: Having worshipped the one named Vāsudeva there according to the proper ritual of worship, / one attains the fruit of a thousand Rājasūya sacrifices on the Unmīlitā.

1.121.s:
yadodaye tu savituryāmyā tvekādaśīṃ spṛśet /
tadā vañjulikākhyāṃ tu tāṃ tyaktvopoṣayetsadā //
1.121.d:
यदोदये तु सवितुर्याम्या त्वेकादशीं स्पृशेत् ।
तदा वञ्जुलिकाख्यां तु तां त्यक्त्वोपोषयेत्सदा ॥
1.121.m: When at sunrise the Yamī [Dvādaśī] touches the eleventh lunar day, / then, leaving it aside, one should always fast on the one named Vañjulikā.

1.121.s:
asyāṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ devaṃ gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ /
pūjayetsatataṃ bhaktyā sarvasyābhayadaṃ param //
1.121.d:
अस्यां संकर्षणं देवं गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ।
पूजयेत्सततं भक्त्या सर्वस्याभयदं परम् ॥
1.121.m: On this day one should constantly worship with devotion the god Saṃkarṣaṇa, the supreme granter of fearlessness to all, / with offerings such as fragrant pastes.

1.121.s:
eṣā mahādvādaśī tu sarvakratuphalapradā /
sarvapāpaharā proktā sarvasaṃpatpradāyinī //
1.121.d:
एषा महाद्वादशी तु सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदा ।
सर्वपापहरा प्रोक्ता सर्वसंपत्प्रदायिनी ॥
1.121.m: This great twelfth day grants the fruit of all sacrifices; / it is declared to remove all sins and bestow all prosperity.

1.121.s:
kuhūrāke yadā vṛddhe syātāṃ vipra yadā tadā /
pakṣavarddhanikā nāma dvādaśī sā mahāphalā //
1.121.d:
कुहूराके यदा वृद्धे स्यातां विप्र यदा तदा ।
पक्षवर्द्धनिका नाम द्वादशी सा महाफला ॥
1.121.m: When, O brāhmaṇa, the new-moon day or the full-moon day expands, / that twelfth day of great fruit is named Pakṣavarddhanikā.

1.121.s:
tasyāṃ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ pradyumnaṃ jagatāṃ patim /
sarvaiśvaryyapradaṃ sākṣātputra pautravivardhanam //
1.121.d:
तस्यां संपूजयेद्देवं प्रद्युम्नं जगतां पतिम् ।
सर्वैश्वर्य्यप्रदं साक्षात्पुत्र पौत्रविवर्धनम् ॥
1.121.m: On that day one should thoroughly worship the god Pradyumna, the lord of the worlds, / who directly bestows all sovereignty and increases sons and grandsons.

1.121.s:
yadā tu dhavale pakṣe dvādaśī syānmadhānvitā //ṭha
tadā proktā jayā nāma sarvaśatruvināśinī //
1.121.d:
यदा तु धवले पक्षे द्वादशी स्यान्मधान्विता ॥ठ
तदा प्रोक्ता जया नाम सर्वशत्रुविनाशिनी ॥
1.121.m: When in the bright fortnight the twelfth day is conjoined with Maghā, / then it is declared to be Jayā, which destroys all enemies.

1.121.s:
asyāṃ saṃpūjayeddeva maniruddhaṃ ramāpatim /
sarvakāmapradaṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvasaubhāgyadāyakam //
1.121.d:
अस्यां संपूजयेद्देव मनिरुद्धं रमापतिम् ।
सर्वकामप्रदं नॄणां सर्वसौभाग्यदायकम् ॥
1.121.m: On this day one should worship the god Aniruddha, the husband of Ramā, / who grants all desires to mortals and bestows all good fortune.

1.121.s:
śravaṇarkṣayutā cetsyāddvādaśī dhavale dale /
tadā sā vijayā nāma tasyāmacedgadādharam //
1.121.d:
श्रवणर्क्षयुता चेत्स्याद्द्वादशी धवले दले ।
तदा सा विजया नाम तस्यामचेद्गदाधरम् ॥
1.121.m: If the twelfth day in the bright half is joined with the asterism Śravaṇa, / then it is Vijayā by name; on it one should worship the Mace-Bearer.

1.121.s:
sarvasaukhyapradaṃ śaśvatsarvabhogaparāyaṇam /
sarvatīrthaphalaṃ vipra tāṃ copoṣyāpnuyānnaraḥ //
1.121.d:
सर्वसौख्यप्रदं शश्वत्सर्वभोगपरायणम् ।
सर्वतीर्थफलं विप्र तां चोपोष्याप्नुयान्नरः ॥
1.121.m: He continually grants all happiness and is the goal of all enjoyment. / Fasting on it, O brāhmaṇa, a man obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.

1.121.s:
yadā syācca site pakṣe prājāpatyarkṣasaṃyutā /
dvādaśī sā mahāpuṇyā jayantī nāmataḥ smṛtā //
1.121.d:
यदा स्याच्च सिते पक्षे प्राजापत्यर्क्षसंयुता ।
द्वादशी सा महापुण्या जयन्ती नामतः स्मृता ॥
1.121.m: When in the bright fortnight the twelfth day is conjoined with the asterism Rohiṇī, / that highly meritorious twelfth day is known by the name Jayantī.

1.121.s:
yasyāṃ samarccayeddevaṃ vāmanaṃ siddhidaṃ nṛṇām /
upoṣitaiṣā viprendra sarvavrataphalapradā //
1.121.d:
यस्यां समर्च्चयेद्देवं वामनं सिद्धिदं नृणाम् ।
उपोषितैषा विप्रेन्द्र सर्वव्रतफलप्रदा ॥
1.121.m: On it one should worship the god Vāmana, who grants success to mortals. / Fasted upon, O prince of brāhmaṇas, this bestows the fruit of all vows,

1.121.s:
sarvadānaphalā cāpi bhuktimuktipradāyinī /
yadā tu syātsite pakṣe dvādaśī jīvabhānvitā //
1.121.d:
सर्वदानफला चापि भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनी ।
यदा तु स्यात्सिते पक्षे द्वादशी जीवभान्विता ॥
1.121.m: gives the fruit of all gifts, and grants worldly enjoyment and liberation. / But when in the bright fortnight the twelfth day is joined with the asterism Puṣya,

1.121.s:
tadāparājitā proktā sarvajñā napradāyinī /
asyāṃ samarcayeddevaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam //
1.121.d:
तदापराजिता प्रोक्ता सर्वज्ञा नप्रदायिनी ।
अस्यां समर्चयेद्देवं नारायणमनामयम् ॥
1.121.m: then it is declared to be Aparājitā, which bestows omniscience. / On this day one should worship the free-from-affliction god Nārāyaṇa,

1.121.s:
saṃsārapāśavicchittikārakaṃ jñānasāgaram /
asyāstūpoṣaṇādeva muktaḥ syādvipra bhojanaḥ //
1.121.d:
संसारपाशविच्छित्तिकारकं ज्ञानसागरम् ।
अस्यास्तूपोषणादेव मुक्तः स्याद्विप्र भोजनः ॥
1.121.m: the causer of the cutting of worldly bonds, the ocean of knowledge. / Merely by fasting on this, O brāhmaṇa, a mortal becomes liberated.

1.121.s:
yadā tvāṣāḍhaśuklāyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ maitrabhaṃ bhavet /
tadā vratadvayaṃ kāryyaṃ na doṣo 'traikadaivatam //
1.121.d:
यदा त्वाषाढशुक्लायां द्वादश्यां मैत्रभं भवेत् ।
तदा व्रतद्वयं कार्य्यं न दोषो ऽत्रैकदैवतम् ॥
1.121.m: When on the bright twelfth of Āṣāḍha there is the asterism Anurādhā, / then a double vow is to be performed; there is no fault in this, since the deity is one.

1.121.s:
śravaṇarkṣayutāyāṃ ca dvādaśyāṃ bhādraśuklake /
ūrjje sitāyāṃ dvādaśyāmantyabhe ca vratadvayam //
1.121.d:
श्रवणर्क्षयुतायां च द्वादश्यां भाद्रशुक्लके ।
ऊर्ज्जे सितायां द्वादश्यामन्त्यभे च व्रतद्वयम् ॥
1.121.m: And on the twelfth in the bright Bhādrapada conjoined with the asterism Śravaṇa, / and on the bright twelfth of Kārttika with the final asterism, there is a double vow.

1.121.s:
etābhyo 'ntra viprendra dvādaśyāmekabhuktakam /
nisargataḥ samuddiṣṭaṃ vrataṃ pātakanāśanam //
1.121.d:
एताभ्यो ऽन्त्र विप्रेन्द्र द्वादश्यामेकभुक्तकम् ।
निसर्गतः समुद्दिष्टं व्रतं पातकनाशनम् ॥
1.121.m: Apart from these, O prince of brāhmaṇas, eating once on the twelfth day / is naturally prescribed as a vow that destroys fallenness.

1.121.s:
ekādaśyā vrataṃ nityaṃ dvādaśyāḥ sahitaṃ yataḥ /
nodyāpanamihoddiṣṭaṃ karttavyaṃ jīvitāvidhi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe bṛhadupākhyāne pūrvabhāge caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasya dvādaśīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.121.d:
एकादश्या व्रतं नित्यं द्वादश्याः सहितं यतः ।
नोद्यापनमिहोद्दिष्टं कर्त्तव्यं जीविताविधि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे बृहदुपाख्याने पूर्वभागे चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्य द्वादशीव्रतनिरूपणं नामैकविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.121.m:
Since the vow of the eleventh day is regular together with the twelfth, / no concluding rite is prescribed here; it should be performed throughout life.

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-first chapter in the fourth quarter of the first part in the Great Purāṇa of Nārada, in the Great Narrative, entitled 'Determination of the Vow of the Twelfth Day of the Twelve Months.'

1.122.s:
sanātana uvāca
athātaṛ saṃpravakṣyāmi trayodaśyā vratāni te /
yāni kṛtvā naro bhaktyā subhago jāyate bhuvi //
1.122.d:
सनातन उवाच
अथातऋ संप्रवक्ष्यामि त्रयोदश्या व्रतानि ते ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो भक्त्या सुभगो जायते भुवि ॥
1.122.m: Sanātana said: / Now I shall declare to you the vows of the thirteenth day, / performing which with devotion a man becomes fortunate on earth.

1.122.s:
madhau śuklatrayodaśyāṃ madanaṃ candanātmakam /
kṛtvā saṃpūjya yatnena vījeyavdyajanena ca //
1.122.d:
मधौ शुक्लत्रयोदश्यां मदनं चन्दनात्मकम् ।
कृत्वा संपूज्य यत्नेन वीजेयव्द्यजनेन च ॥
1.122.m: In Madhu, on the bright thirteenth day, having made Madana out of sandalwood, / having worshipped him with diligence, and fanned him with a fan,

1.122.s:
tataḥ saṃkṣudhitaḥ kāmaḥ putrapautravivarddhanaḥ /
anaṅgapūjāpyatroktā tāṃ nibodha munīśvara //
1.122.d:
ततः संक्षुधितः कामः पुत्रपौत्रविवर्द्धनः ।
अनङ्गपूजाप्यत्रोक्ता तां निबोध मुनीश्वर ॥
1.122.m: then Kāma, aroused, causes the increase of sons and grandsons. / The worship of the Bodiless One is also declared here; learn that, O lord of sages.

1.122.s:
sindūrarajanīrāgaiḥ phalake 'naṅgamālikhet /
ratiprītiyutaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ puṣpacāpeṣudhāriṇam //
1.122.d:
सिन्दूररजनीरागैः फलके ऽनङ्गमालिखेत् ।
रतिप्रीतियुतं श्लक्ष्णं पुष्पचापेषुधारिणम् ॥
1.122.m: With red-lead and turmeric colors, one should paint the Bodiless One on a board, / smooth, accompanied by Rati and Prīti, holding a bow and arrows of flowers.

1.122.s:
kāmadevaṃ vasantaṃ ca vājivaktraṃ vṛṣadhvajam /
madhyāhne pūjayedbhaktyā gandhasragbhūṣaṇāṃśukaiḥ //
1.122.d:
कामदेवं वसन्तं च वाजिवक्त्रं वृषध्वजम् ।
मध्याह्ने पूजयेद्भक्त्या गन्धस्रग्भूषणांशुकैः ॥
1.122.m: At midday, one should worship Kāmadeva, Spring, the Horse-Faced one, and the Bull-Bannered one with devotion, / with fragrant scents, garlands, ornaments, and garments,

1.122.s:
kṣabhyairnānāvidhaiścāpi mantreṇānena nārada /
namo mārāya kāmāya kāmadevasya mūrttaye //
1.122.d:
क्षभ्यैर्नानाविधैश्चापि मन्त्रेणानेन नारद ।
नमो माराय कामाय कामदेवस्य मूर्त्तये ॥
1.122.m: and with various kinds of foods to be chewed, O Nārada, with this mantra: / 'Homage to Māra, to Kāma, to the embodiment of Kāmadeva,

1.122.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivendrāṇāṃ manaḥbhobhakarāya vai /
tattasyāgrato bhaktyā pūjayedaṅganāpatim //
1.122.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवेन्द्राणां मनःभोभकराय वै ।
तत्तस्याग्रतो भक्त्या पूजयेदङ्गनापतिम् ॥
1.122.m: who truly agitates the minds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and Indra.' / Then in front of him, one should worship with devotion the husband of the woman.

1.122.s:
vastramālyāvibhūṣādyaiḥ kāmo 'yamiti cintayet /
saṃpūjya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ gandhavastravibhūṣaṇaiḥ //
1.122.d:
वस्त्रमाल्याविभूषाद्यैः कामो ऽयमिति चिन्तयेत् ।
संपूज्य द्विजदांपत्यं गन्धवस्त्रविभूषणैः ॥
1.122.m: With garments, garlands, ornaments, and the like, one should think: 'This is Kāma.' / Having worshipped a brāhmaṇa married couple with fragrant scents, garments, and ornaments,

1.122.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute vipra varṣe varṣe mahotsavam /
vasaṃtasamaye prāpte hṛṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ sadaiva saḥ //
1.122.d:
एवं यः कुरुते विप्र वर्षे वर्षे महोत्सवम् ।
वसंतसमये प्राप्ते हृष्टः पुष्टः सदैव सः ॥
1.122.m: The twice-born who performs such a great festival year after year / when springtime arrives is ever delighted and well-nourished.

1.122.s:
pratimāsaṃ pūjayedvā yāvadvarṣaṃ samāpyate /
madanaṃ hṛdbhavaṃ kāmaṃ manmathaṃ ca ratipriyam //
1.122.d:
प्रतिमासं पूजयेद्वा यावद्वर्षं समाप्यते ।
मदनं हृद्भवं कामं मन्मथं च रतिप्रियम् ॥
1.122.m: Or he may worship each month until the year is completed: / Madana, Hṛdbhava, Kāma, Manmatha, and Ratipriya,

1.122.s:
anaṅgaṃ caiva kandarpaṃ pūjayenmakaradhvajam /
kusumāyudhasaṃjñaṃ ca tataḥ paścānmanobhavam //
1.122.d:
अनङ्गं चैव कन्दर्पं पूजयेन्मकरध्वजम् ।
कुसुमायुधसंज्ञं च ततः पश्चान्मनोभवम् ॥
1.122.m: Anaṅga, Kandarpa, Makaradhvaja, / the one named Kusumāyudha, and thereafter Manobhava,

1.122.s:
viṣameṣu tathā vipra mālartāpriyamityapi /
ajāyā dānamapyuktaṃ snātvā nadyā vidhānataḥ //
1.122.d:
विषमेषु तथा विप्र मालर्ताप्रियमित्यपि ।
अजाया दानमप्युक्तं स्नात्वा नद्या विधानतः ॥
1.122.m: likewise, O twice-born, Viṣameṣu and Mālartāpriya. / Having bathed in a river according to the prescribed rule, the gift of a she-goat is also enjoined.

1.122.s:
ajāḥ payasvinīrdadyāddaridrāya kuṭuṃbine /
bhūyastvanena dānena sa loke naiva jāyate //
1.122.d:
अजाः पयस्विनीर्दद्याद्दरिद्राय कुटुंबिने ।
भूयस्त्वनेन दानेन स लोके नैव जायते ॥
1.122.m: He should give milch she-goats to an impoverished householder; / by this gift, indeed, he is never born again in this world.

1.122.s:
yadīyaṃ śaninā yuktā sā mahāvāruṇī smṛtā /
gaṅgāyāṃ yadi labhyeta koṭisūryagrahādhikā //
1.122.d:
यदीयं शनिना युक्ता सा महावारुणी स्मृता ।
गङ्गायां यदि लभ्येत कोटिसूर्यग्रहाधिका ॥
1.122.m: If this [thirteenth tithi] is conjoined with Saturn, it is known as the Mahāvāruṇī; / if it is attained at the Gaṅgā, it is greater than ten million solar eclipses.

1.122.s:
śubhayogaḥ śatarkṣaṃ ca śanau kāme madhau site /
mahāmaheti vikhyātā kulakoṭivimuktidā //
1.122.d:
शुभयोगः शतर्क्षं च शनौ कामे मधौ सिते ।
महामहेति विख्याता कुलकोटिविमुक्तिदा ॥
1.122.m: With an auspicious conjunction, the Śatabhiṣaj lunar mansion, on Saturn's day, on the thirteenth, in the bright fortnight of Madhu, / it is renowned as the Mahāmahā, bestowing liberation on ten million ancestors of one's lineage.

1.122.s:
rādhaśuklatrayodaśyāṃ kāmadevavrataṃ smṛtam /
tatra gandhādibhiḥ kāmaṃ pūjayedupavāsavān //
1.122.d:
राधशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां कामदेवव्रतं स्मृतम् ।
तत्र गन्धादिभिः कामं पूजयेदुपवासवान् ॥
1.122.m: The vow of Kāmadeva is remembered to take place on the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha; / fasting on that day, one should worship Kāma with perfumes and other offerings.

1.122.s:
pratimāsaṃ tataḥ paścāttrayodaśyāṃ site dale /
evameva vrataṃ kāryaṃ varṣānte gāmalaṅkṛtām //
1.122.d:
प्रतिमासं ततः पश्चात्त्रयोदश्यां सिते दले ।
एवमेव व्रतं कार्यं वर्षान्ते गामलङ्कृताम् ॥
1.122.m: Thereafter, every month on the thirteenth of the bright fortnight, / this vow must be performed in the very same way. At the end of the year, an adorned cow

1.122.s:
dadyādviprāya satkṛtya vratasāṃgatvasiddhaye /
jyeṣṭhaśuklatrayodaśyāṃ daurbhāgyaśamanaṃ vratam //
1.122.d:
दद्याद्विप्राय सत्कृत्य व्रतसांगत्वसिद्धये ।
ज्येष्ठशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां दौर्भाग्यशमनं व्रतम् ॥
1.122.m: should be given to a twice-born after honoring him, for the successful completion of the vow. / On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, there is a vow that quells misfortune.

1.122.s:
tatra snātvā nadītoye pūjayecchucideśajam /
śvetamandāramarkaṃ vā karavīraṃ ca raktakam //
1.122.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा नदीतोये पूजयेच्छुचिदेशजम् ।
श्वेतमन्दारमर्कं वा करवीरं च रक्तकम् ॥
1.122.m: Having bathed there in the river water, one should worship, grown in a pure place, / a white mandāra, or an arka, and a red karavīra.

1.122.s:
nirīkṣya gagane sūryaṃ prārthayenmantratastadā /
mandārakaravīrārkā bhavanto bhāskarāṃśajāḥ //
1.122.d:
निरीक्ष्य गगने सूर्यं प्रार्थयेन्मन्त्रतस्तदा ।
मन्दारकरवीरार्का भवन्तो भास्करांशजाः ॥
1.122.m: Looking at the sun in the sky, one should then pray with this mantra: / 'O mandāra, karavīra, and arka, you are born from portions of the Sun!

1.122.s:
pūjitā mama daurbhāgyaṃ nāśayantu namo 'stu vaḥ /
itthaṃ yor'cayate bhaktyā varṣe varṣe drumatrayam //
1.122.d:
पूजिता मम दौर्भाग्यं नाशयन्तु नमो ऽस्तु वः ।
इत्थं योर्ऽचयते भक्त्या वर्षे वर्षे द्रुमत्रयम् ॥
1.122.m: Having been worshipped, may you destroy my misfortune! Salutations unto you!' / He who worships these three trees with devotion in this manner year after year,

1.122.s:
naśyate tasya daurbhāgyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
śuciśuklatrayodaśyāmekabhaktaṃ samācaret //
1.122.d:
नश्यते तस्य दौर्भाग्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
शुचिशुक्लत्रयोदश्यामेकभक्तं समाचरेत् ॥
1.122.m: his misfortune is destroyed; no doubt should be entertained here. / On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, one should observe a single meal.

1.122.s:
pūjayitvā jagannāthāvumāmāheśvarī tanūḥ /
haimyau raupyau ca mṛnmapyau yathāśaktyā vidhāya ca //
1.122.d:
पूजयित्वा जगन्नाथावुमामाहेश्वरी तनूः ।
हैम्यौ रौप्यौ च मृन्मप्यौ यथाशक्त्या विधाय च ॥
1.122.m: Having worshipped the Lords of the Universe, the bodies of Umā and Maheśvara, / fashioned of gold, silver, or clay according to one's means,

1.122.s:
siṃhokṣasthe devagṛhe goṣṭhe brāhmaṇaveśmani /
sthāpayitvā pratiṣṭhāpya daivamantreṇa nārada //
1.122.d:
सिंहोक्षस्थे देवगृहे गोष्ठे ब्राह्मणवेश्मनि ।
स्थापयित्वा प्रतिष्ठाप्य दैवमन्त्रेण नारद ॥
1.122.m: seated on a lion and a bull, in a temple, in a cowshed, or in a brāhmaṇa's house, / having installed and consecrated them with divine mantras, O Nārada,

1.122.s:
tataḥ pañcadinaṃ pūjā caikabhaktaṃ vrataṃ tathā /
tṛtīyadivase prātaḥ snātvā saṃpūjya tau punaḥ //
1.122.d:
ततः पञ्चदिनं पूजा चैकभक्तं व्रतं तथा ।
तृतीयदिवसे प्रातः स्नात्वा संपूज्य तौ पुनः ॥
1.122.m: there is worship for five days, and likewise the vow of a single meal. / On the third day, having bathed in the morning and worshipped the two again,

1.122.s:
samarpaṇīyau viprāya vedavedāṅgaśāline /
varṣe varṣe tataḥ paścādvidheyaṃ varṣapañcakam //
1.122.d:
समर्पणीयौ विप्राय वेदवेदाङ्गशालिने ।
वर्षे वर्षे ततः पश्चाद्विधेयं वर्षपञ्चकम् ॥
1.122.m: they must be presented to a twice-born possessing the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. / Thereafter, year after year, it should be performed for five years.

1.122.s:
tadante dhenuyugmena sahitau tau pradāpayet /
itthaṃ naro vā nārī vā kṛtvā vratamidaṃ śubham //
1.122.d:
तदन्ते धेनुयुग्मेन सहितौ तौ प्रदापयेत् ।
इत्थं नरो वा नारी वा कृत्वा व्रतमिदं शुभम् ॥
1.122.m: At the conclusion of that period, one should give the two along with a pair of cows. / A man or a woman who has performed this auspicious vow in this manner

1.122.s:
naiva dāṃpatyavicchedaṃ labhate saptajanmasu /
nabhaḥ śuklatrayodaśyāṃ ratikāmavrataṃ śubham //
1.122.d:
नैव दांपत्यविच्छेदं लभते सप्तजन्मसु ।
नभः शुक्लत्रयोदश्यां रतिकामव्रतं शुभम् ॥
1.122.m: never suffers separation between husband and wife for seven births. / On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa, there is the auspicious vow of Rati and Kāma,

1.122.s:
vaidhavyavāraṇaṃ strīṇāṃ tathā saṃtānavardhanam /
kṛtopavāsā kanyaiva nārī vā dvijasattama //
1.122.d:
वैधव्यवारणं स्त्रीणां तथा संतानवर्धनम् ।
कृतोपवासा कन्यैव नारी वा द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.122.m: which averts widowhood for women and increases offspring. / Fasting, whether an unmarried maiden or a married woman, O best of the twice-born,

1.122.s:
tāmre vā mṛnmaye vāpi sauvarṇe rājate tathā /
ratikāmau pravinyasya gandhādyaiḥ samyagarcayet //
1.122.d:
ताम्रे वा मृन्मये वापि सौवर्णे राजते तथा ।
रतिकामौ प्रविन्यस्य गन्धाद्यैः सम्यगर्चयेत् ॥
1.122.m: having placed Rati and Kāma upon a copper, clay, golden, / or silver vessel, one should worship them properly with perfumes and other offerings.

1.122.s:
tatastu dvijadāṃpatyaṃ caturdaśyāṃ nimantrya ca /
satakṛtya bhojya pratime dadyāttābhyāṃ sadakṣiṇe //
1.122.d:
ततस्तु द्विजदांपत्यं चतुर्दश्यां निमन्त्र्य च ।
सतकृत्य भोज्य प्रतिमे दद्यात्ताभ्यां सदक्षिणे ॥
1.122.m: Then, having invited a twice-born couple on the fourteenth, / honoring them and feeding them, one should give the two images to them along with a sacrificial fee.

1.122.s:
evaṃ caturdaśābdaṃ ca kṛtvā vratamanuttamam /
dhenuyugmānvite deye vratasaṃpūrtihetave //
1.122.d:
एवं चतुर्दशाब्दं च कृत्वा व्रतमनुत्तमम् ।
धेनुयुग्मान्विते देये व्रतसंपूर्तिहेतवे ॥
1.122.m: Having performed this unsurpassed vow in this manner for fourteen years, / [two images] accompanied by a pair of cows must be given for the sake of the vow's complete fulfillment.

1.122.s:
bhādraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ gotrirātravrataṃ smṛtam /
lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ kṛtvā sauvarṇaṃ vāpi rājatam //
1.122.d:
भाद्रशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां गोत्रिरात्रव्रतं स्मृतम् ।
लक्ष्मीनारायणं कृत्वा सौवर्णं वापि राजतम् ॥
1.122.m: On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada, the Go-trirātra vow is remembered. / Having made images of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa from gold or silver,

1.122.s:
pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya maṇḍale 'ṣṭadale śubhe /
pīṭhe vinyasya vastrāḍhyaṃ gandhādyaiḥ paripūjayet //
1.122.d:
पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य मण्डले ऽष्टदले शुभे ।
पीठे विन्यस्य वस्त्राढ्यं गन्धाद्यैः परिपूजयेत् ॥
1.122.m: bathing them with the five nectars, placing them on an auspicious eight-petalled sacred diagram / and a ritual seat, lavishly adorned with garments, one should worship them completely with perfumes and other offerings.

1.122.s:
ārārtikaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā dadyātsānnodakaṃ ghaṭam /
evaṃ dinatrayaṃ kṛtvā vratānte māsamarcya ca //
1.122.d:
आरार्तिकं ततः कृत्वा दद्यात्सान्नोदकं घटम् ।
एवं दिनत्रयं कृत्वा व्रतान्ते मासमर्च्य च ॥
1.122.m: Then, having performed the wave-offering of lamps, one should give a pot with food and water. / Having done this for three days and worshipped for a month at the end of the vow,

1.122.s:
samyagarthaṃ ca saṃpādya dadyānmantreṇa nārada /
pañcagāvaḥ samutpannā mathyamāne mahodadhau //
1.122.d:
सम्यगर्थं च संपाद्य दद्यान्मन्त्रेण नारद ।
पञ्चगावः समुत्पन्ना मथ्यमाने महोदधौ ॥
1.122.m: and having properly prepared the offering, one should give it with the mantra, O Nārada: / 'Five cows arose when the great ocean was churned;

1.122.s:
tāsāṃ madhye tu yā nandā tasyai dhenvai namo namaḥ /
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tato dadyādviprāya mantrataḥ //
1.122.d:
तासां मध्ये तु या नन्दा तस्यै धेन्वै नमो नमः ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ततो दद्याद्विप्राय मन्त्रतः ॥
1.122.m: among them, salutations, salutations to that milch cow Nandā!' / Then, having circumambulated it, one should give it to a twice-born with this mantra:

1.122.s:
gāvo mamāgrataḥ santu gāvo me saṃtu pṛṣṭhataḥ /
gāvo me pārśvataḥ saṃtu gavāṃ madhye vasāmyaham //
1.122.d:
गावो ममाग्रतः सन्तु गावो मे संतु पृष्ठतः ।
गावो मे पार्श्वतः संतु गवां मध्ये वसाम्यहम् ॥
1.122.m: 'May cows be in front of me; may cows be behind me; / may cows be at my sides; may I dwell in the midst of cows!'

1.122.s:
tataśca dvijadāṃpatyaṃ samyagabhyarcya bhojayet /
lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ tasmai satkṛtya pratipādayet //
1.122.d:
ततश्च द्विजदांपत्यं सम्यगभ्यर्च्य भोजयेत् ।
लक्ष्मीनारायणं तस्मै सत्कृत्य प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
1.122.m: Then, having duly worshipped a twice-born couple, one should feed them; / honoring him, one should present the image of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa to that twice-born.

1.122.s:
aśvamedhasahasrāṇi rājasūyaśatāni ca /
kṛtvā yatphalamāpnoti gotrirātravratācca tat //
1.122.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्राणि राजसूयशतानि च ।
कृत्वा यत्फलमाप्नोति गोत्रिरात्रव्रताच्च तत् ॥
1.122.m: Whatever fruit one attains by performing thousands of horse-sacrifices / and hundreds of royal-consecration sacrifices, that is attained through the Go-trirātra vow.

1.122.s:
iṣe śuklatrayodaśyāṃ trirātraśokakavratam /
haimaṃ hyaśokaṃ nirmāya pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ //
1.122.d:
इषे शुक्लत्रयोदश्यां त्रिरात्रशोककव्रतम् ।
हैमं ह्यशोकं निर्माय पूजयित्वा विधानतः ॥
1.122.m: On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, there is the three-night Aśoka vow. / Having fashioned a golden aśoka tree and worshipped it according to the rule,

1.122.s:
upavāsaparā nārī nityaṃ kuryātpradakṣiṇāḥ /
aṣṭottaraśataṃ vipra mantreṇānena sādaram //
1.122.d:
उपवासपरा नारी नित्यं कुर्यात्प्रदक्षिणाः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं विप्र मन्त्रेणानेन सादरम् ॥
1.122.m: the woman devoted to fasting should continuously perform circumambulations / one hundred and eight times, O twice-born, with respect and with this mantra:

1.122.s:
hareṇa nirmitaḥ pūrvaṃ tvamaśoka kṛpālunā /
lokopakārakaraṇastatprasīda śivapriya //
1.122.d:
हरेण निर्मितः पूर्वं त्वमशोक कृपालुना ।
लोकोपकारकरणस्तत्प्रसीद शिवप्रिय ॥
1.122.m: 'Formerly created by the compassionate Hara, / you bring welfare to the world, O Aśoka! Therefore be pleased, O darling of Śiva!'

1.122.s:
tatastṛtīye divase vṛkṣe tasminvṛṣadhvajam /
samabhyarcya vidhānena dvijaṃ saṃbhojya dāpayet //
1.122.d:
ततस्तृतीये दिवसे वृक्षे तस्मिन्वृषध्वजम् ।
समभ्यर्च्य विधानेन द्विजं संभोज्य दापयेत् ॥
1.122.m: Then, on the third day, having duly worshipped the Bull-bannered Lord / upon that tree, and having fed a twice-born, one should give it away.

1.122.s:
evaṃ kṛtavratā nārī vaidhavyaṃ nāpnuyātkvacit /
putrapautrādi sahitā bhartuśca syātsuvallabhā //
1.122.d:
एवं कृतव्रता नारी वैधव्यं नाप्नुयात्क्वचित् ।
पुत्रपौत्रादि सहिता भर्तुश्च स्यात्सुवल्लभा ॥
1.122.m: A woman who has performed this vow in this manner never suffers widowhood; / endowed with sons, grandsons, and other descendants, she becomes exceedingly dear to her husband.

1.122.s:
ūrjjakṛṣṇatrayodaśyāmekabhaktaḥ samāhitaḥ /
pradoṣe tailadīpaṃ tu prajvālyābhyarcya yatnataḥ //
1.122.d:
ऊर्ज्जकृष्णत्रयोदश्यामेकभक्तः समाहितः ।
प्रदोषे तैलदीपं तु प्रज्वाल्याभ्यर्च्य यत्नतः ॥
1.122.m: On the thirteenth of the dark fortnight of Kārttika, eating a single meal, concentrated in mind, / having carefully kindled and worshipped an oil lamp at dusk,

1.122.s:
gṛhadvāre bahirdadyādyamo me prīyatāmiti /
evaṃ kṛte tu viprendra yamapīḍā na jāyate //
1.122.d:
गृहद्वारे बहिर्दद्याद्यमो मे प्रीयतामिति ।
एवं कृते तु विप्रेन्द्र यमपीडा न जायते ॥
1.122.m: one should offer it outside the house door, reciting: 'May Yama be pleased with me.' / When this is done, O leader of the twice-born, torment by Yama does not occur.

1.122.s:
ūrjśuklatrayodaśyāmekabhojī dvijottama /
punaḥ snātvā pradoṣe tu vāgyataḥ susamāhitaḥ //
1.122.d:
ऊर्ज्शुक्लत्रयोदश्यामेकभोजी द्विजोत्तम ।
पुनः स्नात्वा प्रदोषे तु वाग्यतः सुसमाहितः ॥
1.122.m: On the thirteenth of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, eating a single meal, O best of the twice-born, / having bathed again at dusk, with speech restrained and well-concentrated,

1.122.s:
pradīpānāṃ sahasreṇa śatenāpyathavā dvija /
pradīpayecchivaṃ vāpi dvātriṃśaddīpamālayā //
1.122.d:
प्रदीपानां सहस्रेण शतेनाप्यथवा द्विज ।
प्रदीपयेच्छिवं वापि द्वात्रिंशद्दीपमालया ॥
1.122.m: with a thousand lamps, or even a hundred, O twice-born, / or with a garland of thirty-two lamps, one should illuminate Śiva.

1.122.s:
ghṛtena dīpayeddvīpāngandhādyaiḥ pūjayecchivam /
phalairnānāvidhaiścaiva naivedyairapi nārada //
1.122.d:
घृतेन दीपयेद्द्वीपान्गन्धाद्यैः पूजयेच्छिवम् ।
फलैर्नानाविधैश्चैव नैवेद्यैरपि नारद ॥
1.122.m: One should kindle the lamps with ghee and worship Śiva with perfumes and other offerings, / with various kinds of fruits, and also with food offerings, O Nārada.

1.122.s:
tataḥ stuvīta deveśaṃ śivaṃ nāmnāṃ śatena ca /
tāni nāmāni kīrtyante sarvābhīṣṭapradāni vai //
1.122.d:
ततः स्तुवीत देवेशं शिवं नाम्नां शतेन च ।
तानि नामानि कीर्त्यन्ते सर्वाभीष्टप्रदानि वै ॥
1.122.m: Then one should praise Śiva, the Lord of Gods, with a hundred names; / those names are now recited, which truly grant all desired objects:

1.122.s:
namo rudrāya bhīmāya nīlakaṇṭhāya vedhase /
kaparddine sureśāya vyomakeśāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d:
नमो रुद्राय भीमाय नीलकण्ठाय वेधसे ।
कपर्द्दिने सुरेशाय व्योमकेशाय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: 'Salutation to Rudra, to the Terrible, to the Blue-throated, to the Creator, / to the One with Braided Hair, to the Lord of the Gods, to the Sky-haired One, indeed salutation!

1.122.s:
vṛṣadhvajāya somāya somanāthāya vai namaḥ /
digaṃbarāya bhṛṅgāya umākāntāya varddhine //
1.122.d:
वृषध्वजाय सोमाय सोमनाथाय वै नमः ।
दिगंबराय भृङ्गाय उमाकान्ताय वर्द्धिने ॥
1.122.m: Salutation indeed to the Bull-bannered One, to Soma, to the Lord of Soma, / to the Space-clad One, to Bhṛṅgin, to Umā's Beloved, to the Increaser,

1.122.s:
tapomayāya vyāptāya śipiviṣyāya vai namaḥ /
vyālapriyāya vyālāya vyālānāṃ pataye namaḥ //
1.122.d:
तपोमयाय व्याप्ताय शिपिविष्याय वै नमः ।
व्यालप्रियाय व्यालाय व्यालानां पतये नमः ॥
1.122.m: to the Embodiment of Austerity, to the All-pervading, to Śipiviṣṭa, indeed salutation! / To the Serpent-lover, to the Serpent, to the Lord of Serpents, salutation!

1.122.s:
mahīdharāya vyomāya paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ /
tripuraghnāya siṃhāya śārdūlāyārṣabhāya ca //
1.122.d:
महीधराय व्योमाय पशूनां पतये नमः ।
त्रिपुरघ्नाय सिंहाय शार्दूलायार्षभाय च ॥
1.122.m: To the Earth-supporter, to the Sky, to the Lord of Beasts, salutation! / To the Slayer of Tripura, to the Lion, to the Tiger, and to the Bull,

1.122.s:
mitāya mitanāthāya siddhāya parameṣṭhine /
vedagītāya guptāya vedaguhyāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d:
मिताय मितनाथाय सिद्धाय परमेष्ठिने ।
वेदगीताय गुप्ताय वेदगुह्याय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: to the Measured, to the Lord of the Measured, to the Perfected, to the Supreme Lord, / to the One Sung by the Vedas, to the Hidden, to the Mystery of the Vedas, salutation!'

1.122.s:
dīrghāya dīrgharūpāya dīrghārthāya mahīyase /
namo jagatpratiṣṭhāya vyomarūpāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d:
दीर्घाय दीर्घरूपाय दीर्घार्थाय महीयसे ।
नमो जगत्प्रतिष्ठाय व्योमरूपाय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: Homage to the vast, to the one whose form is vast, to the vast-purposed, to the most exalted! / Homage to the support of the world, to the one whose form is space; homage indeed!

1.122.s:
kalyāṇāya viśiṣyāya śiṣṭāya paramātmane /
gajakṛtti dharāyātha andhakāsurabhedine //
1.122.d:
कल्याणाय विशिष्याय शिष्टाय परमात्मने ।
गजकृत्ति धरायाथ अन्धकासुरभेदिने ॥
1.122.m: To the auspicious, to the most distinguished, to the disciplined, to the Supreme Self, / to the wearer of the elephant skin, and then to the slayer of the demon Andhaka;

1.122.s:
nīlalohitaśuklāya caḍamuṇḍapriyāya ca /
bhaktipriyāya devāya yajñāntāyāvyayāya ca //
1.122.d:
नीललोहितशुक्लाय चडमुण्डप्रियाय च ।
भक्तिप्रियाय देवाय यज्ञान्तायाव्ययाय च ॥
1.122.m: to the blue, red, and white, to the one beloved of Caṇḍī and Muṇḍā, / to the god who loves devotion, to the end of sacrifices, and to the imperishable;

1.122.s:
maheśāya namastubhyaṃ mahādevaharāya ca /
trinetrāya trivedāya vedāṅgāya namo namaḥ //
1.122.d:
महेशाय नमस्तुभ्यं महादेवहराय च ।
त्रिनेत्राय त्रिवेदाय वेदाङ्गाय नमो नमः ॥
1.122.m: to Maheśa, homage to you, to Mahādeva, and to Hara, / to the three-eyed, to the three Vedas, to the limb of the Veda, homage, homage!

1.122.s:
arthāyārthasvarūpāya paramārthāya vai namaḥ /
viśvarūpāya viśvāya viśvanāthāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d:
अर्थायार्थस्वरूपाय परमार्थाय वै नमः ।
विश्वरूपाय विश्वाय विश्वनाथाय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: To wealth, to the essential nature of wealth, to the supreme goal; homage indeed! / To the universal form, to the universe, to the lord of the universe; homage indeed!

1.122.s:
śaṅkarāya ca kālāya kālāvayavarūpiṇe /
arūpāya virūpāya sūkṣmasūkṣmāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d:
शङ्कराय च कालाय कालावयवरूपिणे ।
अरूपाय विरूपाय सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्माय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: To Śaṅkara, and to Time, to the one having the form of the divisions of time, / to the formless, to the multiform, to the subtlest of the subtle; homage indeed!

1.122.s:
śmaśānavāsine tubhyaṃ namaste kṛttivāsase /
śaśāṅkaśekharāyātha rudrabhūmiśritāya ca //
1.122.d:
श्मशानवासिने तुभ्यं नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे ।
शशाङ्कशेखरायाथ रुद्रभूमिश्रिताय च ॥
1.122.m: Homage to you who dwell in the cremation ground; homage to you who are clad in animal skins, / and then to the one adorned with the crescent moon, and to the one resorting to Rudra's ground;

1.122.s:
durgāya durgapārāya durgāvayavasākṣiṇe /
liṅgarūpāya liṅgāya liṅgānapataye namaḥ //
1.122.d:
दुर्गाय दुर्गपाराय दुर्गावयवसाक्षिणे ।
लिङ्गरूपाय लिङ्गाय लिङ्गानपतये नमः ॥
1.122.m: to the impassable, to the one beyond difficulty, to the witness of the limbs of Durgā, / to the one whose form is the liṅga, to the liṅga, to the lord of liṅgas; homage!

1.122.s: namaḥ prabhāvarūpāya prabhāvārthāya vai namaḥ //
1.122.d: नमः प्रभावरूपाय प्रभावार्थाय वै नमः ॥
1.122.m: Homage to the one whose form is majesty, to the goal of majesty; homage indeed!

1.122.s:
namo namaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya te mṛtyuñjayāyātmabhavasvarūpiṇe /
triyaṃbakāya śitikaṇṭhabhārgiṇe gaurīyuje maṅgalahetave namaḥ //
1.122.d:
नमो नमः कारणकारणाय ते मृत्युञ्जयायात्मभवस्वरूपिणे ।
त्रियंबकाय शितिकण्ठभार्गिणे गौरीयुजे मङ्गलहेतवे नमः ॥
1.122.m: Homage, homage to you, the cause of causes, the conqueror of death, the one whose essential nature is self-born, / the three-eyed one, the blue-throated Bhārgava, united with Gaurī, the source of auspiciousness; homage!

1.122.s:
nāmnāṃ śatamidaṃ vipra pinākiguṇakīrtanam /
paṭhitvā dakṣiṇīkṛtya prāyānnijaniketanam //
1.122.d:
नाम्नां शतमिदं विप्र पिनाकिगुणकीर्तनम् ।
पठित्वा दक्षिणीकृत्य प्रायान्निजनिकेतनम् ॥
1.122.m: O brāhmaṇa, having recited this hundred names, which praises the virtues of the wielder of the Pināka, / and having circumambulated [the deity], one should go to one's own abode.

1.122.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra mahādevaprasādataḥ /
bhuktveha bhogānakhilānante śivapadaṃ labhet //
1.122.d:
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र महादेवप्रसादतः ।
भुक्त्वेह भोगानखिलानन्ते शिवपदं लभेत् ॥
1.122.m: Having observed the observance in this way, O brāhmaṇa, by the grace of Mahādeva, / after enjoying all pleasures in this world, one will attain the state of Śiva at the end.

1.122.s:
mārgaśuklatrayodaśyāṃ yo 'naṅgaṃ vidhinā yajet /
trikālamekakālaṃ vā śivasaṃgamasaṃbhavam //
1.122.d:
मार्गशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां यो ऽनङ्गं विधिना यजेत् ।
त्रिकालमेककालं वा शिवसंगमसंभवम् ॥
1.122.m: Whoever worships Anaṅga according to rule on the thirteenth day of the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, / either three times [a day] or once, arisen from the union of Śiva [and Śakti],

1.122.s:
gandhādyairupacāraistu pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ /
ghaṭe maṅgalapaṭṭe vā bhojayeddvijadaṃpatī //
1.122.d:
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैस्तु पूजयित्वा विधानतः ।
घटे मङ्गलपट्टे वा भोजयेद्द्विजदंपती ॥
1.122.m: and having worshipped [him] properly with articles of worship such as perfumes, / on a water-pot or on an auspicious board, he should feed a brāhmaṇa couple.

1.122.s:
tataśca dakṣiṇāṃ datvā svayamekāśanaṃ caret /
evaṃ kṛte tu vidhivadvratī saubhāgyabhājanaḥ //
jāyate bhuvi viprendra mahādevaprasādataḥ //
1.122.d:
ततश्च दक्षिणां दत्वा स्वयमेकाशनं चरेत् ।
एवं कृते तु विधिवद्व्रती सौभाग्यभाजनः ॥
जायते भुवि विप्रेन्द्र महादेवप्रसादतः ॥
1.122.m: Then, having given a priestly gift, he should himself eat only one meal. / When this is done according to rule, the observer of the observance becomes an owner of good fortune / in this world, O prince among brāhmaṇas, by the grace of Mahādeva.

1.122.s:
pauṣaśuklatrayodaśyāṃ samabhyarcyācyutaṃ harim /
ghṛtapātraṃ dvijendrāya pradadyātsarvasiddhaye //
1.122.d:
पौषशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां समभ्यर्च्याच्युतं हरिम् ।
घृतपात्रं द्विजेन्द्राय प्रदद्यात्सर्वसिद्धये ॥
1.122.m: On the thirteenth day of the bright half of Pauṣa, having worshipped Acyuta Hari, / he should give a vessel of clarified butter to a chief of brāhmaṇas for the attainment of all success.

1.122.s:
māghaśuklatrayodaśyāṃ samārabhya dinatrayam /
māghasnānavrataṃ vipra nānākāmaphalāvaham //
1.122.d:
माघशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां समारभ्य दिनत्रयम् ।
माघस्नानव्रतं विप्र नानाकामफलावहम् ॥
1.122.m: Beginning on the thirteenth day of the bright half of Māgha for three days, / the observance of bathing in Māgha, O brāhmaṇa, brings the fruit of diverse desires.

1.122.s:
prayāge māghamāse tu tryahaṃ snātasya yatphalam /
nāśvameghasahasreṇa tatphalaṃ labhate bhuvi //
1.122.d:
प्रयागे माघमासे तु त्र्यहं स्नातस्य यत्फलम् ।
नाश्वमेघसहस्रेण तत्फलं लभते भुवि ॥
1.122.m: The fruit that is obtained by one who bathes for three days at Prayāga in the month of Māgha / is not obtained on earth by a thousand horse-sacrifices.

1.122.s:
tatra snānaṃ japo homo dānaṃ cānantyamaśnute /
phaālgune tu site pakṣe trayodaśyāmupoṣitaḥ //
1.122.d:
तत्र स्नानं जपो होमो दानं चानन्त्यमश्नुते ।
फआल्गुने तु सिते पक्षे त्रयोदश्यामुपोषितः ॥
1.122.m: Ablution, recitation, fire oblation, and giving gifts performed there attain endlesness. / But having fasted on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight in Phālguna,

1.122.s:
namaskṛtya jagannāthaṃ prāraṃbhe dhanadavratam /
mahārājaṃ yakṣapatiṃ gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ //
1.122.d:
नमस्कृत्य जगन्नाथं प्रारंभे धनदव्रतम् ।
महाराजं यक्षपतिं गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ॥
1.122.m: having bowed to the Lord of the Universe, one begins the observance of the Giver of Wealth: / [worshipping] the great king, the lord of the yakṣas, with services such as perfumes,

1.122.s:
likhitaṃ varṇakaiḥ paṭṭe pūjayedbhaktibhāvataḥ /
evaṃ śuklatrayodaśyāṃ pratimāsaṃ dvijottama //
1.122.d:
लिखितं वर्णकैः पट्टे पूजयेद्भक्तिभावतः ।
एवं शुक्लत्रयोदश्यां प्रतिमासं द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.122.m: depicted with colors on a wooden board, he should worship with a devout heart. / In this way, on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of every month, O best of brāhmaṇas,

1.122.s:
saṃpūjayetsopavāsaścaikabhukto bhavennaraḥ /
tato vratānte tu punaḥ sauvarṇaṃ dhananāyakam //
1.122.d:
संपूजयेत्सोपवासश्चैकभुक्तो भवेन्नरः ।
ततो व्रतान्ते तु पुनः सौवर्णं धननायकम् ॥
1.122.m: a man should worship while fasting, or he may take a single meal. / Then, at the end of the observance, having further made a golden lord of wealth,

1.122.s:
vidhāya nidhibhiḥ sārddhaṃ sauvarṇābhirdvijottama /
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ snānaiḥ pañcāmṛtādibhiḥ //
1.122.d:
विधाय निधिभिः सार्द्धं सौवर्णाभिर्द्विजोत्तम ।
उपचारैः षोडशभिः स्नानैः पञ्चामृतादिभिः ॥
1.122.m: along with golden treasures, O best of brāhmaṇas, / with the sixteen services, and with baths consisting of the five nectars and the like,

1.122.s:
naivedyairvividhairbhaktyā pūjayettu samāhitaḥ /
tato dhenumalaṅkṛtya vastrasraggandhabhūṣaṇaiḥ //
1.122.d:
नैवेद्यैर्विविधैर्भक्त्या पूजयेत्तु समाहितः ।
ततो धेनुमलङ्कृत्य वस्त्रस्रग्गन्धभूषणैः ॥
1.122.m: and with diverse food-offerings, concentrated in mind, he should worship with devotion. / Then, having decorated an auspicious cow together with her calf / with garments, garlands, perfumes, and ornaments,

1.122.s:
savatsāṃ dāpayedvipra samyagvedavide śubhām /
saṃbhojya viprānmiṣṭānnairdvādaśātha trayodaśa //
1.122.d:
सवत्सां दापयेद्विप्र सम्यग्वेदविदे शुभाम् ।
संभोज्य विप्रान्मिष्टान्नैर्द्वादशाथ त्रयोदश ॥
1.122.m: O brāhmaṇa, he should present it to a proper knower of the Veda. / Having fed twelve or thirteen brāhmaṇas with sweet foods,

1.122.s:
guruṃ samarcya vastrādyaiḥ pratimāṃ tāṃ nivedayet /
dvijebhyo dakṣaṇāṃ śaktyā datvā natvā visṛjya ca //
1.122.d:
गुरुं समर्च्य वस्त्राद्यैः प्रतिमां तां निवेदयेत् ।
द्विजेभ्यो दक्षणां शक्त्या दत्वा नत्वा विसृज्य च ॥
1.122.m: and having worshipped the guru with garments and other gifts, he should present that image. / Having given a priestly gift to the brāhmaṇas according to his ability, having bowed down, and having dismissed them,

1.122.s:
svayaṃ bhuñjīta matimāniṣṭaiḥ saha samāhitaḥ /
evaṃ kṛte vrate vipra nirdhanaḥ prāpya vaibhavam //
1.122.d:
स्वयं भुञ्जीत मतिमानिष्टैः सह समाहितः ।
एवं कृते व्रते विप्र निर्धनः प्राप्य वैभवम् ॥
1.122.m: the wise man, focused in mind, should himself eat together with his cherished ones. / When the observance has been performed in this way, O brāhmaṇa, a poor man attains abundance,

1.122.s:
modate bhuvi vikhyāto rājarāja ivāparaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvādaśamāsasthitatrayodaśīvratakathanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.122.d:
मोदते भुवि विख्यातो राजराज इवापरः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वादशमासस्थितत्रयोदशीव्रतकथनं नाम द्वाविंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.122.m:
and rejoices on the earth, renowned like a second king of kings.

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-second chapter, titled 'The Exposition of the Observances of the Thirteenth Day in the Twelve Months' in the Great Narrative of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.123.s:
sanātana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi caturdaśyā vratāni te /
yāni kṛtvā naro loke sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt //
1.123.d:
सनातन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि चतुर्दश्या व्रतानि ते ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो लोके सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.123.m: Sanātana said: / Listen, O Nārada! I will tell you the observances of the fourteenth day, / by performing which a man attains all desires in the world.

1.123.s:
caitraśukla caturdaśyāṃ kuṅkumāgarucandanaiḥ /
gandhādyairvastramaṇibhiḥ kāryāryā mahatī śive //
1.123.d:
चैत्रशुक्ल चतुर्दश्यां कुङ्कुमागरुचन्दनैः ।
गन्धाद्यैर्वस्त्रमणिभिः कार्यार्या महती शिवे ॥
1.123.m: On the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra, with saffron, agallochum, and sandalwood, / with perfumes and other offerings, garments and gems, a great worship should be offered to Śivā.

1.123.s:
vitānadhvajachatrāṇi datvā pūjyāśca mātaraḥ /
evaṃ kṛtvārcanaṃ vipra sopavāso 'thavaikabhuk //
1.123.d:
वितानध्वजछत्राणि दत्वा पूज्याश्च मातरः ।
एवं कृत्वार्चनं विप्र सोपवासो ऽथवैकभुक् ॥
1.123.m: Having offered canopies, banners, and umbrellas, the Mothers should also be worshipped. / Having performed worship in this manner, O brāhmaṇa, while fasting or eating one meal,

1.123.s:
aśvamedhādhikaṃ puṇyaṃ labhate mānavo bhuvi /
atraiva damanārcāṃ ca kārayedgandhapuṣpakaiḥ //
1.123.d:
अश्वमेधाधिकं पुण्यं लभते मानवो भुवि ।
अत्रैव दमनार्चां च कारयेद्गन्धपुष्पकैः ॥
1.123.m: a mortal obtains on earth merit greater than that of a horse-sacrifice. / Right here, one should also have the worship with damana flowers performed with perfumes and blossoms;

1.123.s:
samarpayetsupūrṇāyāṃ śivāya śivarūpiṇe /
rādhakṛṣṇaca turddaśyāṃ sopavāso niśāgame //
1.123.d:
समर्पयेत्सुपूर्णायां शिवाय शिवरूपिणे ।
राधकृष्णच तुर्द्दश्यां सोपवासो निशागमे ॥
1.123.m: he should offer them to Śiva, who embodies auspiciousness, on the completely full [tithi]. / On the fourteenth day of the dark half of Vaiśākha, fasting at the arrival of night,

1.123.s:
liṅgamabhyarcayeccaivaṃ snātvā dhautāṃbaraḥ sudhīḥ /
gandhādyairupacāraiśca bilvapatraiśca sarvataḥ //
1.123.d:
लिङ्गमभ्यर्चयेच्चैवं स्नात्वा धौतांबरः सुधीः ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैश्च बिल्वपत्रैश्च सर्वतः ॥
1.123.m: having bathed and dressed in clean clothes, the wise man should worship the liṅga / with services such as perfumes, and with bilva leaves on all sides.

1.123.s:
datvā mantraṃ dvijāgryāya bhuñjīta ca pare 'hani /
evameva tu kṛṣṇāsu sarvāsu dvijasattama //
1.123.d:
दत्वा मन्त्रं द्विजाग्र्याय भुञ्जीत च परे ऽहनि ।
एवमेव तु कृष्णासु सर्वासु द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.123.m: Having given a mantra to a superior brāhmaṇa, he should eat on the next day. / In this very manner, on all dark [fourteenth days], O best of brāhmaṇas,

1.123.s:
śivavrataṃ prakartavyaṃ dhanasaṃtānamicchatā /
rādhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ śrīnṛsiṃhavrataṃ caret //
1.123.d:
शिवव्रतं प्रकर्तव्यं धनसंतानमिच्छता ।
राधशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां श्रीनृसिंहव्रतं चरेत् ॥
1.123.m: the observance of Śiva should be performed by one who desires wealth and offspring. / On the fourteenth day of the bright half of Vaiśākha, one should observe the holy observance of Nṛsiṃha.

1.123.s:
upavāsavidhānena śakto 'śaktastathaikabhuk /
niśāgame tu saṃpūjya nṛsiṃhaṃ daityasūdanam //
1.123.d:
उपवासविधानेन शक्तो ऽशक्तस्तथैकभुक् ।
निशागमे तु संपूज्य नृसिंहं दैत्यसूदनम् ॥
1.123.m: By the rule of fasting, if capable, or if incapable, eating a single meal; / and having worshipped Nṛsiṃha, the slayer of the Daityas, at the arrival of night,

1.123.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ snānaiḥ pañcāmṛtādibhiḥ /
tataḥ kṣamāpayeddevaṃ mantreṇānena nārada //
1.123.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिः स्नानैः पञ्चामृतादिभिः ।
ततः क्षमापयेद्देवं मन्त्रेणानेन नारद ॥
1.123.m: with the sixteen services and with baths consisting of the five nectars and the like, / he should then ask the god's pardon with this mantra, O Nārada:

1.123.s:
tatpahāṭakakeśānta jvalatpāvakalocana /
vajrādhikanakhasparśadivyasiṃha namo 'stu ta //
1.123.d:
तत्पहाटककेशान्त ज्वलत्पावकलोचन ।
वज्राधिकनखस्पर्शदिव्यसिंह नमो ऽस्तु त ॥
1.123.m: 'O you whose hair-tips are like molten gold, whose eyes are blazing fire, / whose touch of claws is harder than a thunderbolt, divine lion, homage be to you!'

1.123.s:
iti saṃprārthya deveśaṃ vratī syātsthaṇḍileśayaḥ /
jitendriyo jitakrodhaḥ sarvabhogavivarjjitaḥ //
1.123.d:
इति संप्रार्थ्य देवेशं व्रती स्यात्स्थण्डिलेशयः ।
जितेन्द्रियो जितक्रोधः सर्वभोगविवर्ज्जितः ॥
1.123.m: Having thus prayed to the Lord of gods, the observer of the observance should sleep on the bare ground, / with senses conquered, anger conquered, and free from all sensual enjoyments.

1.123.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute vipra vidhivadvratamuttamam /
varṣe varṣe sa labhate bhuktabhogo hareḥ padam //
1.123.d:
एवं यः कुरुते विप्र विधिवद्व्रतमुत्तमम् ।
वर्षे वर्षे स लभते भुक्तभोगो हरेः पदम् ॥
1.123.m: Whoever properly performs this excellent observance year after year in this manner, O brāhmaṇa, / after enjoying pleasures, attains the abode of Hari.

1.123.s:
oṅkāreśvarayātrā ca kāryātraiva munīśvara /
durlabhaṃ vārcanaṃ tatra darśanaṃ pāpanāśanam //
1.123.d:
ओङ्कारेश्वरयात्रा च कार्यात्रैव मुनीश्वर ।
दुर्लभं वार्चनं तत्र दर्शनं पापनाशनम् ॥
1.123.m: The pilgrimage to Oṅkāreśvara should also be undertaken at this time, O lord among sages. / Rare is the worship there; the sight of it destroys sins.

1.123.s:
kimatra bahunoktena pūjādhyānajapekṣaṇam /
yadbhavettatsamuddiṣṭaṃ jñānamokṣapradaṃ nṛṇām //
1.123.d:
किमत्र बहुनोक्तेन पूजाध्यानजपेक्षणम् ।
यद्भवेत्तत्समुद्दिष्टं ज्ञानमोक्षप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
1.123.m: What is the use of saying much here? Whatever worship, meditation, recitation, and beholding / there may be, it has been stated to grant knowledge and liberation to men.

1.123.s:
atra liṅgavrataṃ cāpi karttavyaṃ pāpanāśanam /
pañcāmṛtaistu saṃsnāpya liṅgamālipya kuṅkumaiḥ //
1.123.d:
अत्र लिङ्गव्रतं चापि कर्त्तव्यं पापनाशनम् ।
पञ्चामृतैस्तु संस्नाप्य लिङ्गमालिप्य कुङ्कुमैः ॥
1.123.m: Here, the observance of the liṅga, which destroys sins, should also be performed. / Having bathed the liṅga with the five nectars and smeared it with saffron,

1.123.s:
naivedyaiśca phalairdhūpairdīpairvastravibhūṣaṇaiḥ /
