evaṃ yaḥ pūjayetpaiṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvārthasiddhidam //
1.123.d:
नैवेद्यैश्च फलैर्धूपैर्दीपैर्वस्त्रविभूषणैः ।
एवं यः पूजयेत्पैष्टं लिङ्गं सर्वार्थसिद्धिदम् ॥
1.123.m: with food offerings, fruits, incense, lamps, garments, and ornaments, / whoever thus worships a liṅga made of flour, which grants the attainment of all aims,

1.123.s:
bhuktiṃ muktiṃ sa labhate mahādevaprasādataḥ /
jyeṣṭhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ divā pañcatapā niśaḥ //
1.123.d:
भुक्तिं मुक्तिं स लभते महादेवप्रसादतः ।
ज्येष्ठशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां दिवा पञ्चतपा निशः ॥
1.123.m: attains enjoyment and liberation by the grace of Mahādeva. / On the fourteenth day of the bright half of Jyeṣṭha, practicing the five fires during the day and at the beginning of the night,

1.123.s:
mukhe dadeddhemadhenuṃ rudravratamidaṃ smṛtam /
śuciśuklacaturdaśyāṃ śivaṃ saṃpūjya mānavaḥ //
1.123.d:
मुखे ददेद्धेमधेनुं रुद्रव्रतमिदं स्मृतम् ।
शुचिशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां शिवं संपूज्य मानवः ॥
1.123.m: one should give a golden cow; this is known as the observance of Rudra. / On the fourteenth day of the bright half of Āṣāḍha, having worshipped Śiva, a man

1.123.s:
deśakālodbhavaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sarvasaṃpadamāpnuyāt /
nabhaḥ śuklacaturdaśyāṃ pavitrāropaṇaṃ matam //
1.123.d:
देशकालोद्भवैः पुष्पैः सर्वसंपदमाप्नुयात् ।
नभः शुक्लचतुर्दश्यां पवित्रारोपणं मतम् ॥
1.123.m: With flowers born of the region and season, he obtains all prosperity. / On the bright fourteenth of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), the investiture of the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa) is recognized.

1.123.s:
tatsvaśākhoktavidhinā kartavyaṃ dvijasattama /
śatābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā tato devyai nivedayet //
1.123.d:
तत्स्वशाखोक्तविधिना कर्तव्यं द्विजसत्तम ।
शताभिमन्त्रितं कृत्वा ततो देव्यै निवेदयेत् ॥
1.123.m: It should be performed according to the rule declared in one's own Vedic branch, O best of the twice-born. / Having consecrated it a hundred times with mantra, one should then present it to the Goddess.

1.123.s:
pavitrāropaṇaṃ kṛtvā naro nāryathavā yadi /
mahādevyāḥ prasādena bhuktiṃ muktimavāpnuyāt //
1.123.d:
पवित्रारोपणं कृत्वा नरो नार्यथवा यदि ।
महादेव्याः प्रसादेन भुक्तिं मुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.123.m: If a man or a woman performs the investiture of the sacred thread, / by the grace of the Great Goddess they attain worldly enjoyment and liberation.

1.123.s:
bhādraśuklacaturdaśyāmanantavratamuttamam /
karttavyamekabhuktaṃ hi godhūmaprasthapiṣṭakam //
1.123.d:
भाद्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यामनन्तव्रतमुत्तमम् ।
कर्त्तव्यमेकभुक्तं हि गोधूमप्रस्थपिष्टकम् ॥
1.123.m: On the bright fourteenth of Bhādrapada is the excellent Anantavrata. / One should eat only once: a prastha measure of wheat flour,

1.123.s:
vipācya śarkarājyāktamanantāya nivedayet /
gandhādyaiḥ prāk samabhyarcyaḥ kārpāsaṃ paṭṭajaṃ tu vā //
1.123.d:
विपाच्य शर्कराज्याक्तमनन्ताय निवेदयेत् ।
गन्धाद्यैः प्राक् समभ्यर्च्यः कार्पासं पट्टजं तु वा ॥
1.123.m: cooked and mixed with sugar and ghee, should be offered to Ananta. / Having previously worshipped with fragrances and other offerings, a thread of cotton or silk,

1.123.s:
caturdaśagranthiyutaṃ sūtraṃ kṛtvā suśobhanam /
tataḥ purāṇamuttārya sūtraṃ kṣiptvā jalāśayeṃ //
1.123.d:
चतुर्दशग्रन्थियुतं सूत्रं कृत्वा सुशोभनम् ।
ततः पुराणमुत्तार्य सूत्रं क्षिप्त्वा जलाशयें ॥
1.123.m: made very splendid with fourteen knots, [should be prepared]. / Then, having taken off the old thread and cast it into a reservoir of water,

1.123.s:
nibaghnīyānnavaṃ nārī vāme dakṣe pumānbhuje /
vipācya piṣṭapakvaṃ tatpradadyāddakṣiṇānvitam //
1.123.d:
निबघ्नीयान्नवं नारी वामे दक्षे पुमान्भुजे ।
विपाच्य पिष्टपक्वं तत्प्रदद्याद्दक्षिणान्वितम् ॥
1.123.m: a woman should bind the new one on her left arm, and a man on his right. / Having cooked that prepared pastry, he should present it accompanied by a sacrificial fee.

1.123.s:
svayaṃ ca tanmitaṃ cādyādevaṃ kuryādvratottamam /
dvisaptavarṣaparyantaṃ tata udyāpayetsudhīḥ //
1.123.d:
स्वयं च तन्मितं चाद्यादेवं कुर्याद्व्रतोत्तमम् ।
द्विसप्तवर्षपर्यन्तं तत उद्यापयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.123.m: And he himself should eat an equal measure of it; thus one should perform the excellent vow / for a period of fourteen years; then the wise person should perform the concluding rite (udyāpana).

1.123.s:
maṇḍalaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ dhānyavarṇaiḥ prakalpya ca /
suśobhane nyasettatra kalaśaṃ tāmrajaṃ mune //
1.123.d:
मण्डलं सर्वतोभद्रं धान्यवर्णैः प्रकल्प्य च ।
सुशोभने न्यसेत्तत्र कलशं ताम्रजं मुने ॥
1.123.m: Having prepared a sarvatobhadra maṇḍala with grains of various colors, / in that very beautiful [spot] he should place a copper vessel, O sage.

1.123.s:
tasyopari nyaseddhaimīmanantapratimāṃ śubhām /
pītapaṭṭāṃśukācchannāṃ tatra tāṃ vidhinā yajet //
1.123.d:
तस्योपरि न्यसेद्धैमीमनन्तप्रतिमां शुभाम् ।
पीतपट्टांशुकाच्छन्नां तत्र तां विधिना यजेत् ॥
1.123.m: Upon it he should place an auspicious golden image of Ananta / covered with a yellow silk cloth; there he should worship it according to the rule.

1.123.s:
gaṇeśaṃ mātṛkāḥ kheṭāṃllokapāṃśca yajetpṛthak /
tato homaṃ haviṣyeṇa kṛtvā pūrṇāhutiṃ caret //
1.123.d:
गणेशं मातृकाः खेटांल्लोकपांश्च यजेत्पृथक् ।
ततो होमं हविष्येण कृत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं चरेत् ॥
1.123.m: One should worship Gaṇeśa, the Mothers, the planets, and the guardians of the directions separately; / then, having performed a fire oblation with sacrificial food (haviṣya), one should perform the final offering (pūrṇāhuti).

1.123.s:
śayyāṃ sopaskarāṃ dhenuṃ pratimāṃ ca dvijottama /
pradadyādgurave bhaktyā dvijānanyāṃścaturdaśa //
1.123.d:
शय्यां सोपस्करां धेनुं प्रतिमां च द्विजोत्तम ।
प्रदद्याद्गुरवे भक्त्या द्विजानन्यांश्चतुर्दश ॥
1.123.m: A bed with all its furnishings, a cow, and the image, O best of the twice-born, / he should give to the guru with devotion, and having fed fourteen other twice-born men

1.123.s:
saṃbhojya miṣṭapakvānnairdakṣiṇābhiḥ pratoṣayet /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute 'nantavrataṃ pratyakṣamādarāt //
1.123.d:
संभोज्य मिष्टपक्वान्नैर्दक्षिणाभिः प्रतोषयेत् ।
एवं यः कुरुते ऽनन्तव्रतं प्रत्यक्षमादरात् ॥
1.123.m: with sweet, cooked foods, he should satisfy them with sacrificial fees. / Whoever thus performs the Anantavrata openly with reverence,

1.123.s:
so 'pyanantaprasādena jāyate bhuktimuktibhāk /
kadalīvratamapyatra tadvidhānaṃ ca me śṛṇu //
1.123.d:
सो ऽप्यनन्तप्रसादेन जायते भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् ।
कदलीव्रतमप्यत्र तद्विधानं च मे शृणु ॥
1.123.m: he too, by the grace of Ananta, comes to partake of enjoyment and liberation. / The kadalī vow also occurs here; hear from me its rite.

1.123.s:
naro vā yadi vā nārī raṃbhāmupavanasthitām /
snātvā saṃpūjayedgandhapuṣpadhānyāṅkurādibhiḥ //
1.123.d:
नरो वा यदि वा नारी रंभामुपवनस्थिताम् ।
स्नात्वा संपूजयेद्गन्धपुष्पधान्याङ्कुरादिभिः ॥
1.123.m: A man or a woman, having bathed, should worship / a plantain tree standing in a garden with fragrant pastes, flowers, grain-sprouts, and the like,

1.123.s:
dadhidūrvākṣatairddvīpairvastrapakkānnasaṃ cathaiḥ /
evaṃ saṃpūjya mantreṇa tataḥ saṃprārthayerdvatī //
1.123.d:
दधिदूर्वाक्षतैर्द्द्वीपैर्वस्त्रपक्कान्नसं चथैः ।
एवं संपूज्य मन्त्रेण ततः संप्रार्थयेर्द्वती ॥
1.123.m: with curd, dūrvā grass, unbroken grain, lamps, cloth, and an abundance of cooked food. / Having thus worshipped with mantra, the observer of the vow should then pray:

1.123.s:
apsaro marakanyābhirnāgakanyābhirārcite /
śarīrārogyalāvaṇyaṃ dehi devi namo 'stu te //
1.123.d:
अप्सरो मरकन्याभिर्नागकन्याभिरार्चिते ।
शरीरारोग्यलावण्यं देहि देवि नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.123.m: "O you who are worshipped by the maidens of the apsarases, gods, and nāgas! / Grant health of body and beauty, O goddess; homage be to you!"

1.123.s:
iti saṃprārthyaṃ kanyāstu catasro vā suvāsinīḥ /
saṃbhojyāṃ śukasidvarakajjalālaktacarcitāḥ //
1.123.d:
इति संप्रार्थ्यं कन्यास्तु चतस्रो वा सुवासिनीः ।
संभोज्यां शुकसिद्वरकज्जलालक्तचर्चिताः ॥
1.123.m: Having prayed thus, having fed four maidens or married women / adorned with garments, vermilion, collyrium, and red lac,

1.123.s:
namaskṛtya nijaṃ gehaṃ samāpya niyamaṃ vrajet /
evaṃ kṛte vrate vipra labdhvā saubhāgyamuttamam //
1.123.d:
नमस्कृत्य निजं गेहं समाप्य नियमं व्रजेत् ।
एवं कृते व्रते विप्र लब्ध्वा सौभाग्यमुत्तमम् ॥
1.123.m: and bowed to them, he should go to his own house and conclude his observance. / The vow having been performed thus, O brahmin, having attained excellent good fortune,

1.123.s:
iha loke vimānena svargaloke vrajetparam /
iṣakṛṣṇacaturddaśyāṃ viṣaśastrāṃbuvahnibhiḥ //
1.123.d:
इह लोके विमानेन स्वर्गलोके व्रजेत्परम् ।
इषकृष्णचतुर्द्दश्यां विषशस्त्रांबुवह्निभिः ॥
1.123.m: in this world, he departs beyond to heaven in a celestial vehicle. / On the dark fourteenth of Iṣa (Āśvina), for those killed by poison, weapons, water, and fire,

1.123.s:
sarpaśvāpadavajrādyairhatānāṃ brahmaghātinām /
caturddaśyāṃ kriyāśrāddhamekoddiṣṭavidhānataḥ //
1.123.d:
सर्पश्वापदवज्राद्यैर्हतानां ब्रह्मघातिनाम् ।
चतुर्द्दश्यां क्रियाश्राद्धमेकोद्दिष्टविधानतः ॥
1.123.m: by serpents, wild beasts, thunderbolts, and the like, and for slayers of brahmins, / the funeral rite (śrāddha) should be performed on the fourteenth according to the rule of an ekoddiṣṭa rite.

1.123.s:
kartavyaṃ vipravargaṃ ca bhojayenmiṣṭapakvakaiḥ /
tarpaṇaṃ ca gavāṃ grāsaṃ baliṃ caiva śvakākayoḥ //
1.123.d:
कर्तव्यं विप्रवर्गं च भोजयेन्मिष्टपक्वकैः ।
तर्पणं च गवां ग्रासं बलिं चैव श्वकाकयोः ॥
1.123.m: It should be performed, and he should feed a gathering of brahmins with sweet cooked foods. / Having made libations, an offering of food to cows, and offerings to dogs and crows,

1.123.s:
kṛtvā camya svayaṃ paścādbhuñjīyādbandhubhiḥ saha /
evaṃ yaḥ kurute vipra śrāddhaṃ saṃpannadakṣiṇam //
1.123.d:
कृत्वा चम्य स्वयं पश्चाद्भुञ्जीयाद्बन्धुभिः सह ।
एवं यः कुरुते विप्र श्राद्धं संपन्नदक्षिणम् ॥
1.123.m: and having sipped water, he himself should eat afterward along with his kinsmen. / Whoever thus performs the funeral rite with abundant sacrificial fees, O brahmin,

1.123.s:
sa uddhṛtya pitṝngaccheddevalokaṃ sanātanam /
iṣaśukla caturddaśyāṃ dharmarājaṃ dvijottama //
1.123.d:
स उद्धृत्य पितॄन्गच्छेद्देवलोकं सनातनम् ।
इषशुक्ल चतुर्द्दश्यां धर्मराजं द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.123.m: he rescues his ancestors and goes to the eternal world of the gods. / On the bright fourteenth of Iṣa, O best of the twice-born,

1.123.s:
gandhādyaiḥ samyagabhyarcya sauvarṇaṃ bhojya vāṅavam /
dadyāttasmai dharmarājastrāyate bhuvi nārada //
1.123.d:
गन्धाद्यैः सम्यगभ्यर्च्य सौवर्णं भोज्य वाङवम् ।
दद्यात्तस्मै धर्मराजस्त्रायते भुवि नारद ॥
1.123.m: having fully worshipped Dharmarāja with fragrances and other offerings, / he should give him a golden [image], food, and a vessel; Dharmarāja protects him on earth, O Nārada.

1.123.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute dharmapratimādānamuttamam /
sa bhuktveha varānbhogāndivaṃ dharmājñayā vrajet //
1.123.d:
एवं यः कुरुते धर्मप्रतिमादानमुत्तमम् ।
स भुक्त्वेह वरान्भोगान्दिवं धर्माज्ञया व्रजेत् ॥
1.123.m: Whoever makes this excellent gift of an image of Dharma / enjoys excellent pleasures here and goes to heaven by the command of Dharma.

1.123.s:
ūrjjakṛṣṇacaturddaśyāṃ tailābhyaṅgaṃ vidhūdaye /
kṛtvā snātvārcayeddharmaṃ narakādabhayaṃ labhet //
1.123.d:
ऊर्ज्जकृष्णचतुर्द्दश्यां तैलाभ्यङ्गं विधूदये ।
कृत्वा स्नात्वार्चयेद्धर्मं नरकादभयं लभेत् ॥
1.123.m: On the dark fourteenth of Ūrja (Kārttika), having applied an oil-massage at moonrise / and bathed, he should worship Dharma; he obtains freedom from fear of hell.

1.123.s:
pradoṣe tailadīpāṃstu dīpayedyamatuṣṭaye /
catuṣpathe gṛhādbrāhmapradeśe vā samāhitaḥ //
1.123.d:
प्रदोषे तैलदीपांस्तु दीपयेद्यमतुष्टये ।
चतुष्पथे गृहाद्ब्राह्मप्रदेशे वा समाहितः ॥
1.123.m: At twilight (pradoṣa), one should light oil lamps for the gratification of Yama / at a crossroads, outside the house, or in an open area, with composed mind.

1.123.s:
vatsare hemalaṃbyākhye māsi śrīmati kārtike /
śuklapakṣe caturddaśyāmaruṇābhyudayaṃ prati //
1.123.d:
वत्सरे हेमलंब्याख्ये मासि श्रीमति कार्तिके ।
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्द्दश्यामरुणाभ्युदयं प्रति ॥
1.123.m: In the year named Hemalamba, in the auspicious month of Kārttika, / on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, toward daybreak,

1.123.s:
snātvā viśveśvaro devo devaiḥ saha munīśvara /
maṇikarṇika tīrthe ca tripuṇḍraṃ bhasmanā dadhat //
1.123.d:
स्नात्वा विश्वेश्वरो देवो देवैः सह मुनीश्वर ।
मणिकर्णिक तीर्थे च त्रिपुण्ड्रं भस्मना दधत् ॥
1.123.m: Lord Viśveśvara bathed along with the gods, O lord of sages, / at the sacred ford Maṇikarṇikā, bearing the tripuṇḍra mark with ashes.

1.123.s:
svātmānaṃ svayamabhyarcya cakre pāśupatavratam /
tatastatra mahāpūjāṃ liṅge gandhādibhiścaret //
1.123.d:
स्वात्मानं स्वयमभ्यर्च्य चक्रे पाशुपतव्रतम् ।
ततस्तत्र महापूजां लिङ्गे गन्धादिभिश्चरेत् ॥
1.123.m: Having worshipped himself by himself, he undertook the Pāśupata vow. / Then he should perform a great worship to the liṅga there with fragrances and other offerings,

1.123.s:
droṇapuṣpairbilvadalairarkapuṣpaiśca ketakaiḥ /
puṣpaiḥ phalairmiṣṭapakvairnaivedyairvividhairapi //
1.123.d:
द्रोणपुष्पैर्बिल्वदलैरर्कपुष्पैश्च केतकैः ।
पुष्पैः फलैर्मिष्टपक्वैर्नैवेद्यैर्विविधैरपि ॥
1.123.m: with droṇa flowers, bilva leaves, arka flowers, and ketaka blossoms, / with flowers, fruits, sweet cooked foods, and diverse offerings.

1.123.s:
evaṃ kṛtvaikabhuktaṃ tu vrataṃ viśveśatoṣaṇam /
labhate vāñchitānkāmānihāmutra ca nārada //
1.123.d:
एवं कृत्वैकभुक्तं तु व्रतं विश्वेशतोषणम् ।
लभते वाञ्छितान्कामानिहामुत्र च नारद ॥
1.123.m: Having thus performed the vow pleasing to Viśveśa with a single meal, / one attains one's desired wishes both in this world and the next, O Nārada.

1.123.s:
brahmakūrcavrataṃ cātra kartavyamṛddhimicchatā /
sopavāsaḥ pañcagavyaṃ pibedrātrau jitendriyaḥ //
1.123.d:
ब्रह्मकूर्चव्रतं चात्र कर्तव्यमृद्धिमिच्छता ।
सोपवासः पञ्चगव्यं पिबेद्रात्रौ जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.123.m: And the Brahmakūrca vow should be performed here by one desiring prosperity. / Fasting, with senses conquered, he should drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) at night:

1.123.s:
kapilāyāstu gomūtraṃ kṛṣṇāyā gomayaṃ tathā /
śvetāyāḥ kṣīramuditaṃ raktāyāśca tathā dadhi //
1.123.d:
कपिलायास्तु गोमूत्रं कृष्णाया गोमयं तथा ।
श्वेतायाः क्षीरमुदितं रक्तायाश्च तथा दधि ॥
1.123.m: urine from a tawny cow, dung from a black cow, / milk prescribed from a white cow, and curd from a red cow;

1.123.s:
gṛhītvā karburāyāśca ghṛtamekatra melayet /
kuśāṃ bunā tataḥ prātaḥ snātvā santarpyaṃ devatāḥ //
1.123.d:
गृहीत्वा कर्बुरायाश्च घृतमेकत्र मेलयेत् ।
कुशां बुना ततः प्रातः स्नात्वा सन्तर्प्यं देवताः ॥
1.123.m: having taken ghee from a speckled cow, he should mix them together / with kuśa-grass water. Then in the morning, having bathed and satisfied the deities,

1.123.s:
brahmaṇāṃstoṣayitvā ca bhuñjīyādvāgyataḥ svayam /
brahmakūrcavrataṃ hyetatsarvapātakanāśanam //
1.123.d:
ब्रह्मणांस्तोषयित्वा च भुञ्जीयाद्वाग्यतः स्वयम् ।
ब्रह्मकूर्चव्रतं ह्येतत्सर्वपातकनाशनम् ॥
1.123.m: and having gratified the brahmins, he himself should eat with restrained speech. / For this Brahmakūrca vow destroys all sins.

1.123.s:
yacca bālye kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ kaumāre vārddhake 'pi yat /
brahmakūrcopavāsena tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati //
1.123.d:
यच्च बाल्ये कृतं पापं कौमारे वार्द्धके ऽपि यत् ।
ब्रह्मकूर्चोपवासेन तत्क्षणादेव नश्यति ॥
1.123.m: Whatever sin was committed in childhood, in youth, or in old age, / it is destroyed that very moment by the Brahmakūrca fast.

1.123.s:
pāṣāṇavratamapyatra proktaṃ tacchṛṇu nārada /
sopavāso divā naktaṃ pāṣāṇākārapiṣṭacakam //
1.123.d:
पाषाणव्रतमप्यत्र प्रोक्तं तच्छृणु नारद ।
सोपवासो दिवा नक्तं पाषाणाकारपिष्टचकम् ॥
1.123.m: The Pāṣāṇa vow is also declared here; hear that, O Nārada: / Fasting by day, at night, having worshipped a flour cake shaped like a stone,

1.123.s:
prārcya gandhādibhirgauṃrīṃ ghṛtapaṅkvamupāharet /
vratametaccaritvā tu yathoktaṃ dvijasattama //
1.123.d:
प्रार्च्य गन्धादिभिर्गौंरीं घृतपङ्क्वमुपाहरेत् ।
व्रतमेतच्चरित्वा तु यथोक्तं द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.123.m: and having worshipped Gaurī with fragrances and the like, he should offer it cooked in ghee. / Having performed this vow as declared, O best of the twice-born,

1.123.s:
aiśvaryasaukhyasaubhāgyarūpāṇi prāpnuyānnaraḥ /
mārgaśuklacaturdaśyāmekabhuktaḥ puroditam //
1.123.d:
ऐश्वर्यसौख्यसौभाग्यरूपाणि प्राप्नुयान्नरः ।
मार्गशुक्लचतुर्दश्यामेकभुक्तः पुरोदितम् ॥
1.123.m: a man attains sovereignty, happiness, good fortune, and beauty. / Having eaten once as previously stated on the bright fourteenth of Mārgaśīrṣa,

1.123.s:
nirāhāro vṛṣaṃ svarṇaṃ prārcya dadyāddvijātaye /
pare 'hni prātarutthāya snātvā somaṃ maheśvaram //
1.123.d:
निराहारो वृषं स्वर्णं प्रार्च्य दद्याद्द्विजातये ।
परे ऽह्नि प्रातरुत्थाय स्नात्वा सोमं महेश्वरम् ॥
1.123.m: and remaining without food [thereafter], having worshipped a golden bull, he should give it to a twice-born man. / Having risen in the morning on the next day and bathed, he should worship

1.123.s:
pūjayetkamalaiḥ puṣpairgandhamālyānulepanaiḥ /
dvijānsambhojya miṣṭānnaustoṣayeddakṣiṇādibhiḥ //
1.123.d:
पूजयेत्कमलैः पुष्पैर्गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ।
द्विजान्सम्भोज्य मिष्टान्नौस्तोषयेद्दक्षिणादिभिः ॥
1.123.m: Soma and Maheśvara with lotus flowers, fragrances, garlands, and unguents. / Having fed the twice-born with sweet foods, he should satisfy them with sacrificial fees and other gifts.

1.123.s:
etacchivavrataṃ vipra bhuktimuktipradāyakam /
kartṛāṇāmupadeṣṭṛāṇāṃ sāhyānāmanumodinām //
1.123.d:
एतच्छिवव्रतं विप्र भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम् ।
कर्तृआणामुपदेष्टृआणां साह्यानामनुमोदिनाम् ॥
1.123.m: This Śiva vow, O brahmin, bestows enjoyment and liberation / on those who perform it, those who teach it, those who assist it, and those who approve of it.

1.123.s:
pauṣaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ virūpākṣavrataṃ smṛtam /
kapardīśvarasāṃnidhyaṃ prāpsyāmyatra vicintya ca //
1.123.d:
पौषशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां विरूपाक्षव्रतं स्मृतम् ।
कपर्दीश्वरसांनिध्यं प्राप्स्याम्यत्र विचिन्त्य च ॥
1.123.m: On the bright fourteenth of Pauṣa, the Virūpākṣa vow is remembered. / Thinking, "Here I shall attain the presence of Kapardīśvara,"

1.123.s:
snātvāgādhajale vipra virūpākṣaṃ śivaṃ yajet /
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasaṃpadā //
1.123.d:
स्नात्वागाधजले विप्र विरूपाक्षं शिवं यजेत् ।
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसंपदा ॥
1.123.m: and having bathed in deep water, O brahmin, he should worship Virūpākṣa Śiva / with an abundance of fragrances, garlands, prostrations, incense, lamps, and food.

1.123.s:
tatsthaṃ dvijātaye dattvā modate divi devavat /
māghakṛṣṇacaturddaśyāṃ yamatarpaṇamīritam //
1.123.d:
तत्स्थं द्विजातये दत्त्वा मोदते दिवि देववत् ।
माघकृष्णचतुर्द्दश्यां यमतर्पणमीरितम् ॥
1.123.m: Having given that [image] to a twice-born man, he rejoices in heaven like a god. / On the dark fourteenth of Māgha, the water offering (tarpaṇa) to Yama is proclaimed.

1.123.s:
anarkābhyudite kāle snātvā saṃtarpayedyamam /
dvisaptanāmabhiḥ proktaiḥ sarvapāpavimuktaye //
1.123.d:
अनर्काभ्युदिते काले स्नात्वा संतर्पयेद्यमम् ।
द्विसप्तनामभिः प्रोक्तैः सर्वपापविमुक्तये ॥
1.123.m: At a time before the sun has risen, having bathed, one should offer libation to Yama / with the fourteen proclaimed names, for release from all sins.

1.123.s:
tiladarbhāṃbubhiḥ kāryaṃ tarppaṇaṃ dvijabhojanam /
kṛśarānnaṃ svayaṃ cāpi tadevāśnīta vāgyataḥ //
1.123.d:
तिलदर्भांबुभिः कार्यं तर्प्पणं द्विजभोजनम् ।
कृशरान्नं स्वयं चापि तदेवाश्नीत वाग्यतः ॥
1.123.m: The libation should be performed with sesame, darbha grass, and water, and feeding of twice-borns [should be done]; / he himself should also eat that very food of kṛśara, restraining his speech.

1.123.s:
antyakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ śivarātrivrataṃ dvija /
nirjalaṃ samupoṣyātra divānaktaṃ prapūjayet //
1.123.d:
अन्त्यकृष्णचतुर्दश्यां शिवरात्रिव्रतं द्विज ।
निर्जलं समुपोष्यात्र दिवानक्तं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.123.m: On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the final [month, Māgha or Phālguna], O twice-born, is the vow of Śivarātri; / fasting here without water, one should worship day and night,

1.123.s:
svayaṃbhuvādikaṃ liṅgaṃ pārthivaṃ vā samāhitaḥ /
gandhādyairupacāraiśca sāṃbubilvadalādibhiḥ //
1.123.d:
स्वयंभुवादिकं लिङ्गं पार्थिवं वा समाहितः ।
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैश्च सांबुबिल्वदलादिभिः ॥
1.123.m: with focused mind, a self-manifest or other linga, or an earthen one, / with perfumes and other offerings, with water, bilva leaves, and the like,

1.123.s:
dhūpairdīpaiśca naivedyaiḥ stotrapāṭhairjapādibhiḥ /
tataḥ pare 'hni saṃpūjya punarevopacārakaiḥ //
1.123.d:
धूपैर्दीपैश्च नैवेद्यैः स्तोत्रपाठैर्जपादिभिः ।
ततः परे ऽह्नि संपूज्य पुनरेवोपचारकैः ॥
1.123.m: with incenses, lamps, food offerings, recitations of hymns, mantras, and so forth. / Then, on the following day, having worshipped again with the offerings,

1.123.s:
saṃbhojya viprānmiṣṭānnairvisṛjellabdhadakṣiṇān /
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ martyo mahādevaprasādataḥ //
1.123.d:
संभोज्य विप्रान्मिष्टान्नैर्विसृजेल्लब्धदक्षिणान् ।
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं मर्त्यो महादेवप्रसादतः ॥
1.123.m: having fed the brahmins with sweet foods, one should dismiss them after they have received their priestly fees. / Having performed this vow in this manner, a mortal, by the grace of Mahādeva,

1.123.s:
amartyabhogān labhate daivataiḥ susabhājitaḥ /
antyaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ durgāṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ //
1.123.d:
अमर्त्यभोगान् लभते दैवतैः सुसभाजितः ।
अन्त्यशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां दुर्गां संपूज्य भक्तितः ॥
1.123.m: attains immortal pleasures, warmly honoured by the gods. / Having worshipped Durgā with devotion on the fourteenth day of the final bright fortnight,

1.123.s:
gandhādyairupacāraistu viprānsaṃbhojayettataḥ /
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra durgāyāścaikabhojanaḥ //
1.123.d:
गन्धाद्यैरुपचारैस्तु विप्रान्संभोजयेत्ततः ।
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र दुर्गायाश्चैकभोजनः ॥
1.123.m: with perfumes and other offerings, one should then feed brahmins. / Having performed this vow of Durgā in this manner, O twice-born, eating only once a day,

1.123.s:
labhate vāñchitānkāmānihāmutra ca nārada /
caitrakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāmupavāsaṃ vidhāya ca //
1.123.d:
लभते वाञ्छितान्कामानिहामुत्र च नारद ।
चैत्रकृष्णचतुर्दश्यामुपवासं विधाय च ॥
1.123.m: one obtains desired pleasures in this world and the next, O Nārada. / And having observed a fast on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Caitra,

1.123.s:
kedārodakapānena vācimedhaphalaṃ bhavet /
udyāpane tu sarvāṃsāṃ sāmānyo vidhirucyate //
1.123.d:
केदारोदकपानेन वाचिमेधफलं भवेत् ।
उद्यापने तु सर्वांसां सामान्यो विधिरुच्यते ॥
1.123.m: by drinking the water of Kedāra, the fruit of a horse-sacrifice is gained. / Now the common rule for the concluding rite of all [the fourteenth-day vows] is stated:

1.123.s:
kuṃbhāścaturdaśaivātra sapūgākṣatamodakāḥ /
sadakṣiṇāṃśukāstāmrāmṛnmayāścāvraṇā navāḥ //
1.123.d:
कुंभाश्चतुर्दशैवात्र सपूगाक्षतमोदकाः ।
सदक्षिणांशुकास्ताम्रामृन्मयाश्चाव्रणा नवाः ॥
1.123.m: Fourteen pots indeed here, with areca nuts, unbroken grain, and sweetmeats, / with priestly gifts and garments, made of copper and earthenware, unblemished and new,

1.123.s:
tāvanto vaśadaṇḍāśca pavitrāṇyāsanāni ca /
pātrāṇi yajñasūtrāṇi tāvatyeva hi kalpayet //
1.123.d:
तावन्तो वशदण्डाश्च पवित्राण्यासनानि च ।
पात्राणि यज्ञसूत्राणि तावत्येव हि कल्पयेत् ॥
1.123.m: as many bamboo staffs, purification rings, seats, / vessels, and sacred threads indeed should one prepare.

1.123.s:
śeṣaṃ prāguktavatkuryādvittaśāṭhyavivarjjitaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthabhāge dvādaśamāsasthitacaturdaśīvratavarṇanaṃ nāma trayoviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.123.d:
शेषं प्रागुक्तवत्कुर्याद्वित्तशाठ्यविवर्ज्जितः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थभागे द्वादशमासस्थितचतुर्दशीव्रतवर्णनं नाम त्रयोविंशत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
1.123.m:
The remainder he should perform as previously stated, devoid of dishonesty regarding wealth.

Thus ends the hundred and twenty-third chapter, named the Description of the Vow of the Fourteenth Day throughout the Twelve Months, in the fourth part of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the Pūrvabhāga of the illustrious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.124.s:
sanātana uvāca
atha nārada vakṣyāmi śṛṇu pūrṇāvratāni te /
yāni kṛtvā naro nārī prāpnuyātsukhasaṃtatim //
1.124.d:
सनातन उवाच
अथ नारद वक्ष्यामि शृणु पूर्णाव्रतानि ते ।
यानि कृत्वा नरो नारी प्राप्नुयात्सुखसंततिम् ॥
1.124.m: Sanātana said: / Now, O Nārada, I will speak to you of the full-moon vows; listen, / by performing which a man or a woman will obtain unbroken happiness.

1.124.s:
caitrapūrṇā tu viprendra manvādiḥ samudāhṛtā /
asyāṃ sānnodakaṃ kuṃbhaṃ pradadyātsomatuṣṭaye //
1.124.d:
चैत्रपूर्णा तु विप्रेन्द्र मन्वादिः समुदाहृता ।
अस्यां सान्नोदकं कुंभं प्रदद्यात्सोमतुष्टये ॥
1.124.m: The full moon of Caitra, O chief of twice-borns, is declared to be the beginning of a Manvantara; / on this day, one should give a jar containing food and water for the pleasure of Soma.

1.124.s:
vaiśākhyāmapi pūrṇāyāṃ dānaṃ sarvasya sarvadam /
yadyaddravyaṃ dadedvipre tattadāpnoti niścitam //
1.124.d:
वैशाख्यामपि पूर्णायां दानं सर्वस्य सर्वदम् ।
यद्यद्द्रव्यं ददेद्विप्रे तत्तदाप्नोति निश्चितम् ॥
1.124.m: Also on the full moon of Vaiśākha, giving one's all bestows everything; / whatever item one gives to a brahmin, that very thing he surely obtains.

1.124.s:
dharmarājavrataṃ cātra kathitaṃ tanniśāmaya /
śṛtānnamudakuṃbhaṃ ca vaiśākhyāṃ vai dvijottame //
1.124.d:
धर्मराजव्रतं चात्र कथितं तन्निशामय ।
शृतान्नमुदकुंभं च वैशाख्यां वै द्विजोत्तमे ॥
1.124.m: And the vow of Dharmarāja here is related; listen to it: / Cooked food and a water-pot, on the full moon of Vaiśākha, indeed, to an excellent twice-born,

1.124.s:
dadyādgodānaphaladaṃ dharmarājasya tuṣṭaye /
atra kṛṣṇājinaṃ dadyātsakhuraṃ ca saśṛṅgakam //
1.124.d:
दद्याद्गोदानफलदं धर्मराजस्य तुष्टये ।
अत्र कृष्णाजिनं दद्यात्सखुरं च सशृङ्गकम् ॥
1.124.m: one should give, yielding the fruit of the gift of a cow, for the pleasure of Dharmarāja. / Here, one should give a black buckskin with hooves and horns,

1.124.s:
tilaiḥ sahasamācchādya vastrairhemnā dvijātaye /
yastu kṛṣṇājinaṃ dadyātsatkṛtya vidhipūrvakam //
1.124.d:
तिलैः सहसमाच्छाद्य वस्त्रैर्हेम्ना द्विजातये ।
यस्तु कृष्णाजिनं दद्यात्सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.124.m: covered with sesame seeds, along with garments and gold, to a twice-born. / The one who gives a black buckskin, having honoured [him] according to rule,

1.124.s:
sarvaśāstravide saptadvīpabhūmipradaḥ sa vai /
modate viṣṇu loke hi yāvaccandrārkatārakam //
1.124.d:
सर्वशास्त्रविदे सप्तद्वीपभूमिप्रदः स वै ।
मोदते विष्णु लोके हि यावच्चन्द्रार्कतारकम् ॥
1.124.m: to a knower of all the scriptures, is indeed a giver of the earth with its seven continents; / he rejoices in the world of Viṣṇu as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

1.124.s:
kuṃbhānsvacchajalaiḥ pūrṇānhiraṇyena samanvitān /
yaḥ pradadyāddvijāgryebhyaḥ sa na śocati karhicit //
1.124.d:
कुंभान्स्वच्छजलैः पूर्णान्हिरण्येन समन्वितान् ।
यः प्रदद्याद्द्विजाग्र्येभ्यः स न शोचति कर्हिचित् ॥
1.124.m: He who gives jars filled with clear water, accompanied by gold, / to the best of twice-borns, never grieves.

1.124.s:
atha jyeṣṭasya pūrṇāyāṃ vaṭasāvitrikaṃ vratam /
sopavāsā vaṭaṃ siṃcetsalilairamṛtopamaiḥ //
1.124.d:
अथ ज्येष्टस्य पूर्णायां वटसावित्रिकं व्रतम् ।
सोपवासा वटं सिंचेत्सलिलैरमृतोपमैः ॥
1.124.m: Now, on the full moon of Jyeṣṭha is the vow of Vaṭasāvitrī. / Fasting, she should sprinkle the banyan tree with waters resembling nectar,

1.124.s:
sṛtreṇa veṣṭayeccaiva saśatāṣṭapradakṣiṇam /
tataḥ saṃprārthaddaivīṃ sāvitrīṃ supativratām //
1.124.d:
सृत्रेण वेष्टयेच्चैव सशताष्टप्रदक्षिणम् ।
ततः संप्रार्थद्दैवीं सावित्रीं सुपतिव्रताम् ॥
1.124.m: and wrap it with thread while making one hundred and eight circumambulations. / Then she should pray to the divine Sāvitrī, devoted to her husband:

1.124.s:
jagatpūjye jaganmātaḥ sāvitri patidaivate /
patyā sahāviyogaṃ me vaṭasthe kuru te namaḥ //
1.124.d:
जगत्पूज्ये जगन्मातः सावित्रि पतिदैवते ।
पत्या सहावियोगं मे वटस्थे कुरु ते नमः ॥
1.124.m: “O you worshipped by the world, O mother of the world, O Sāvitrī whose deity is her husband! / Residing in the banyan tree, make me never separated from my husband; reverence to you!”

1.124.s:
iti saprārthya yā nārī bhojayitvā pare 'hani /
suvāsinīḥ svayaṃ bhuñjyātsā syātsaubhāgyabhāginī //
1.124.d:
इति सप्रार्थ्य या नारी भोजयित्वा परे ऽहनि ।
सुवासिनीः स्वयं भुञ्ज्यात्सा स्यात्सौभाग्यभागिनी ॥
1.124.m: Having prayed thus, the woman who, having fed auspicious married women on the next day, / eats herself, will share in good fortune.

1.124.s:
āṣāḍhasya tu pūrṇāyāṃ gopadmavratamucyate /
caturbhujaṃ mahākāyaṃ jāṃbūnadasamaprabham //
1.124.d:
आषाढस्य तु पूर्णायां गोपद्मव्रतमुच्यते ।
चतुर्भुजं महाकायं जांबूनदसमप्रभम् ॥
1.124.m: On the full moon of Āṣāḍha, the vow of Gopadma is taught. / [Meditating on Hari as] having four arms, a vast body, radiant like Jambūnada gold,

1.124.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmaramāgaruḍaśobhitam /
sevitaṃ munibhirdevairyakṣagandharvakinnaraiḥ //
1.124.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मरमागरुडशोभितम् ।
सेवितं मुनिभिर्देवैर्यक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरैः ॥
1.124.m: adorned with conch, discus, mace, and lotus, Ramā and Garuḍa, / served by sages, gods, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kinnaras,

1.124.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ hariṃ tatra snātvā pūjāṃ samācaret /
pauruṣeṇaiva sūktena gandhādyairupacārakaiḥ //
1.124.d:
एवंविधं हरिं तत्र स्नात्वा पूजां समाचरेत् ।
पौरुषेणैव सूक्तेन गन्धाद्यैरुपचारकैः ॥
1.124.m: having bathed, one should perform the worship of Hari of such a form there / using the Puruṣasūkta, with perfumes and other offerings.

1.124.s:
ācāryaṃ vastrabhūṣādyaistoṣayetsnigdhamānasaḥ /
bhojayenmiṣṭapakvānnairdvijānanyāṃśca śaktitaḥ //
1.124.d:
आचार्यं वस्त्रभूषाद्यैस्तोषयेत्स्निग्धमानसः ।
भोजयेन्मिष्टपक्वान्नैर्द्विजानन्यांश्च शक्तितः ॥
1.124.m: With an affectionate mind, one should please the ācārya with garments, ornaments, and the like, / and feed brahmins and others according to one's capacity with sweet cooked foods.

1.124.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ vipra prasādātkamalāpateḥ /
aihikāmuṣmikānkāmāṃllabhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.124.d:
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र प्रसादात्कमलापतेः ।
ऐहिकामुष्मिकान्कामांल्लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.124.m: Having performed the vow thus, O twice-born, by the grace of the Lord of Kamalā, / one obtains desires of this world and the next; there is no doubt about this.

1.124.s:
kokilāvratamapyatra proktaṃ tadvidhirucyate /
pūrṇimāyāṃ samārabhya vrataṃ snāyādbrahirjale //
1.124.d:
कोकिलाव्रतमप्यत्र प्रोक्तं तद्विधिरुच्यते ।
पूर्णिमायां समारभ्य व्रतं स्नायाद्ब्रहिर्जले ॥
1.124.m: The Kokilā vow also is declared here; its procedure is stated: / Beginning on the full-moon day, one should bathe in water outside [the village]

1.124.s:
pūrṇāntaṃ śrāvaṇe māsi gaurīrūpāṃ ca kokilām /
svarṇapakṣāṃ ratnanetrāṃ pravālamukhapaṅkajām //
1.124.d:
पूर्णान्तं श्रावणे मासि गौरीरूपां च कोकिलाम् ।
स्वर्णपक्षां रत्ननेत्रां प्रवालमुखपङ्कजाम् ॥
1.124.m: until the full moon in the month of Śrāvaṇa; and [worship] the cuckoo in the form of Gaurī, / with golden wings, gem-like eyes, and a lotus-like coral beak,

1.124.s:
kastūrīvarṇasaṃyuktāmutpannāṃ nandane vane /
cūtacaṃpakavṛkṣasthāṃ kalagītaninādinīm //
1.124.d:
कस्तूरीवर्णसंयुक्तामुत्पन्नां नन्दने वने ।
चूतचंपकवृक्षस्थां कलगीतनिनादिनीम् ॥
1.124.m: endowed with the colour of musk, born in the Nandana forest, / perched upon mango and campaka trees, sounding with sweet songs.

1.124.s:
cintayetpārvatīṃ devīṃ kokilārūpadhāriṇīm /
gandhādyaiḥ pratyahaṃ prārccellikhitāṃ varṇakaiḥ paṭe //
1.124.d:
चिन्तयेत्पार्वतीं देवीं कोकिलारूपधारिणीम् ।
गन्धाद्यैः प्रत्यहं प्रार्च्चेल्लिखितां वर्णकैः पटे ॥
1.124.m: One should meditate upon the goddess Pārvatī who has taken the form of a cuckoo; / painted with colours on a cloth, one should worship her daily with perfumes and other offerings.

1.124.s:
tato vratānte haimīṃ vā tilapiṣṭamayīṃ dvija /
dadyādviprāya mantreṇa bhaktyā sasvarṇadakṣiṇām //
1.124.d:
ततो व्रतान्ते हैमीं वा तिलपिष्टमयीं द्विज ।
दद्याद्विप्राय मन्त्रेण भक्त्या सस्वर्णदक्षिणाम् ॥
1.124.m: Then, at the end of the vow, O twice-born, [an image] made of gold or of sesame flour, / one should give with devotion to a brahmin with a mantra, together with a priestly fee in gold:

1.124.s:
devīṃ caitrarathotpanne kokile haravallabhe /
saṃpūjya dattā viprāya sarvasaukhyakarī bhava //
1.124.d:
देवीं चैत्ररथोत्पन्ने कोकिले हरवल्लभे ।
संपूज्य दत्ता विप्राय सर्वसौख्यकरी भव ॥
1.124.m: “O goddess, born in the Caitraratha forest, O cuckoo, beloved of Hara! / Being worshipped and given to the brahmin, bring about all happiness!”

1.124.s:
dvijaṃ suvāsinīstriṃśadekāṃ vā bhojayettataḥ /
vastrādidakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā datvā natvā visarjayet //
1.124.d:
द्विजं सुवासिनीस्त्रिंशदेकां वा भोजयेत्ततः ।
वस्त्रादिदक्षिणां शक्त्या दत्वा नत्वा विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Then one should feed thirty auspicious married women, or even one, along with a twice-born; / having given priestly gifts of garments and so forth according to ability, and having bowed, one should dismiss them.

1.124.s:
evaṃ yā kurute nārī kokilāvratamuttam /
sā labhetsukhasaubhāgyaṃ saptajanmasunārada //
1.124.d:
एवं या कुरुते नारी कोकिलाव्रतमुत्तम् ।
सा लभेत्सुखसौभाग्यं सप्तजन्मसुनारद ॥
1.124.m: The woman who performs this supreme Kokilā vow in this manner / shall obtain happiness and good fortune for seven births, O Nārada.

1.124.s:
atha śrāvaṇapūrṇāyāṃ vedopākaraṇaṃ smṛtam /
yajurbhistatra karttavyaṃ devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam //
1.124.d:
अथ श्रावणपूर्णायां वेदोपाकरणं स्मृतम् ।
यजुर्भिस्तत्र कर्त्तव्यं देवर्षिपितृतर्पणम् ॥
1.124.m: Now, on the Śrāvaṇa full moon, the commencement of Vedic study is prescribed; / libations to gods, ṛṣis, and ancestors are to be performed there by followers of the Yajurveda,

1.124.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ pūjanaṃ cāpi svaśākhoktavidhānataḥ /
bahavṛcaistu caturdvaśyāṃ sāmagairbhādrage kare //
1.124.d:
ऋषीणां पूजनं चापि स्वशाखोक्तविधानतः ।
बहवृचैस्तु चतुर्द्वश्यां सामगैर्भाद्रगे करे ॥
1.124.m: and worship of the ṛṣis as well, according to the rule prescribed in one’s own Vedic branch. / By Rigvedins, however, [it is performed] on the fourteenth; by Samavedins, when the moon is in Hasta in Bhādrapada.

1.124.s: rakṣāvidhānaṃ ca tathā kartavyaṃ vidhipūrvakam //
1.124.d: रक्षाविधानं च तथा कर्तव्यं विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.124.m: And likewise, the protective ritual should be performed according to rule:

1.124.s:
siddhārthākṣatarājikāśca vidhṛtā raktāṃśukāṃśe sitāḥ kausuṃbhena ca tantunātha salilaiḥ prakṣālya kāṃsye dhṛtāḥ /
gandhādyairabhipūjya devanikarānsaṃprārthya viṣṇvādikānbadhnīyāddvijahastataḥ pramudito natvā prakoṣṭhe svake //
1.124.d:
सिद्धार्थाक्षतराजिकाश्च विधृता रक्तांशुकांशे सिताः कौसुंभेन च तन्तुनाथ सलिलैः प्रक्षाल्य कांस्ये धृताः ।
गन्धाद्यैरभिपूज्य देवनिकरान्संप्रार्थ्य विष्ण्वादिकान्बध्नीयाद्द्विजहस्ततः प्रमुदितो नत्वा प्रकोष्ठे स्वके ॥
1.124.m: White mustard seeds, unbroken grains, and black mustard seeds, placed in a piece of red cloth with a safflower thread, washed with water and held in a brass vessel, / worshipped with perfumes and the like, having prayed to the assembly of gods, Viṣṇu and others, one should joyfully, having bowed, bind it on his wrist from the hand of a twice-born.

1.124.s:
tatastu dakṣiṇāṃ datvā dvijebhyo 'dhyāyamācaret /
visṛjya ca ṛṣīnsapta dhārayedbrahmasūtrakam //
1.124.d:
ततस्तु दक्षिणां दत्वा द्विजेभ्यो ऽध्यायमाचरेत् ।
विसृज्य च ऋषीन्सप्त धारयेद्ब्रह्मसूत्रकम् ॥
1.124.m: Then, having given a fee to the twice-borns, he should commence Vedic study; / and having dismissed the seven sages, he should put on the sacred thread,

1.124.s:
rañjitaṃ kuṅkumādyaiśca navīnaṃ nirmitaṃ svayam /
śaktyā saṃbhojya viprāgryānekabhuktaṃ samācaret //
1.124.d:
रञ्जितं कुङ्कुमाद्यैश्च नवीनं निर्मितं स्वयम् ।
शक्त्या संभोज्य विप्राग्र्यानेकभुक्तं समाचरेत् ॥
1.124.m: which is coloured with saffron and the like, newly made by oneself. / Having fed the best of twice-borns according to one's capacity, one should eat only one meal [that day].

1.124.s:
kṛte hyasminvrate vipra vārṣikaṃ karmaṃ vaidikam /
vismṛtaṃ vidhihīnaṃ ca na kṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet //
1.124.d:
कृते ह्यस्मिन्व्रते विप्र वार्षिकं कर्मं वैदिकम् ।
विस्मृतं विधिहीनं च न कृतं सुकृतं भवेत् ॥
1.124.m: When this vow is performed, O twice-born, the annual Vedic rite / that was forgotten, deficient in rule, or unperformed, becomes well-performed.

1.124.s:
prauṣṭhapadyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmumāmāheśvaravratam /
ekabhuktaśca yastāṃ tu śivaṃ saṃpūjya yatnataḥ //
1.124.d:
प्रौष्ठपद्यां पौर्णमास्यामुमामाहेश्वरव्रतम् ।
एकभुक्तश्च यस्तां तु शिवं संपूज्य यत्नतः ॥
1.124.m: On the full moon day of Prauṣṭhapadā is the Umā-Māheśvara observance. / Having eaten once [the previous day], one who worships Śiva with care,

1.124.s:
kṛtāñjaliḥ prārthayecchvaḥ kariṣye ca vrataṃ prabho /
evaṃ vijñāpya devaṃ tu gṛhṇīyādvratamuttamam //
1.124.d:
कृताञ्जलिः प्रार्थयेच्छ्वः करिष्ये च व्रतं प्रभो ।
एवं विज्ञाप्य देवं तु गृह्णीयाद्व्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
1.124.m: Should pray with folded hands: ‘Tomorrow I will perform the observance, O Lord.’ / Having thus petitioned the god, he should undertake the supreme observance.

1.124.s:
rātrau devāntike suptvā utthāyāparayāmake /
kṛtamaitrādinityastu bhasmarudrākṣadhṛk tataḥ //
1.124.d:
रात्रौ देवान्तिके सुप्त्वा उत्थायापरयामके ।
कृतमैत्रादिनित्यस्तु भस्मरुद्राक्षधृक् ततः ॥
1.124.m: Having slept near the god at night and arisen in the final watch, / having performed the morning duties and the like, wearing ashes and rudrākṣa beads,

1.124.s:
pūjayecchaṅkaraṃ samyagupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ /
bilvapatraiḥ sugandhāḍhyerṃnaivedyairdhūpadīpakaiḥ //
1.124.d:
पूजयेच्छङ्करं सम्यगुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः ।
बिल्वपत्रैः सुगन्धाढ्येर्ंनैवेद्यैर्धूपदीपकैः ॥
1.124.m: He should properly worship Śaṅkara with various types of services, / with bilva leaves, fragrant offerings, food offerings, incense, and lamps.

1.124.s:
tataścopavasedvidvānāpradoṣaṃ vindhūdaye /
punaḥ saṃpūjya tatraiva rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ caret //
1.124.d:
ततश्चोपवसेद्विद्वानाप्रदोषं विन्धूदये ।
पुनः संपूज्य तत्रैव रात्रौ जागरणं चरेत् ॥
1.124.m: Then the wise man should fast until twilight; when the moon rises, / having worshipped again right there, he should keep vigil through the night.

1.124.s:
evaṃ pañcadaśābdāntaṃ kṛtvā vratamatandritaḥ /
varṣe varṣe tadutsarge vidadhyādvidhipūrvakam //
1.124.d:
एवं पञ्चदशाब्दान्तं कृत्वा व्रतमतन्द्रितः ।
वर्षे वर्षे तदुत्सर्गे विदध्याद्विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.124.m: Having performed the observance thus unwearied until fifteen years [have elapsed], / year after year, he should carry out its formal conclusion according to the rules.

1.124.s:
umāyāśca maheśasya sauvarṇī pratimādvayam /
haimā raupyā mṛnmayāśca ghaṭāḥ pañcadaśottamāḥ //
1.124.d:
उमायाश्च महेशस्य सौवर्णी प्रतिमाद्वयम् ।
हैमा रौप्या मृन्मयाश्च घटाः पञ्चदशोत्तमाः ॥
1.124.m: Two golden images of Umā and Maheśa [are made], / and fifteen excellent jars of gold, silver, or clay.

1.124.s:
tatraikasminghaṭe sthāpyaṃ savastraṃ pratimādvayam /
pañcāmṛtena saṃsrāpya jalaiḥ śuddhaistator'cayet //
1.124.d:
तत्रैकस्मिन्घटे स्थाप्यं सवस्त्रं प्रतिमाद्वयम् ।
पञ्चामृतेन संस्राप्य जलैः शुद्धैस्ततोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.124.m: The two clothed images are to be placed upon one jar there; / having bathed them with the five nectars and with pure waters, he should then worship them

1.124.s:
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhistataḥ pañcadaśa dvijān /
bhojayeccaiva miṣṭānnairdadyāttebhyaśca dakṣiṇām //
1.124.d:
उपचारैः षोडशभिस्ततः पञ्चदश द्विजान् ।
भोजयेच्चैव मिष्टान्नैर्दद्यात्तेभ्यश्च दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.124.m: With the sixteen services; then he should feed / fifteen Brāhmaṇas with sweet foods and give them priestly gifts.

1.124.s:
kuṃbhamekaikamīśasya mūrtyāḍhyaṃ guraver'payet /
evaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caiva umāmāheśvarābhidham //
1.124.d:
कुंभमेकैकमीशस्य मूर्त्याढ्यं गुरवेर्ऽपयेत् ।
एवं कृत्वा व्रतं चैव उमामाहेश्वराभिधम् ॥
1.124.m: He should offer each jar, endowed with an image of the Lord, to the guru. / Having performed this observance named Umā-Māheśvara,

1.124.s:
jāyate bhuvi vikhyāto nidhānaṃ sarvasaṃpadām /
athāsminneva divase śakravratamapi smṛtam //
1.124.d:
जायते भुवि विख्यातो निधानं सर्वसंपदाम् ।
अथास्मिन्नेव दिवसे शक्रव्रतमपि स्मृतम् ॥
1.124.m: He becomes renowned on earth, a storehouse of all prosperity. / Now, on this very day, the Śakra observance is also remembered.

1.124.s:
prātaḥ snātvā vidhānena saṃpūjya suranāyakam /
gandhādyaiṃrupacāraistu naivedyānāṃ ca rāśibhiḥ //
1.124.d:
प्रातः स्नात्वा विधानेन संपूज्य सुरनायकम् ।
गन्धाद्यैंरुपचारैस्तु नैवेद्यानां च राशिभिः ॥
1.124.m: Having bathed in the morning according to rule, and having worshipped the leader of the gods / with services such as fragrances and heaps of food offerings,

1.124.s:
tato nimantritānviprānsaṃbhojya vidhivaddvija /
samāgatāṃstathaivānyāndīnānāthāṃśca bhojayet //
1.124.d:
ततो निमन्त्रितान्विप्रान्संभोज्य विधिवद्द्विज ।
समागतांस्तथैवान्यान्दीनानाथांश्च भोजयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Then having fed the invited Brāhmaṇas according to rule, O twice-born one, / he should likewise feed others who have arrived, the poor, and the helpless.

1.124.s:
etacchakravrataṃ vipra kartavyaṃ prativārṣikam /
rājñā vā dhaninānyena dhānyaniṣpattimicchatā //
1.124.d:
एतच्छक्रव्रतं विप्र कर्तव्यं प्रतिवार्षिकम् ।
राज्ञा वा धनिनान्येन धान्यनिष्पत्तिमिच्छता ॥
1.124.m: This Śakra observance, O Brāhmaṇa, should be performed annually / by a king or another wealthy person desiring the production of grain.

1.124.s:
āśvine māsi pūrṇāyāṃ vrataṃ kojāgarābhidham /
tena snātvā vidhānena sopavāso jitendriyaḥ //
1.124.d:
आश्विने मासि पूर्णायां व्रतं कोजागराभिधम् ।
तेन स्नात्वा विधानेन सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.124.m: On the full moon day in the month of Āśvina is the observance named Kojāgara. / Having bathed according to rule, fasting and with senses subdued,

1.124.s:
lakṣmīmabhyarcya sauvarṇīṃ ghaṭe saṃsthāpya tāmraje /
mṛnmaye vā savastrāntāmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidham //
1.124.d:
लक्ष्मीमभ्यर्च्य सौवर्णीं घटे संस्थाप्य ताम्रजे ।
मृन्मये वा सवस्त्रान्तामुपचारैः पृथग्विधम् ॥
1.124.m: Having placed a golden image of Lakṣmī, adorned with garments, / upon a copper or earthen jar, having worshipped her with various services,

1.124.s:
tataḥ sāyantane kāle 'bhyudite tārakādhipe /
haimānraupyānmṛnmayānvā ghṛtapūrṇānpradīpayet //
1.124.d:
ततः सायन्तने काले ऽभ्युदिते तारकाधिपे ।
हैमान्रौप्यान्मृन्मयान्वा घृतपूर्णान्प्रदीपयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Then, in the evening when the lord of the stars has arisen, / he should light [lamps] of gold, silver, or clay, filled with clarified butter,

1.124.s:
lakṣaṃ tadardhamayutaṃ sahasraṃ śatameva vā /
ghṛtaśarkarasaṃmiśraṃ vipācya bahu pāyasam //
1.124.d:
लक्षं तदर्धमयुतं सहस्रं शतमेव वा ।
घृतशर्करसंमिश्रं विपाच्य बहु पायसम् ॥
1.124.m: A hundred thousand, half of that, ten thousand, a thousand, or even a hundred. / Having cooked abundant milk-rice mixed with clarified butter and sugar,

1.124.s:
bahupātreṣu saṃsthāpya kaumudyāṃ śītadīdhiteḥ /
yāmamātre gate rātryā lakṣmyai tadvinivedayet //
1.124.d:
बहुपात्रेषु संस्थाप्य कौमुद्यां शीतदीधितेः ।
याममात्रे गते रात्र्या लक्ष्म्यै तद्विनिवेदयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Placing it in many vessels under the moonbeams of the cold-rayed one, / when one watch of the night has passed, he should offer it to Lakṣmī.

1.124.s:
tataḥ saṃbhojayettena viprānbhaktyā tataśca taiḥ /
sahaiva jāgaraṃ kuryyānnṛtyagītasumaṅgalaiḥ //
1.124.d:
ततः संभोजयेत्तेन विप्रान्भक्त्या ततश्च तैः ।
सहैव जागरं कुर्य्यान्नृत्यगीतसुमङ्गलैः ॥
1.124.m: Then he should feed Brāhmaṇas with it with devotion; then / he should keep vigil along with them, accompanied by dancing, singing, and auspicious activities.

1.124.s:
tato 'ruṇodaye snātvā tāṃ mūrtiṃ guraver'payet /
asyāṃ rātrau mahālakṣmīrvarābhayakarāṃbujā //
1.124.d:
ततो ऽरुणोदये स्नात्वा तां मूर्तिं गुरवेर्ऽपयेत् ।
अस्यां रात्रौ महालक्ष्मीर्वराभयकरांबुजा ॥
1.124.m: Then, having bathed at dawn, he should give that image to the guru. / On this night, Mahālakṣmī, whose lotus-like hands grant boons and fearlessness,

1.124.s:
niśīthe carate loke ko jāgartiṃ dharātale /
tasmai vittaṃ prayacchāmi jāgrate pūjakāya me //
1.124.d:
निशीथे चरते लोके को जागर्तिं धरातले ।
तस्मै वित्तं प्रयच्छामि जाग्रते पूजकाय मे ॥
1.124.m: Roams through the world at midnight, [asking,] ‘Who is awake on the surface of the earth? / To him, the waking worshipper of mine, I grant wealth.’

1.124.s:
varṣe varṣe kṛtaṃ caitadvrataṃ lakṣmīpratoṣaṇam /
samṛddhimaihikīṃ dadyāddvehānte pāralaukikīm //
1.124.d:
वर्षे वर्षे कृतं चैतद्व्रतं लक्ष्मीप्रतोषणम् ।
समृद्धिमैहिकीं दद्याद्द्वेहान्ते पारलौकिकीम् ॥
1.124.m: This observance pleasing to Lakṣmī, performed year after year, / bestows worldly prosperity and other-worldly [bliss] at the end of the body.

1.124.s:
kārtikyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ tu kuryātkārtikadarśanam /
vipratvalabdhaye bhūyaḥ sarvaśatrujayāya ca //
1.124.d:
कार्तिक्यां पूर्णिमायां तु कुर्यात्कार्तिकदर्शनम् ।
विप्रत्वलब्धये भूयः सर्वशत्रुजयाय च ॥
1.124.m: On the full moon day of Kārttika, one should perform the viewing of Kārttika, / in order to attain brāhmaṇa-hood once again and to conquer all enemies.

1.124.s:
atraiva dīpadānena vidheyastripurotsavaḥ /
niśāmukhe dvijaśreṣṭha sarvajīvasukhāvahaḥ //
1.124.d:
अत्रैव दीपदानेन विधेयस्त्रिपुरोत्सवः ।
निशामुखे द्विजश्रेष्ठ सर्वजीवसुखावहः ॥
1.124.m: On this very [day], through the donation of lamps, the Tripura festival is to be celebrated / at nightfall, O best of the twice-born, bringing happiness to all living beings.

1.124.s:
kīṭāḥ pataṅgā maśakāśca vṛkṣā jale sthale ye vicaranti jīvāḥ /
dṛṣṭvā pradīpānnahi te 'pi janminaḥ punaśca muktiṃ hi labhanta eva ca //
1.124.d:
कीटाः पतङ्गा मशकाश्च वृक्षा जले स्थले ये विचरन्ति जीवाः ।
दृष्ट्वा प्रदीपान्नहि ते ऽपि जन्मिनः पुनश्च मुक्तिं हि लभन्त एव च ॥
1.124.m: Insects, moths, mosquitoes, trees, and whichever living beings roam on water or land, / having seen the lamps, those born beings never [return to rebirth] and indeed attain liberation.

1.124.s: atra candrodaye vipra saṃpūjyāḥ kṛttikāśca ṣaṭ //
1.124.d: अत्र चन्द्रोदये विप्र संपूज्याः कृत्तिकाश्च षट् ॥
1.124.m: Here, at moonrise, O Brāhmaṇa, the six Kṛttikās are to be worshipped,

1.124.s:
kārtikeyastathā khaḍgī varuṇaśca hutāśanaḥ /
gandhapuṣpaistathā dhūpadīpairnaivedyevistaraiḥ //
1.124.d:
कार्तिकेयस्तथा खड्गी वरुणश्च हुताशनः ।
गन्धपुष्पैस्तथा धूपदीपैर्नैवेद्येविस्तरैः ॥
1.124.m: As well as Kārttikeya, the sword-bearer [Khaḍgin], Varuṇa, and the fire [Hutāśana], / with fragrant flowers, incense, lamps, and abundant food offerings,

1.124.s:
paramānnaiḥ phalaiḥ śākairvahnibrāhmaṇatarpaṇaiḥ /
evaṃ devānsamabhyarcya dīpo deyo gṛhādbahiḥ //
1.124.d:
परमान्नैः फलैः शाकैर्वह्निब्राह्मणतर्पणैः ।
एवं देवान्समभ्यर्च्य दीपो देयो गृहाद्बहिः ॥
1.124.m: With fine food, fruits, herbs, and offerings to fire and Brāhmaṇas. / Having thus worshipped the gods, a lamp should be placed outside the house.

1.124.s:
dīpopānte tathā gartaścaturasro manoharaḥ /
caturddaṃśāṅgulaḥ kāryaḥ secyaścadanavāriṇā //
1.124.d:
दीपोपान्ते तथा गर्तश्चतुरस्रो मनोहरः ।
चतुर्द्दंशाङ्गुलः कार्यः सेच्यश्चदनवारिणा ॥
1.124.m: And near the lamp, a beautiful four-sided pit / of fourteen aṅgulas should be made and sprinkled with sandalwood water.

1.124.s:
gavāṃ kṣīreṇa saṃpūrya haimaṃ tatra vinikṣipet /
muktānetrasamāyuktaṃ matsyaṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanam //
1.124.d:
गवां क्षीरेण संपूर्य हैमं तत्र विनिक्षिपेत् ।
मुक्तानेत्रसमायुक्तं मत्स्यं सर्वाङ्गशोभनम् ॥
1.124.m: Having filled it with cows' milk, one should place therein a golden / fish with eyes of pearl, beautiful in all its limbs.

1.124.s:
mahāmatsyāya ca nama iti mantraṃ samuccaran /
gandhādyaistatra saṃpūjya dvijāya pratipādayet //
1.124.d:
महामत्स्याय च नम इति मन्त्रं समुच्चरन् ।
गन्धाद्यैस्तत्र संपूज्य द्विजाय प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Uttering the mantra: ‘Obeisance to the Great Fish,’ / having worshipped it there with fragrances and the like, he should present it to a Brāhmaṇa.

1.124.s:
kṣīrasāgaradānaṃ te mayoktaṃ dvijasattama /
dānasyāsya prabhāveṇa modate harisannidhau //
1.124.d:
क्षीरसागरदानं ते मयोक्तं द्विजसत्तम ।
दानस्यास्य प्रभावेण मोदते हरिसन्निधौ ॥
1.124.m: The gift of the Milk Ocean has been described to you, O best of the twice-born; / by the power of this gift, one rejoices in the presence of Hari.

1.124.s:
atra kṛttvā vṛṣotsargaṃ vrataṃ naktaṃ ca nārada /
rudralokamavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.124.d:
अत्र कृत्त्वा वृषोत्सर्गं व्रतं नक्तं च नारद ।
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.124.m: Having performed here the release of a bull and the night-fast observance, O Nārada, / he attains the world of Rudra; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.

1.124.s:
mārgaśīrṣyā pūrṇimāyāṃ svarṇāḍhyaṃ lavaṇāḍhakam /
devaṃ viprāya śāntāya sarvakāmasamṛddhaye //
1.124.d:
मार्गशीर्ष्या पूर्णिमायां स्वर्णाढ्यं लवणाढकम् ।
देवं विप्राय शान्ताय सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥
1.124.m: On the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa, an āḍhaka measure of salt endowed with gold / [is to be given] to a peaceful Brāhmaṇa for the fulfilment of all desires.

1.124.s:
idaṃ jagatpurā lakṣmyā tyaktamāsīttato hariḥ /
purandaraśca somaśca tathā tiṣyo bṛhaspatiḥ //
1.124.d:
इदं जगत्पुरा लक्ष्म्या त्यक्तमासीत्ततो हरिः ।
पुरन्दरश्च सोमश्च तथा तिष्यो बृहस्पतिः ॥
1.124.m: Long ago, this world was abandoned by Lakṣmī; then Hari, / Purandara, Soma, and also Tiṣya and Bṛhaspati—

1.124.s:
pañcaite puṣyayuktāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ jagadbalāt /
alaṅkṛtaṃ punaścakuḥ saubhāgyotsavakelibhiḥ //
1.124.d:
पञ्चैते पुष्ययुक्तायां पौर्णमास्यां जगद्बलात् ।
अलङ्कृतं पुनश्चकुः सौभाग्योत्सवकेलिभिः ॥
1.124.m: These five, on the full moon day joined with the Puṣya constellation, / adorned the world once again by force with festive sports of good fortune.

1.124.s:
tasmānnaraḥ puṣyayoge sarvasaubhāgyavṛddhaye /
gaurasarṣapakalkena samālabhya svakāṃ tanum //
1.124.d:
तस्मान्नरः पुष्ययोगे सर्वसौभाग्यवृद्धये ।
गौरसर्षपकल्केन समालभ्य स्वकां तनुम् ॥
1.124.m: Therefore, when the Puṣya conjunction occurs, a man, for the increase of all good fortune, / having smeared his body with a paste of white mustard,

1.124.s:
snāyātsarvauṃṣadhijalairdhārayecca navāṃśuke /
dṛṣṭvā ca maṅgalaṃ dravyaṃ spṛṣṭvā natvā tator'cayet //
1.124.d:
स्नायात्सर्वौंषधिजलैर्धारयेच्च नवांशुके ।
दृष्ट्वा च मङ्गलं द्रव्यं स्पृष्ट्वा नत्वा ततोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.124.m: Should bathe with waters containing all medicinal herbs and put on two new garments. / Having seen an auspicious object, touched it, and bowed, he should then worship

1.124.s:
hariśakrendupuṣyejyāngandhādyarupacārakaiḥ /
vidhāya homaṃ viprāṃśca tarpayetpāyasāśanaiḥ //
1.124.d:
हरिशक्रेन्दुपुष्येज्यान्गन्धाद्यरुपचारकैः ।
विधाय होमं विप्रांश्च तर्पयेत्पायसाशनैः ॥
1.124.m: Hari, Śakra, Indu, Puṣya, and Bṛhaspati with services such as fragrances; / having performed fire oblation, he should satisfy Brāhmaṇas with meals of milk-rice.

1.124.s:
etatkṛtvā vrataṃ vipra ramāprītivivarddhanam /
alakṣmīnāśanaṃ caiva modateha paratra ca //
1.124.d:
एतत्कृत्वा व्रतं विप्र रमाप्रीतिविवर्द्धनम् ।
अलक्ष्मीनाशनं चैव मोदतेह परत्र च ॥
1.124.m: Having performed this observance, which enhances the favour of Ramā, O Brāhmaṇa, / and destroys misfortune, he rejoices here and in the hereafter.

1.124.s:
paurṇamāsyāṃ tato mādhyāṃ tilakārpāsakaṃbalam /
ratnāni kañcukoṣṇīṣapādatrāṇāni vā dhanam //
1.124.d:
पौर्णमास्यां ततो माध्यां तिलकार्पासकंबलम् ।
रत्नानि कञ्चुकोष्णीषपादत्राणानि वा धनम् ॥
1.124.m: Then, on the full moon day of Māgha, sesame, cotton, a blanket, / gems, a tunic, a turban, footwear, or wealth—

1.124.s:
datvā pramodate svarge dānaṃ vittānusārataḥ /
yastvatra śaṅkaraṃ devaṃ pūjayedvidhipūrvakam //
1.124.d:
दत्वा प्रमोदते स्वर्गे दानं वित्तानुसारतः ।
यस्त्वत्र शङ्करं देवं पूजयेद्विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.124.m: Having given a gift according to one's wealth, he rejoices in heaven. / But whoever worships the god Śaṅkara here according to rule,

1.124.s:
so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpyaviṣṇuloke mahīyate /
phaālgune pūrṇimāyāṃ tu holikāpūjanaṃ matam //
1.124.d:
सो ऽश्वमेधफलं प्राप्यविष्णुलोके महीयते ।
फआल्गुने पूर्णिमायां तु होलिकापूजनं मतम् ॥
1.124.m: He, having obtained the fruit of a horse sacrifice, is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / On the full moon day of Phālguna, the worship of Holikā is prescribed.

1.124.s:
saṃcayaṃ sarvakāṣṭhānāmupalānāṃ ca kārayet /
tatrāgniṃ vidhivaddhrutvā rakṣoghnairmantravistaraiḥ //
1.124.d:
संचयं सर्वकाष्ठानामुपलानां च कारयेत् ।
तत्राग्निं विधिवद्ध्रुत्वा रक्षोघ्नैर्मन्त्रविस्तरैः ॥
1.124.m: One should make a heap of all kinds of wood and cow-dung cakes; / having kindled a fire there according to rule with extensive demon-slaying mantras,

1.124.s:
"asṛkpābhayasaṃtrastaiḥ kṛtā tvaṃ holi bāliśaiḥ /
atastvāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi bhūte bhūtipradā bhava" //
1.124.d:
"असृक्पाभयसंत्रस्तैः कृता त्वं होलि बालिशैः ।
अतस्त्वां पूजयिष्यामि भूते भूतिप्रदा भव" ॥
1.124.m: ‘You, O Holi, were made by children terrified by the fear of blood-drinkers; / therefore I will worship you, O spirit, be the bestower of prosperity!’

1.124.s:
iti mantreṇa sandīpya kāṣṭhādikṣepaṇaistataḥ /
parikramyotsavaḥ kāryyo gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ //
1.124.d:
इति मन्त्रेण सन्दीप्य काष्ठादिक्षेपणैस्ततः ।
परिक्रम्योत्सवः कार्य्यो गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः ॥
1.124.m: Having kindled [the fire] with this mantra, then by throwing wood and the like, / having circumambulated, a festival should be celebrated with the sounds of songs and musical instruments.

1.124.s:
holikā rākṣasī ceyaṃ prahlādabhayadāyinī /
tatastāṃ pradahṝntyevaṃ kāṣṭhādyairgītamaṅgalaiḥ //
1.124.d:
होलिका राक्षसी चेयं प्रह्लादभयदायिनी ।
ततस्तां प्रदहॄन्त्येवं काष्ठाद्यैर्गीतमङ्गलैः ॥
1.124.m: And this Holikā was an ogre who brought terror to Prahlāda; / therefore they burn her thus with wood and other fuels, amidst auspicious songs.

1.124.s:
saṃvatsarasya dāho 'yaṃ kāmadāho matāntare /
iti jānīhi viprendra loke sthitiranekadhā //
1.124.d:
संवत्सरस्य दाहो ऽयं कामदाहो मतान्तरे ।
इति जानीहि विप्रेन्द्र लोके स्थितिरनेकधा ॥
1.124.m: In another tradition, this is the burning of the year, or the burning of Kāma. / Know this, O best of Brahmins; the customs in the world are diverse.

1.124.s:
pakṣānte dve pṛthagvaive tato 'māvratamucyate /
pṛthakchṛṇuṣva me vipra pitṝṇāmativallabham //
1.124.d:
पक्षान्ते द्वे पृथग्वैवे ततो ऽमाव्रतमुच्यते ।
पृथक्छृणुष्व मे विप्र पितॄणामतिवल्लभम् ॥
1.124.m: There are indeed two separate [observances] at the ends of the fortnights. Now the vow of the new-moon day is spoken of; / listen to me separately, O Brahmin, concerning what is exceedingly dear to the ancestors.

1.124.s:
caitravaiśākhayostatra darśe pitṛsamarcanam /
pārvaṇena vidhānena śrāddhaṃ vittānusārataḥ //
1.124.d:
चैत्रवैशाखयोस्तत्र दर्शे पितृसमर्चनम् ।
पार्वणेन विधानेन श्राद्धं वित्तानुसारतः ॥
1.124.m: On the new moon of Caitra and Vaiśākha, the worship of the ancestors is to be performed, / [namely,] the ancestral rite according to the pārvaṇa procedure, in keeping with one's wealth.

1.124.s:
dvijānāṃ bhojanaṃ dānaṃ gavādīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
sarvamāseṣvamāyāṃ vai bahupuṇyapradaṃ yataḥ //
1.124.d:
द्विजानां भोजनं दानं गवादीनां विशेषतः ।
सर्वमासेष्वमायां वै बहुपुण्यप्रदं यतः ॥
1.124.m: Feeding Brahmins and giving gifts, especially of cows and other offerings, / on the new-moon day in all months, indeed bestows great merit.

1.124.s:
jyeṣṭhāmāyāṃ vrataṃ proktaṃ sāvitryāḥ kasya nārada /
vidhānaṃ jyeṣṭhapūrṇāvadihāpi parikīrtitam //
1.124.d:
ज्येष्ठामायां व्रतं प्रोक्तं सावित्र्याः कस्य नारद ।
विधानं ज्येष्ठपूर्णावदिहापि परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.124.m: On the new moon of Jyeṣṭha, the vow of Sāvitrī is prescribed, O Nārada; / its procedure has been proclaimed to be just like that of the full moon of Jyeṣṭha here as well.

1.124.s:
śucau nabhasi bhādre ca māse pūrṇāntike dvija /
pitṛśrāddhaṃ dānahomasurārcānantyaśnute //
1.124.d:
शुचौ नभसि भाद्रे च मासे पूर्णान्तिके द्विज ।
पितृश्राद्धं दानहोमसुरार्चानन्त्यश्नुते ॥
1.124.m: In the months of Śuci, Nabhas, and Bhādra, near the full-moon day, O twice-born, / an ancestral rite, giving of gifts, fire oblation, and worship of the gods obtain infinity.

1.124.s:
bhādradarśe 'parāhne tu tilakṣetrasamudbhavān /
viriñcimanunāmantrya huṃphaṭ chinnānkuśān dvija //
1.124.d:
भाद्रदर्शे ऽपराह्ने तु तिलक्षेत्रसमुद्भवान् ।
विरिञ्चिमनुनामन्त्र्य हुंफट् छिन्नान्कुशान् द्विज ॥
1.124.m: On the new moon of Bhādra, in the afternoon, having consecrated [kuśa grasses] grown in sesame fields / with the Viriñci mantra, with 'huṃ phaṭ', cut the kuśa grasses, O Brahmin.

1.124.s:
sarvadā sarvakāryeṣu yojayedekadāparān /
iṣāmāyāṃ viśeṣaṇa pitṝṇāṃ śrāddhatarpaṇam //
1.124.d:
सर्वदा सर्वकार्येषु योजयेदेकदापरान् ।
इषामायां विशेषण पितॄणां श्राद्धतर्पणम् ॥
1.124.m: One should always employ them in all rites, and on another occasion [gather] others. / On the new moon of Iṣa, the ancestral rite and water oblation for the ancestors are especially [prescribed],

1.124.s:
vidheyaṃ jāhnavītoye muktidaṃ ca gayāsthale /
ūrjjāmāyāṃ dīpadānaṃ devā gāragṛheṣu ca //
1.124.d:
विधेयं जाह्नवीतोये मुक्तिदं च गयास्थले ।
ऊर्ज्जामायां दीपदानं देवा गारगृहेषु च ॥
1.124.m: to be performed in the water of the Jāhnavī; and in the place of Gayā it grants liberation. / On the new moon of Ūrja, the offering of lamps in temples and homes,

1.124.s:
nadyārāmataḍāgeṣu caityagoṣṭhāpaṇeṣu ca /
samarcanaṃ tathā lakṣmyāḥ svarṇaraupye kṛtākṛte //
1.124.d:
नद्यारामतडागेषु चैत्यगोष्ठापणेषु च ।
समर्चनं तथा लक्ष्म्याः स्वर्णरौप्ये कृताकृते ॥
1.124.m: at rivers, gardens, and ponds, and at monuments, cowpens, and market-stalls, / as well as the worship of Lakṣmī in gold and silver, whether fashioned or unformed,

1.124.s:
dyūtaṃ ca varṣaphaladaṃ jaye cāpiparājaye /
gavāṃ pūjātra vihitā śṛṅgādyaṅgānurañjanaiḥ //
1.124.d:
द्यूतं च वर्षफलदं जये चापिपराजये ।
गवां पूजात्र विहिता शृङ्गाद्यङ्गानुरञ्जनैः ॥
1.124.m: and gambling, which yields the fruit of the whole year in victory and even in defeat, [should be performed]. / Here the worship of cows is enjoined, by ornamenting their horns and other limbs,

1.124.s:
yavasānnādidānaiśca namaskārapradakṣiṇaiḥ /
mārge 'pi pitṛpūjā syācchraddhairbrāhmaṇabhojanaiḥ //
1.124.d:
यवसान्नादिदानैश्च नमस्कारप्रदक्षिणैः ।
मार्गे ऽपि पितृपूजा स्याच्छ्रद्धैर्ब्राह्मणभोजनैः ॥
1.124.m: by gifts of grass, food, and the like, and by reverent salutations and circumambulations. / In Mārgaśīrṣa also, there should be ancestral worship through faithful offerings and feeding of Brahmins.

1.124.s:
brahmacaryādi niyamairjapahomārcanādibhiḥ /
pauṣe māghe ca viprendra pitṛśrāddhaṃ phalādhikam //
1.124.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यादि नियमैर्जपहोमार्चनादिभिः ।
पौषे माघे च विप्रेन्द्र पितृश्राद्धं फलाधिकम् ॥
1.124.m: With the vows of celibacy and the like, with recitation, fire oblation, and worship, / the ancestral rite in Pauṣa and Māgha, O best of Brahmins, bears greater fruit.

1.124.s:
amāyāṃ karṇapātārkayuktāyāṃ tu gayādhikam /
phaālgune kevalaṃ śrāddhaṃ dvijānāṃ bhojanaṃ tathā //
1.124.d:
अमायां कर्णपातार्कयुक्तायां तु गयाधिकम् ।
फआल्गुने केवलं श्राद्धं द्विजानां भोजनं तथा ॥
1.124.m: When the new moon is conjoined with Karṇapāta and the Sun, [the fruit is] greater than at Gayā. / In Phālguna, an ancestral rite alone, as well as the feeding of Brahmins,

1.124.s:
dānādi sarvaphaladaṃ darśe some 'dhikaṃ phalam /
itthaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ tithikṛtyaṃ mune tava //
1.124.d:
दानादि सर्वफलदं दर्शे सोमे ऽधिकं फलम् ।
इत्थं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं तिथिकृत्यं मुने तव ॥
1.124.m: and giving gifts yield all fruits; on a Monday new moon, the fruit is even greater. / Thus, O sage, the duty of lunar days has been briefly spoken to you;

1.124.s:
sarvatrāpi viśeṣo 'sti sa purāṇāntare sthitaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde dvādaśamāsasthitapaurṇamāsya māvāsyāvratakathanaṃ nāma caturviṃśatyadhikaśatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.124.d:
सर्वत्रापि विशेषो ऽस्ति स पुराणान्तरे स्थितः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे द्वादशमासस्थितपौर्णमास्य मावास्याव्रतकथनं नाम चतुर्विंशत्यधिकशतमो ऽध्यायः
1.124.m:
there are particular details everywhere, which are recorded in other Purāṇas.

Thus ends the one hundred twenty-fourth chapter in the Fourth Quarter of the Great Narrative in the First Part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, entitled 'The Description of the Vows of the Full-Moon and New-Moon Days in the Twelve Months'.

1.125.s:
sūta uvāca
ityevamuktvā muninā hi pṛṣṭāste vai kumārāḥ kila nāradena /
saṃpūjitāḥ śāstravidāṃ variṣṭhāḥ kṛtāhnikā jagmurumeśalokam //
1.125.d:
सूत उवाच
इत्येवमुक्त्वा मुनिना हि पृष्टास्ते वै कुमाराः किल नारदेन ।
संपूजिताः शास्त्रविदां वरिष्ठाः कृताह्निका जग्मुरुमेशलोकम् ॥
1.125.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus when questioned by the sage, those Kumāras, / worshipped by Nārada, the foremost among knowers of the scriptures, having completed their daily rites, went to the world of the Lord of Umā.

1.125.s:
tatreśamagryarkanibhairmunīndraiḥ śrīvāmadevādibhirarcitāṅghrim /
surāsurendrairabhivandyamugraṃ natvājñayā tasya niṣedururvyām //
1.125.d:
तत्रेशमग्र्यर्कनिभैर्मुनीन्द्रैः श्रीवामदेवादिभिरर्चिताङ्घ्रिम् ।
सुरासुरेन्द्रैरभिवन्द्यमुग्रं नत्वाज्ञया तस्य निषेदुरुर्व्याम् ॥
1.125.m: There, having bowed to the Lord, fierce and worthy of praise by the chiefs of gods and demons, whose feet were worshipped by eminent sages resembling the foremost sun, such as the venerable Vāmadeva, / they sat upon the ground at his command.

1.125.s:
śrutvātha tatrākhilaśāstrasāraṃ śivāgamaṃ te paśupāśamokṣaṇam /
jagmustato jñānaghanasvarūpā natvā purāriṃ svapiturnikāśam //
1.125.d:
श्रुत्वाथ तत्राखिलशास्त्रसारं शिवागमं ते पशुपाशमोक्षणम् ।
जग्मुस्ततो ज्ञानघनस्वरूपा नत्वा पुरारिं स्वपितुर्निकाशम् ॥
1.125.m: Having heard there the Śiva-āgama, the essence of all scriptures, which brings release from the bonds of the individual soul, / they, whose essence was concentrated knowledge, having bowed to the Enemy of Pura, went into the presence of their father.

1.125.s:
tatpādapadme praṇatiṃ vidhāya pitrāpi satkṛtya sabhājitāste /
labdhvāśiṣo 'dyāpi caranti śaśvallokeṣu tīrthāni ca tīrthabhūtāḥ //
1.125.d:
तत्पादपद्मे प्रणतिं विधाय पित्रापि सत्कृत्य सभाजितास्ते ।
लब्ध्वाशिषो ऽद्यापि चरन्ति शश्वल्लोकेषु तीर्थानि च तीर्थभूताः ॥
1.125.m: Having made prostration at his lotus feet, honored and welcomed by their father, / having received his blessings, they, having become sacred fords themselves, constantly roam the sacred fords in the worlds even today.

1.125.s:
jagmustato vai badarīvanānte surendravargairupasevyamānam /
dadhyuściraṃ viṣṇupadābjamavyayaṃ dhyāyanti yadyatayo vītarāgāḥ //
1.125.d:
जग्मुस्ततो वै बदरीवनान्ते सुरेन्द्रवर्गैरुपसेव्यमानम् ।
दध्युश्चिरं विष्णुपदाब्जमव्ययं ध्यायन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः ॥
1.125.m: Then they went to the edge of the Badarī forest, attended by groups of the lords of gods, / and meditated for a long time upon the imperishable lotus feet of Viṣṇu, on which ascetics free from passion meditate.

1.125.s:
nārado 'pi tato viprā kumārebhyaḥ samīhitam /
labdhvā jñānaṃ savijñānaṃ bhṛśaṃ prītamanā hyabhūt //
1.125.d:
नारदो ऽपि ततो विप्रा कुमारेभ्यः समीहितम् ।
लब्ध्वा ज्ञानं सविज्ञानं भृशं प्रीतमना ह्यभूत् ॥
1.125.m: Nārada too, O Brahmins, having obtained from the Kumāras the desired / knowledge together with direct realization, became exceedingly pleased in mind.

1.125.s:
sa tasmātsvarṇadītīrādāgatya piturantike /
praṇamya satkṛtaḥ pitrā brahmaṇā niṣasāda ca //
1.125.d:
स तस्मात्स्वर्णदीतीरादागत्य पितुरन्तिके ।
प्रणम्य सत्कृतः पित्रा ब्रह्मणा निषसाद च ॥
1.125.m: He, having come from the bank of that golden river into the presence of his father / and bowed, was honored by his father Brahmā and sat down.

1.125.s:
kumārebhyaḥ śrutaṃ yacca jñānaṃ vijñānasaṃyutam /
varṇayāmāsa tattvena so 'pi śrutvā mumoda ca //
1.125.d:
कुमारेभ्यः श्रुतं यच्च ज्ञानं विज्ञानसंयुतम् ।
वर्णयामास तत्त्वेन सो ऽपि श्रुत्वा मुमोद च ॥
1.125.m: And the knowledge accompanied by direct realization which he had heard from the Kumāras / he described in truth; and he, having heard it, also rejoiced.

1.125.s:
atha praṇamya śirasā labdhāśīrmunisattamaḥ /
ājagāma ca kailāsaṃ munisiddhaniṣevitam //
1.125.d:
अथ प्रणम्य शिरसा लब्धाशीर्मुनिसत्तमः ।
आजगाम च कैलासं मुनिसिद्धनिषेवितम् ॥
1.125.m: Then, having bowed with his head and received his blessing, that best of sages / went to Kailāsa, frequented by sages and Siddhas,

1.125.s:
nānāścaryamayaṃ śaśvatsarvarttukusumadrumaiḥ /
mandāraiḥ pārijātaiśca caṃpakāśokavañjulaiḥ //
1.125.d:
नानाश्चर्यमयं शश्वत्सर्वर्त्तुकुसुमद्रुमैः ।
मन्दारैः पारिजातैश्च चंपकाशोकवञ्जुलैः ॥
1.125.m: filled with various wonders, constantly [adorned] with trees blooming in all seasons, / with mandāra, pārijāta, campaka, aśoka, and vañjula trees,

1.125.s:
anyaiśca vividhairvṛkṣairnānāpakṣigaṇāvṛtaiḥ /
vātoddhūtaśikhaiḥ pānthānāhvayadbhirivāvṛtam //
1.125.d:
अन्यैश्च विविधैर्वृक्षैर्नानापक्षिगणावृतैः ।
वातोद्धूतशिखैः पान्थानाह्वयद्भिरिवावृतम् ॥
1.125.m: and with other various trees surrounded by flocks of diverse birds, / as if calling travelers with their crowns shaken by the wind,

1.125.s:
nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ siddhakinnarasaṃkulam /
sarobhiḥ svacchasalilairlasatkāñcanapaṅkajaiḥ //
1.125.d:
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं सिद्धकिन्नरसंकुलम् ।
सरोभिः स्वच्छसलिलैर्लसत्काञ्चनपङ्कजैः ॥
1.125.m: crowded with various herds of deer, filled with Siddhas and Kinnaras, / with lakes of clear water and shining golden lotuses,

1.125.s:
śobhitaṃ sārasairhaṃsaiścakrāhvādyairnināditam /
svarddhanīpātanir ghṛṣṭaṃ krīḍadbhiścāpsarogaṇaiḥ //
1.125.d:
शोभितं सारसैर्हंसैश्चक्राह्वाद्यैर्निनादितम् ।
स्वर्द्धनीपातनिर् घृष्टं क्रीडद्भिश्चाप्सरोगणैः ॥
1.125.m: graced and made resonant by cranes, swans, and cakravāka birds, / washed by the descent of the heavenly river, with troops of Apsarases sporting

1.125.s:
salile 'lakanandāyāḥ kucakuṅkumapiṅgale /
āmodamuditairnāgaiḥ salilaiḥ puṣkaroddhṛtaiḥ //
1.125.d:
सलिले ऽलकनन्दायाः कुचकुङ्कुमपिङ्गले ।
आमोदमुदितैर्नागैः सलिलैः पुष्करोद्धृतैः ॥
1.125.m: in the water of the Alakanandā, reddish-yellow with the saffron from their breasts, / crowded with elephants delighted by the fragrance, bathing female elephants

1.125.s:
snāpayadbhiḥ kareṇūśca kalabhāṃśca samākule /
atha śvetābhrasadṛśe śṛṅge tasya ca bhūbhṛtaḥ //
1.125.d:
स्नापयद्भिः करेणूश्च कलभांश्च समाकुले ।
अथ श्वेताभ्रसदृशे शृङ्गे तस्य च भूभृतः ॥
1.125.m: and young calves with water drawn up in their trunks. / Then, upon a peak of that mountain that resembled a white cloud,

1.125.s:
vaṭaṃ kālābhrasadṛśaṃ dadarśa śatayojanam /
tasyādhastātsamāsīnaṃ yogimaṇḍalamadhyagam //
1.125.d:
वटं कालाभ्रसदृशं ददर्श शतयोजनम् ।
तस्याधस्तात्समासीनं योगिमण्डलमध्यगम् ॥
1.125.m: he saw a banyan tree resembling a dark raincloud, a hundred yojanas [in extent]; / and seated beneath it in the midst of a circle of yogins,

1.125.s:
kapardinaṃ virūpākṣa vyāghracarmāṃbarāvṛtam /
bhūtibhūṣitasarvāṅgaṃ nāgabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam //
1.125.d:
कपर्दिनं विरूपाक्ष व्याघ्रचर्मांबरावृतम् ।
भूतिभूषितसर्वाङ्गं नागभूषणभूषितम् ॥
1.125.m: the one with matted hair, odd-eyed, clothed in a tiger-skin garment, / all his limbs adorned with sacred ash, ornamented with serpents as ornaments,

1.125.s:
rudrākṣamālayā śaśvacchobhitaṃ candraśekharam /
taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārado viprā bhaktinamrātmakandharaḥ //
1.125.d:
रुद्राक्षमालया शश्वच्छोभितं चन्द्रशेखरम् ।
तं दृष्ट्वा नारदो विप्रा भक्तिनम्रात्मकन्धरः ॥
1.125.m: constantly adorned with a garland of rudrākṣa beads, bearing the crescent moon upon his crest. / Seeing him, O Brahmins, Nārada, his neck bowed low with devotion,

1.125.s:
nanām śirasā tasya pādayorjagadīśituḥ /
tataḥ prasannamanasā stutvā vāgbhirvṛṣadhvajam //
1.125.d:
ननाम् शिरसा तस्य पादयोर्जगदीशितुः ।
ततः प्रसन्नमनसा स्तुत्वा वाग्भिर्वृषध्वजम् ॥
1.125.m: bowed with his head at the two feet of that Lord of the universe. / Then, with a delighted mind, having praised the Bull-bannered Lord with words,

1.125.s:
niṣasādājñayā sthāṇoḥ satkṛto yogibhistadā /
athāpṛcchacca kuśalaṃ nāradaṃ jagatāṃ guruḥ //
1.125.d:
निषसादाज्ञया स्थाणोः सत्कृतो योगिभिस्तदा ।
अथापृच्छच्च कुशलं नारदं जगतां गुरुः ॥
1.125.m: he sat down by the command of Sthāṇu, honored by the yogins at that time. / Then the Teacher of the worlds inquired after the welfare of Nārada;

1.125.s:
sa ca prāha prasādena bhavataḥ sarvamasti me /
sarveṣāṃ yogivaryāṇāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tatra vāḍavāḥ //
1.125.d:
स च प्राह प्रसादेन भवतः सर्वमस्ति मे ।
सर्वेषां योगिवर्याणां शृण्वतां तत्र वाडवाः ॥
1.125.m: and he replied, 'By your grace, all is well with me.' / While all the foremost yogins were listening there, O Brahmins,

1.125.s:
papraccha śāṃbhivaṃ jñānaṃ paśupāśavimokṣaṇam /
sa śivaḥ sādaraṃ tasya bhaktyā saṃtuṣṭamānasaḥ //
1.125.d:
पप्रच्छ शांभिवं ज्ञानं पशुपाशविमोक्षणम् ।
स शिवः सादरं तस्य भक्त्या संतुष्टमानसः ॥
1.125.m: he inquired about the Śāmbhava knowledge, which brings release from the bonds of the individual soul. / That Śiva, his mind satisfied by his devotion, with affectionate regard,

1.125.s:
yogamaṣṭāṅgasaṃyuktaṃ prāha praṇatavatsalaḥ /
sa labdhvā śāṃbhavaṃ jñānaṃ śaṅkarāllokaśaṅkarāt //
1.125.d:
योगमष्टाङ्गसंयुक्तं प्राह प्रणतवत्सलः ।
स लब्ध्वा शांभवं ज्ञानं शङ्कराल्लोकशङ्करात् ॥
1.125.m: affectionate to those who bow, taught him yoga endowed with the eight limbs. / Having obtained the Śāmbhava knowledge from Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world,

1.125.s:
suprasannamanā natvā yayau nārāyaṇāntikam /
tatrāpi nārado 'bhīkṣṇaṃ gatāgataparāyaṇaḥ //
1.125.d:
सुप्रसन्नमना नत्वा ययौ नारायणान्तिकम् ।
तत्रापि नारदो ऽभीक्ष्णं गतागतपरायणः ॥
1.125.m: with an exceedingly delighted mind, having bowed, he went into the presence of Nārāyaṇa. / There also Nārada, constantly intent on going and coming,

1.125.s:
sevitaṃ yogibhiḥ siddhairnārāyaṇamatoṣayat /
etadvaḥ kīrtitaṃ viprā nāradīyaṃ mahanmayā //
1.125.d:
सेवितं योगिभिः सिद्धैर्नारायणमतोषयत् ।
एतद्वः कीर्तितं विप्रा नारदीयं महन्मया ॥
1.125.m: pleased Nārāyaṇa, who was served by yogins and Siddhas. / This great Nāradīya has been proclaimed by me to you, O Brahmins,

1.125.s:
upākhyānaṃ vedasamaṃ sarvaśāstranidarśanam /
catuṣpādasamāyuktaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ jñānavarddhanam //
1.125.d:
उपाख्यानं वेदसमं सर्वशास्त्रनिदर्शनम् ।
चतुष्पादसमायुक्तं शृण्वतां ज्ञानवर्द्धनम् ॥
1.125.m: a narrative equal to the Veda, an exposition of all scriptures, / consisting of four quarters, increasing the knowledge of those who listen.

1.125.s:
ya etatkīrtayedviprā nāradīyaṃ śivālaye /
samāje dvijamukhyānāṃ tathā keśavamandire //
1.125.d:
य एतत्कीर्तयेद्विप्रा नारदीयं शिवालये ।
समाजे द्विजमुख्यानां तथा केशवमन्दिरे ॥
1.125.m: Whoever proclaims this Nāradīya, O Brahmins, in an abode of Śiva, / in an assembly of the foremost of Brahmins, or in a temple of Keśava,

1.125.s:
mathurāyāṃ prayāge ca puruṣottamasannidhau /
setau kāñcyāṃ kuśasthalyāṃ gaṅgādvāre kuśasthale //
1.125.d:
मथुरायां प्रयागे च पुरुषोत्तमसन्निधौ ।
सेतौ काञ्च्यां कुशस्थल्यां गङ्गाद्वारे कुशस्थले ॥
1.125.m: in Mathurā, in Prayāga, or in the presence of Puruṣottama, / at the Causeway, in Kāñcī, in Kuśasthalī, at Gaṅgādvāra, or in Kuśasthala,

1.125.s:
puṣkareṣu nadītīre yatra kutrāpi bhaktimān /
sa labhetsarvaya jñānāṃ tīrthānāṃ ca phalaṃ mahat //
1.125.d:
पुष्करेषु नदीतीरे यत्र कुत्रापि भक्तिमान् ।
स लभेत्सर्वय ज्ञानां तीर्थानां च फलं महत् ॥
1.125.m: at Puṣkara, on a riverbank, or wherever a devoted person may be, / he attains the great fruit of all sacrifices and sacred fords,

1.125.s:
dānānāṃ cāpi sarveṣāṃ tapasāṃ vāpyaśeṣataḥ /
upavāsaparo vāpi haviṣyāśī jitendriyaḥ //
1.125.d:
दानानां चापि सर्वेषां तपसां वाप्यशेषतः ।
उपवासपरो वापि हविष्याशी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.125.m: and of all gifts, and of all austerities entirely, / whether intent on fasting, eating sacrificial food, with senses subdued;

1.125.s:
śrotā caiva tathā vaktā nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
śivabhaktirato vāpi śṛṇvan siddhimavāpnuyāt //
1.125.d:
श्रोता चैव तथा वक्ता नारायणपरायणः ।
शिवभक्तिरतो वापि शृण्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.125.m: both the listener and the speaker devoted to Nārāyaṇa, / or engaged in devotion to Śiva, will attain accomplishment by listening [to it].

1.125.s:
asninnaśeṣapuṇyānāṃ siddhīnāṃ ca samudbhavaḥ /
kathitaḥ sarvapāpaghnaḥ paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ sadā //
1.125.d:
अस्निन्नशेषपुण्यानां सिद्धीनां च समुद्भवः ।
कथितः सर्वपापघ्नः पठतां शृण्वतां सदा ॥
1.125.m: In this [Purāṇa] the source of all merits and accomplishments is proclaimed, / destroying all sins for those who recite and listen always.

1.125.s:
kalidoṣaharaṃ puṃsāṃ sarvasaṃpattivarddhanam /
sarveṣāmīpsitaṃ cedaṃ sarvajñānaprakāśakam //
1.125.d:
कलिदोषहरं पुंसां सर्वसंपत्तिवर्द्धनम् ।
सर्वेषामीप्सितं चेदं सर्वज्ञानप्रकाशकम् ॥
1.125.m: It removes the faults of the Kali age for men, increases all prosperity, / fulfills the desires of all, and illuminates all knowledge,

1.125.s:
śaivānāṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca śāktānāṃ sūyasevinām /
tathaiva gāṇapatyānāṃ varṇāśramavatāṃ dvijāḥ //
1.125.d:
शैवानां वैष्णवानां च शाक्तानां सूयसेविनाम् ।
तथैव गाणपत्यानां वर्णाश्रमवतां द्विजाः ॥
1.125.m: for Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, Śāktas, and worshippers of the Sun, / as well as for Gāṇapatyas, and for those observing caste and stage of life, O twice-born,

1.125.s:
tapasāṃ ca vratānāṃ ca phalānāṃ saṃprakāśakam /
mantrāṇāṃ caiva yantrāṇāṃ vedāṅgānāṃ vibhāgaśaḥ //
1.125.d:
तपसां च व्रतानां च फलानां संप्रकाशकम् ।
मन्त्राणां चैव यन्त्राणां वेदाङ्गानां विभागशः ॥
1.125.m: revealing the fruits of austerities and vows, / and of mantras, yantras, and the limbs of the Veda in detail,

1.125.s:
tathāgamānāṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ vedānāṃ caiva saṃgraham /
ya etatpaṭhate bhaktyā śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ //
1.125.d:
तथागमानां सांख्यानां वेदानां चैव संग्रहम् ।
य एतत्पठते भक्त्या शृणुयाद्वा समाहितः ॥
1.125.m: as well as a compendium of Āgamas, Sāṃkhya, and the Vedas. / Whoever recites this with devotion, or listens with a concentrated mind,

1.125.s:
sa labhedvāñchitānkāmāndevādiṣvapi durlabhān /
śrutvedaṃ nāradīyaṃ tu purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam //
1.125.d:
स लभेद्वाञ्छितान्कामान्देवादिष्वपि दुर्लभान् ।
श्रुत्वेदं नारदीयं तु पुराणं वेदसंमितम् ॥
1.125.m: attains desired wishes difficult to obtain even among the gods and others. / Having heard this Nāradīya Purāṇa, equal to the Veda,

1.125.s:
vācakaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā dhanaratnāṃśukādibhiḥ /
bhūmidānairgavāṃ dānai ratnadānaiśca saṃtatam //
1.125.d:
वाचकं पूजयेद्भक्त्या धनरत्नांशुकादिभिः ।
भूमिदानैर्गवां दानै रत्नदानैश्च संततम् ॥
1.125.m: one should worship the reciter with devotion, offering wealth, jewels, garments, and the like, / with gifts of land, gifts of cows, and gifts of gems continuously,

1.125.s:
hastyaśvarathadānaiśca prīṇayetsatataṃ gurum /
yastu vyākurute viprāḥ purāṇaṃ dharmasaṃgraham //
1.125.d:
हस्त्यश्वरथदानैश्च प्रीणयेत्सततं गुरुम् ।
यस्तु व्याकुरुते विप्राः पुराणं धर्मसंग्रहम् ॥
1.125.m: and should constantly please the guru with gifts of elephants, horses, and chariots. / For the one who expounds this Purāṇa, a compendium of dharma, O twice-born,

1.125.s:
caturvargapradaṃ nṝṇāṃ ko 'nyastatsadṛśo guruḥ /
kāyena manasā vācā dhanādyairapi saṃtatam //
1.125.d:
चतुर्वर्गप्रदं नॄणां को ऽन्यस्तत्सदृशो गुरुः ।
कायेन मनसा वाचा धनाद्यैरपि संततम् ॥
1.125.m: bestowing the four goals of life upon men—what other guru is equal to him? / In body, mind, speech, and constantly through wealth and other means,

1.125.s:
priyaṃ samācarettasya gurorddharmopadeśinaḥ /
śrutvā purāṇaṃ vidhivaddhomaṃ kṛtvā surārcanam //
1.125.d:
प्रियं समाचरेत्तस्य गुरोर्द्धर्मोपदेशिनः ।
श्रुत्वा पुराणं विधिवद्धोमं कृत्वा सुरार्चनम् ॥
1.125.m: one should do what is pleasing to that guru who teaches dharma. / Having listened to the Purāṇa according to rule, performed fire oblations, and worshipped the deities,

1.125.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścācchataṃ miṣṭānnapāyasaiḥ /
dakṣiṇāṃ pradadecchaktyā bhaktyā prīyeta mādhavaḥ //
1.125.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्पश्चाच्छतं मिष्टान्नपायसैः ।
दक्षिणां प्रददेच्छक्त्या भक्त्या प्रीयेत माधवः ॥
1.125.m: one should then feed a hundred Brahmins with sweet foods and milk-rice pudding; / one should give a sacrificial fee according to one's ability; Mādhava is pleased by devotion.

1.125.s:
yathā śreṣṭhā nadī gaṅgā puṣkaraṃ ca saro yathā /
kāśī purī nago merurdevo nārāyaṇo hariḥ //
1.125.d:
यथा श्रेष्ठा नदी गङ्गा पुष्करं च सरो यथा ।
काशी पुरी नगो मेरुर्देवो नारायणो हरिः ॥
1.125.m: Just as the Gaṅgā is the foremost river, and Puṣkara is [the foremost] lake, / Kāśī the [foremost] city, Meru the mountain, and God Nārāyaṇa Hari [the foremost deity],

1.125.s:
kṛtaṃ yugaṃ sāmavedo dhenurvipro 'nnamaṃbu ca /
mārgo mṛgendraḥ puruṣo 'śvatthaḥ prahlāda ānanam //
1.125.d:
कृतं युगं सामवेदो धेनुर्विप्रो ऽन्नमंबु च ।
मार्गो मृगेन्द्रः पुरुषो ऽश्वत्थः प्रह्लाद आननम् ॥
1.125.m: the Kṛta age, the Sāmaveda, the cow, the Brahmin, food, and water, / the path, the lion, the Puruṣa, the aśvattha tree, Prahlāda, the mouth,

1.125.s:
uccaiḥ śravā vasaṃtaśca japaḥ śeṣor'yamā dhanuḥ /
pāvako viṣṇurindraśca kapilo vākpatiḥ kaviḥ //
1.125.d:
उच्चैः श्रवा वसंतश्च जपः शेषोर्ऽयमा धनुः ।
पावको विष्णुरिन्द्रश्च कपिलो वाक्पतिः कविः ॥
1.125.m: Uccaiḥśravas, spring, recitation, Śeṣa, Aryaman, the bow, / fire, Viṣṇu, Indra, Kapila, the Lord of Speech [Bṛhaspati], the poet [Śukra],

1.125.s:
arjuno hanumāndarbhaścittaṃ citrarathoṃ'bujam /
urvaśī kāñcanaṃ yadvacchreṣṭāścaite svajātiṣu //
1.125.d:
अर्जुनो हनुमान्दर्भश्चित्तं चित्ररथोंऽबुजम् ।
उर्वशी काञ्चनं यद्वच्छ्रेष्टाश्चैते स्वजातिषु ॥
1.125.m: Arjuna, Hanumān, darbha grass, the mind, Citraratha, the lotus, / Urvaśī, and gold—just as these are foremost among their own kind,

1.125.s:
tathaiva nāradīyaṃ tu purāṇeṣu prakīrtitam /
śāntirastu śivaṃ cāstu sarveṣāṃ vo dvijottamāḥ //
1.125.d:
तथैव नारदीयं तु पुराणेषु प्रकीर्तितम् ।
शान्तिरस्तु शिवं चास्तु सर्वेषां वो द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.125.m: so indeed is the Nāradīya proclaimed among the Purāṇas. / May there be peace, and may there be auspiciousness for all of you, O best of the twice-born!

1.125.s:
gamiṣyāmi guroḥ pārṃśvaṃ vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ /
ityuktvābhyarcitaḥ sūtaḥ śaunakādyairmahātmabhiḥ //
1.125.d:
गमिष्यामि गुरोः पार्ंश्वं व्यासस्यामिततेजसः ।
इत्युक्त्वाभ्यर्चितः सूतः शौनकाद्यैर्महात्मभिः ॥
1.125.m: I shall go to the presence of my guru, Vyāsa of immeasurable splendor.” / Having spoken thus, Sūta was worshipped by the great-souled Śaunaka and the others,

1.125.s:
ājñaptaśca punaḥ sarvairdarśanārthaṃ guroryayau /
te 'pi sarve dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ śaunakādyāḥ samāhitāḥ /
śrutaṃ samyaganuṣṭhāya tatra tasthuśca satriṇaḥ //
1.125.d:
आज्ञप्तश्च पुनः सर्वैर्दर्शनार्थं गुरोर्ययौ ।
ते ऽपि सर्वे द्विजश्रेष्ठाः शौनकाद्याः समाहिताः ।
श्रुतं सम्यगनुष्ठाय तत्र तस्थुश्च सत्रिणः ॥
1.125.m: and, permitted by all, he departed to see his guru. / And all those best twice-born, Śaunaka and the others, composed in mind, / having practiced well what was heard, remained there performing their sacrifice.

1.125.s:
kalikalmaṣaviṣanāśanaṃ hariṃ yo japapūjanavidhibheṣajopasevī /
sa tu nirviṣamanasā sametya yāgaṃ labhate satamabhīpsitaṃ hi lokam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe bṛhadupākhyāne caturthapāde purāṇamahimāvarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samāptoyaṃ bṛhannāradīyapurāṇasya pūrvabhāgaḥ
śrīrādhāmadanamohano jayati tarām
uttarabhāgaḥ
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ
śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ
1.125.d:
कलिकल्मषविषनाशनं हरिं यो जपपूजनविधिभेषजोपसेवी ।
स तु निर्विषमनसा समेत्य यागं लभते सतमभीप्सितं हि लोकम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे बृहदुपाख्याने चतुर्थपादे पुराणमहिमावर्णनं नाम पञ्चविंशोत्तरशततमो ऽध्यायः
समाप्तोयं बृहन्नारदीयपुराणस्य पूर्वभागः
श्रीराधामदनमोहनो जयति तराम्
उत्तरभागः
श्रीगणेशाय नमः
श्रीकृष्णाय नमः
1.125.m:
He who, using the remedy of the rules of recitation and worship, attends upon Hari, the destroyer of the poison that is the impurity of the Kali age, / having reached that sacrifice with a mind free of poison, indeed attains the world desired by the virtuous.

Thus ends the hundred and twenty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Greatness of the Purāṇa,' in the fourth quarter in the great narrative of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

Here ends the first part of the Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

Glorious Rādhā-Madanamohana is supremely victorious.

2.1.s:
pāntu vo jaladaśyāmāḥ śārṅgajyāghātakarkaśāḥ /
trailokyamaṇḍapastaṃbhāścatvāro haribāhavaḥ //
2.1.d:
पान्तु वो जलदश्यामाः शार्ङ्गज्याघातकर्कशाः ।
त्रैलोक्यमण्डपस्तंभाश्चत्वारो हरिबाहवः ॥
2.1.m: Dark as rain clouds, calloused by the striking of the bowstring of Śārṅga, / the four pillars of the pavilion of the three worlds—may the arms of Hari protect you!

2.1.s:
surada suraśiroratnanighṛṣṭamaṇirañjitam /
haripādāṃbujadvandvamabhīṣṭaptadamastu naḥ //
2.1.d:
सुरद सुरशिरोरत्ननिघृष्टमणिरञ्जितम् ।
हरिपादांबुजद्वन्द्वमभीष्टप्तदमस्तु नः ॥
2.1.m: Colored by gems rubbed against the crest-jewels of gods and demons, / may the pair of lotus-feet of Hari grant our desires!

2.1.s:
māndhātovāca
pāpendhanasya ghorasya śuṣkārdrasya dvijottama /
kovahnirdahate tasya tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
2.1.d:
मान्धातोवाच
पापेन्धनस्य घोरस्य शुष्कार्द्रस्य द्विजोत्तम ।
कोवह्निर्दहते तस्य तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
2.1.m: Māndhātṛ said: / For the dreadful firewood of sin, dry and wet, O best of the twice-born, / what fire burns it? You ought to tell that.

2.1.s:
nājñātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu caturmukhasamudbhava /
vidyate tava viprendra trividhasya suniścitam //
2.1.d:
नाज्ञातं त्रिषु लोकेषु चतुर्मुखसमुद्भव ।
