विद्यते तव विप्रेन्द्र त्रिविधस्य सुनिश्चितम् ॥
2.1.m: Nothing in the three worlds is unknown to you, O son of the four-faced [Brahmā], / of threefold nature, O best of the twice-born, that is certain.

2.1.s:
ajñātaṃ pātakaṃ śuṣkaṃ jñātaṃ cārdramudāhṛtam /
bhāvyaṃ vāpyathavātītaṃ vartamāna vadasva naḥ //
2.1.d:
अज्ञातं पातकं शुष्कं ज्ञातं चार्द्रमुदाहृतम् ।
भाव्यं वाप्यथवातीतं वर्तमान वदस्व नः ॥
2.1.m: Sin committed unknowingly is called dry, and that committed knowingly is called wet, / whether future, past, or present—tell us,

2.1.s:
vahnino kena tadbhasma bhavedetanmataṃ mama /
vasiṣṭaṃ uvāca
śrūyatāṃ nṛpaśārdūla vahninā yena tadbhavet //
2.1.d:
वह्निनो केन तद्भस्म भवेदेतन्मतं मम ।
वसिष्टं उवाच
श्रूयतां नृपशार्दूल वह्निना येन तद्भवेत् ॥
2.1.m: by what fire would that be turned to ash? This is my question. / Vasiṣṭha said: / Hear, O tiger among kings, by what fire that happens:

2.1.s: bhasma śuṣkaṃ tathārdraṃ ca pāpamasya hyeśeṣataḥ //
2.1.d: भस्म शुष्कं तथार्द्रं च पापमस्य ह्येशेषतः ॥
2.1.m: the sin, both dry and wet, of this [man] completely becomes ash.

2.1.s:
avāpya vāsaraṃ viṣṇoryo naraḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ /
upavāsaparo bhūtvā pūjayenmadhusūdanam //
2.1.d:
अवाप्य वासरं विष्णोर्यो नरः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
उपवासपरो भूत्वा पूजयेन्मधुसूदनम् ॥
2.1.m: Having reached the day of Viṣṇu, whatever man, with restrained senses, / intent on fasting, should worship Madhusūdana,

2.1.s:
sa dhātrīsnānasahito rātrau jāgaraṇānvitaḥ /
viśodhayati pāpāni kitavo hi yathā dhanam //
2.1.d:
स धात्रीस्नानसहितो रात्रौ जागरणान्वितः ।
विशोधयति पापानि कितवो हि यथा धनम् ॥
2.1.m: he, taking a bath with myrobalan and keeping vigil at night, / cleanses sins away, just as a gambler clears his wealth.

2.1.s:
ekadāśīsamākhyena vahninā pātakendhanam /
bhasmatāṃ yāti rājendra api janmaśatodbhavam //
2.1.d:
एकदाशीसमाख्येन वह्निना पातकेन्धनम् ।
भस्मतां याति राजेन्द्र अपि जन्मशतोद्भवम् ॥
2.1.m: By the fire known as Ekādaśī, the firewood of sins / goes to ashes, O king of kings, even if arisen across a hundred births.

2.1.s:
nedṛśa pāvanaṃ kiñcinnārāṇāṃ bhūpa vidyate /
yādṛśaṃ padmanābhasya dinaṃ pātakahānidam //
2.1.d:
नेदृश पावनं किञ्चिन्नाराणां भूप विद्यते ।
यादृशं पद्मनाभस्य दिनं पातकहानिदम् ॥
2.1.m: There exists no such purifier for men, O king, / as the day of Padmanābha, which destroys sin.

2.1.s:
tāvatpāpāni dehe 'smiṃstiṣṭhanti manujādhipa /
yāvannopavasejjantuḥ padmanābhadimaṃ śubham //
2.1.d:
तावत्पापानि देहे ऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठन्ति मनुजाधिप ।
यावन्नोपवसेज्जन्तुः पद्मनाभदिमं शुभम् ॥
2.1.m: Sins remain in this body only so long, O ruler of men, / as a creature does not fast on the auspicious day of Padmanābha.

2.1.s:
aśvamedhasahasrāṇi rājasūyaśatāni ca /
ekādaśyupavāsasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
2.1.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्राणि राजसूयशतानि च ।
एकादश्युपवासस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
2.1.m: Thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices / do not equal a sixteenth part of a fast on Ekādaśī.

2.1.s:
ekādaśendriyaiḥ pāpaṃ yatkṛtaṃ bhavati prabho /
ekādaśyupavāsena tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ vrajet //
2.1.d:
एकादशेन्द्रियैः पापं यत्कृतं भवति प्रभो ।
एकादश्युपवासेन तत्सर्वं विलयं व्रजेत् ॥
2.1.m: Whatever sin has been committed by the eleven senses, O lord, / all of that dissolves by fasting on Ekādaśī.

2.1.s:
ekādaśīsamaṃ kiñcitpāpanāśaṃ na vidyate /
vyājenāpi kṛtā rājanna darśayati bhāskarim //
2.1.d:
एकादशीसमं किञ्चित्पापनाशं न विद्यते ।
व्याजेनापि कृता राजन्न दर्शयति भास्करिम् ॥
2.1.m: There is no destroyer of sin equal to Ekādaśī; / even if observed under a pretext, O king, it does not reveal the son of the Sun [Yama].

2.1.s:
svargamokṣapradā hyeṣā rājyaputrapradāyinī /
sukalatrapradā hyeṣā śarīrārogyadāyinī //
2.1.d:
स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदा ह्येषा राज्यपुत्रप्रदायिनी ।
सुकलत्रप्रदा ह्येषा शरीरारोग्यदायिनी ॥
2.1.m: For this grants heaven and liberation, bestows kingdom and sons; / indeed, this grants a good wife, and bestows health of body.

2.1.s:
na gaṅgā na gayā bhūpa na kāśī na ca puṣkaram /
na cāpi kairavaṃ kṣetraṃ na revā na ca devikā //
2.1.d:
न गङ्गा न गया भूप न काशी न च पुष्करम् ।
न चापि कैरवं क्षेत्रं न रेवा न च देविका ॥
2.1.m: Neither Gaṅgā nor Gayā, O king, nor Kāśī nor Puṣkara, / nor the sacred field of Kairava, nor the Revā nor the Devikā,

2.1.s:
yamunā candrabhāgā ca puṇyā bhūpa harerdināt /
anāyāsena rājendra prāpyate harimandiram //
2.1.d:
यमुना चन्द्रभागा च पुण्या भूप हरेर्दिनात् ।
अनायासेन राजेन्द्र प्राप्यते हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.1.m: nor the Yamunā nor the Candrabhāgā is as sacred, O king, as the day of Hari. / Without effort, O king of kings, the abode of Hari is reached;

2.1.s:
rātrau jāmaraṇa kṛtvā samupoṣya harerdinam /
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇuloke vrajennaraḥ //
2.1.d:
रात्रौ जामरण कृत्वा समुपोष्य हरेर्दिनम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोके व्रजेन्नरः ॥
2.1.m: having kept vigil at night and fasted on the day of Hari, / freed from all sins, a man goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

2.1.s:
daśaiva mātṛke pakṣe daśa rājendra paitṛke /
bhāryāyā daśa pakṣe ca puruṣānuddharettathā //
2.1.d:
दशैव मातृके पक्षे दश राजेन्द्र पैतृके ।
भार्याया दश पक्षे च पुरुषानुद्धरेत्तथा ॥
2.1.m: He delivers ten generations on the mother's side, ten on the father's side, O king of kings, / and likewise ten generations on the wife's side;

2.1.s:
ātmānamapi rājendra sa nayedvaiṣṇavaṃ puram /
cintāmaṇisamā hyeṣā athavāpi nidheḥ samā //
2.1.d:
आत्मानमपि राजेन्द्र स नयेद्वैष्णवं पुरम् ।
चिन्तामणिसमा ह्येषा अथवापि निधेः समा ॥
2.1.m: he leads himself also, O king of kings, to the city of Viṣṇu. / For this is like the wishing-jewel, or like a treasure,

2.1.s:
saṃkalpapādapaprakhyā vedavākyopamāthavā /
dvādaśīṃ ye prapannā hi narā naravarottama //
2.1.d:
संकल्पपादपप्रख्या वेदवाक्योपमाथवा ।
द्वादशीं ये प्रपन्ना हि नरा नरवरोत्तम ॥
2.1.m: resembling the wishing-tree, or comparable to the words of the Veda. / The men who resort to Dvādaśī, O best of the foremost of men,

2.1.s:
te dvandvabāhavo jātā nāgārikṛtavāhanāḥ /
sragviṇaḥ pītavastrāśca prayānti harimandiram //
2.1.d:
ते द्वन्द्वबाहवो जाता नागारिकृतवाहनाः ।
स्रग्विणः पीतवस्त्राश्च प्रयान्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.1.m: become four-armed, have the enemy of serpents [Garuḍa] as their mount, / wearing garlands and yellow garments, they go to the abode of Hari.

2.1.s:
eṣa prabhāvo hi mayā dvādaśyāḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
pāpendhanasya ghorasya pāvakākhyo mahīpate //
2.1.d:
एष प्रभावो हि मया द्वादश्याः परिकीर्तितः ।
पापेन्धनस्य घोरस्य पावकाख्यो महीपते ॥
2.1.m: This power of the dvādaśī has thus been proclaimed by me, / which is called a fire for the dreadful fuel of sin, O lord of the earth.

2.1.s:
harerddinaṃ sadopoṣyaṃ narairdharmaparāyaṇaiḥ /
icchadbhirvipulānyogānputrapautrādikāṃstathā //
2.1.d:
हरेर्द्दिनं सदोपोष्यं नरैर्धर्मपरायणैः ।
इच्छद्भिर्विपुलान्योगान्पुत्रपौत्रादिकांस्तथा ॥
2.1.m: Hari's day must always be fasted by men devoted to righteousness, / who desire extensive acquisitions, as well as sons, grandsons, and the like.

2.1.s:
haridinamiha martyo yaḥ karotyādareṇa naravara sa tu kukṣiṃ māturāpnoti naiva /
bahuvṛjinasameto 'kāmataḥ kāmato vā vrajati padamanantaṃ lokanāthasya viṣṇoḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge dvādaśīmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.1.d:
हरिदिनमिह मर्त्यो यः करोत्यादरेण नरवर स तु कुक्षिं मातुराप्नोति नैव ।
बहुवृजिनसमेतो ऽकामतः कामतो वा व्रजति पदमनन्तं लोकनाथस्य विष्णोः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे द्वादशीमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम प्रथमो ऽध्यायः
2.1.m:
A mortal here who observes Hari's day with devotion, O best of men, never enters a mother's womb again; / even burdened with many sins, whether unintentionally or intentionally, he goes to the endless abode of Viṣṇu, lord of the world.

Thus ends the first chapter, named 'Description of the Eulogy of Greatness of Dvādaśī', in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.2.s:
vasiṣṭa uvāca
imamevārthamuddiśya naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ /
papracchurmunayaḥ sūtaṃ vyāsaśiṣyaṃ mahāmatim //
2.2.d:
वसिष्ट उवाच
इममेवार्थमुद्दिश्य नैमिषारण्यवासिनः ।
पप्रच्छुर्मुनयः सूतं व्यासशिष्यं महामतिम् ॥
2.2.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / With reference to this very matter, the sages residing in the Naimiṣa forest / questioned Sūta, the high-minded disciple of Vyāsa.

2.2.s:
sa tu pṛṣṭo mahābhāga ekādaśyāḥ suvistaram /
māhātmyaṃ kathayāmāsa upavāsavidhiṃ tathā //
2.2.d:
स तु पृष्टो महाभाग एकादश्याः सुविस्तरम् ।
माहात्म्यं कथयामास उपवासविधिं तथा ॥
2.2.m: Being asked, O illustrious one, he related at full length / the eulogy of greatness of the ekādaśī, and also the rule of fasting.

2.2.s:
tadvākyaṃ sūtaputrasya śrutvā dvijavarottamāḥ /
māhātmyaṃ cakriṇaścāpi sarvapāpaugha śāntidam //
2.2.d:
तद्वाक्यं सूतपुत्रस्य श्रुत्वा द्विजवरोत्तमाः ।
माहात्म्यं चक्रिणश्चापि सर्वपापौघ शान्तिदम् ॥
2.2.m: Having heard that speech of the son of Sūta, and also the eulogy of greatness of the Wielder of the Discus / which brings pacification to the multitude of all sins,

2.2.s:
punaḥ papracchuramalaṃ sūtaṃ paurāṇikaṃ nṛpa /
aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni bhavān jānāti mānada //
2.2.d:
पुनः पप्रच्छुरमलं सूतं पौराणिकं नृप ।
अष्टादश पुराणानि भवान् जानाति मानद ॥
2.2.m: the best of twice-born men questioned once more the stainless Sūta, skilled in the Purāṇas, O king: / "O honor-bestowing one, you know the eighteen Purāṇas,

2.2.s:
kānīnasya prasādenaḥ mahābhāratamapyuta /
tannāsti yanna vetsi tvaṃ purāṇeṣu smṛtiṣvapi //
2.2.d:
कानीनस्य प्रसादेनः महाभारतमप्युत ।
तन्नास्ति यन्न वेत्सि त्वं पुराणेषु स्मृतिष्वपि ॥
2.2.m: and also the Mahābhārata, by the grace of the maiden-born [Vyāsa]; / there is nothing that you do not know among the Purāṇas and the Smṛtis,

2.2.s:
carite raghunāthasya śatakoṭipravistare /
asmākaṃ saṃśayaḥ kaściddhṛdaye saṃpravartate //
2.2.d:
चरिते रघुनाथस्य शतकोटिप्रविस्तरे ।
अस्माकं संशयः कश्चिद्धृदये संप्रवर्तते ॥
2.2.m: or in the deeds of Raghunātha extended to a hundred crores [of verses]. / A doubt has arisen in our hearts;

2.2.s:
taṃ bhavānarhati cchettuṃ yāthārthyena suvistarāt /
titheḥ prāntamupoṣyaṃ syādāhosvinmūlameva ca //
2.2.d:
तं भवानर्हति च्छेत्तुं याथार्थ्येन सुविस्तरात् ।
तिथेः प्रान्तमुपोष्यं स्यादाहोस्विन्मूलमेव च ॥
2.2.m: it is right that you should dispel it thoroughly according to truth: / Should the end of a lunar day be fasted, or rather its beginning?

2.2.s:
daive paitrye samākhyāhi nāvedyaṃ vidyate tavala /
sautiruvāca
titheḥ prāntaṃ surāṇāṃ hi upoṣyaṃ prītivarddhanam //
2.2.d:
दैवे पैत्र्ये समाख्याहि नावेद्यं विद्यते तवल ।
सौतिरुवाच
तिथेः प्रान्तं सुराणां हि उपोष्यं प्रीतिवर्द्धनम् ॥
2.2.m: Explain it with respect to rites for the gods and for the ancestors; there is nothing unknown to you." / Sauti said: / "The end of a lunar day, when fasted, increases the pleasure of the gods,

2.2.s:
mūlaṃ titheḥ pitṝṇāṃ tu kālajñaiḥ priyamīritam /
ataḥ prāntamupoṣyaṃ hi titherdaśaphalepsubhiḥ //
2.2.d:
मूलं तिथेः पितॄणां तु कालज्ञैः प्रियमीरितम् ।
अतः प्रान्तमुपोष्यं हि तिथेर्दशफलेप्सुभिः ॥
2.2.m: while the beginning of a lunar day is declared dear to the ancestors by knowers of time. / Therefore, the end of a lunar day must be fasted by those desiring divine fruits;

2.2.s:
mūlaṃ hi pitṛtṛptyarthaṃ vijñeyaṃ dharmakāṅkṣibhiḥ /
pūrvaviddhā na kartavyā dvitīyā cāṣṭamī tathā //
2.2.d:
मूलं हि पितृतृप्त्यर्थं विज्ञेयं धर्मकाङ्क्षिभिः ।
पूर्वविद्धा न कर्तव्या द्वितीया चाष्टमी तथा ॥
2.2.m: the beginning is to be recognized for the gratification of ancestors by those desiring righteousness. / An overlapped-from-the-previous dvitīyā must not be observed, nor an aṣṭamī,

2.2.s:
ṣaṣṭhī caikādaśī bhūpa dharmakāmārthalipsubhiḥ /
pūrvaviddhā dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kartavyā saptamī sadā //
2.2.d:
षष्ठी चैकादशी भूप धर्मकामार्थलिप्सुभिः ।
पूर्वविद्धा द्विजश्रेष्ठाः कर्तव्या सप्तमी सदा ॥
2.2.m: nor a ṣaṣṭhī, nor an ekādaśī, O king, by those desiring righteousness, pleasure, and wealth. / O best of twice-born men, an overlapped-from-the-previous saptamī must always be observed,

2.2.s:
darśaśca paurṇamāsaśca pituḥ sāṃvatsaraṃ dinam /
pūrvaviddhānimāṃstyaktvā narakaṃ pratipadyate //
2.2.d:
दर्शश्च पौर्णमासश्च पितुः सांवत्सरं दिनम् ।
पूर्वविद्धानिमांस्त्यक्त्वा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
2.2.m: as well as the new moon, the full moon, and the day of a father's annual rite. / Discarding these when overlapped from the previous, one goes to hell,

2.2.s:
hāniṃ ca saṃtaterbhūpadaurbhāgyaṃ samavāpnuyāt /
etacchrutaṃ mayā viprāḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanātpurā //
2.2.d:
हानिं च संततेर्भूपदौर्भाग्यं समवाप्नुयात् ।
एतच्छ्रुतं मया विप्राः कृष्णद्वैपायनात्पुरा ॥
2.2.m: and meets with the loss of offspring, O king, and with misfortune. / This was heard by me formerly from Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, O brahmins.

2.2.s:
ādityodayavelāyāṃ yāstokāpi tithirbhavet /
pūrvaviddhā tu mantavyā prabhūtā nodayaṃ vinā //
2.2.d:
आदित्योदयवेलायां यास्तोकापि तिथिर्भवेत् ।
पूर्वविद्धा तु मन्तव्या प्रभूता नोदयं विना ॥
2.2.m: Whatever lunar day exists at the time of sunrise, even if slight, / is to be considered as overlapping the previous; an extensive one [is not valid] without sunrise.

2.2.s:
pāraṇe maraṇe nṝṇāṃ tithistātkālikī smṛtā /
pitrye 'stamanavelāyāṃ sparśe pūrṇā nigadyate //
2.2.d:
पारणे मरणे नॄणां तिथिस्तात्कालिकी स्मृता ।
पित्र्ये ऽस्तमनवेलायां स्पर्शे पूर्णा निगद्यते ॥
2.2.m: At the breaking of a fast and at the death of men, the lunar day of the relevant time is declared [valid]; / in rites for ancestors, if there is contact at the time of sunset, it is said to be complete.

2.2.s:
na tatrodayinī grāhyā daivasyodayikī tithiḥ /
pratyahaṃ śodhayetprājñastithiṃ daivajñacintakāt //
2.2.d:
न तत्रोदयिनी ग्राह्या दैवस्योदयिकी तिथिः ।
प्रत्यहं शोधयेत्प्राज्ञस्तिथिं दैवज्ञचिन्तकात् ॥
2.2.m: A sunrise-based [tithi] is not to be accepted there; the sunrise-based tithi belongs to the gods. / Everyday a wise man should ascertain the lunar day from an astrologer.

2.2.s:
tithipramāṇaṃ viprendrāḥ kṣapākaradivākarau /
candrārkacāravijñānātkālaṃ kālavido viduḥ //
2.2.d:
तिथिप्रमाणं विप्रेन्द्राः क्षपाकरदिवाकरौ ।
चन्द्रार्कचारविज्ञानात्कालं कालविदो विदुः ॥
2.2.m: The measure of a lunar day, O chief brahmins, is the moon and the sun; / from knowledge of the course of the moon and sun, knowers of time understand time.

2.2.s:
pūrvāyāḥ saṃgadoṣeṇa na yogyāstāḥ prapūjane /
varjayanti narāstajjñā yāmāṃśca caturo dvijāḥ //
2.2.d:
पूर्वायाः संगदोषेण न योग्यास्ताः प्रपूजने ।
वर्जयन्ति नरास्तज्ज्ञा यामांश्च चतुरो द्विजाः ॥
2.2.m: Due to the flaw of contact with the preceding, they are unfit for worship; / men who know that, O twice-born, avoid the four watches.

2.2.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi snānapūjāvidhikramam /
na divā śuddhimāpnoti tadā rātrau vidhīyate //
2.2.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि स्नानपूजाविधिक्रमम् ।
न दिवा शुद्धिमाप्नोति तदा रात्रौ विधीयते ॥
2.2.m: Hereafter I shall explain the order of rules for bathing and worship: / If one does not attain purity by day, then it is prescribed at night.

2.2.s:
dinakāryamaśeṣaṃ hi kartavyaṃ śarvarīmukhe /
vidhireṣa mayā khyāto narāṇāmupavāsinām //
2.2.d:
दिनकार्यमशेषं हि कर्तव्यं शर्वरीमुखे ।
विधिरेष मया ख्यातो नराणामुपवासिनाम् ॥
2.2.m: All daytime rites must be performed at the beginning of the night; / this rule has been proclaimed by me for fasting men.

2.2.s:
alpāyāmatha viprendrā dvādaśyāmaruṇodaye /
snānārcanakriyā kāryyā dānahomādisaṃyutā //
2.2.d:
अल्पायामथ विप्रेन्द्रा द्वादश्यामरुणोदये ।
स्नानार्चनक्रिया कार्य्या दानहोमादिसंयुता ॥
2.2.m: When the twelfth lunar day is short, O foremost brāhmaṇas, at dawn / the rites of bathing and worship, along with gifts, fire oblations, and other [acts], are to be performed.

2.2.s:
trayodaśyāṃ pāraṇe pṛthivīphalam /
śatayajñādhikaṃ vāpi naraḥ prāpnotyasaṃśayam //
2.2.d:
त्रयोदश्यां पारणे पृथिवीफलम् ।
शतयज्ञाधिकं वापि नरः प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
2.2.m: Breaking the fast on the thirteenth lunar day, a man obtains the fruit of the earth, / or more than a hundred sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.

2.2.s:
etasmātkāraṇādviprāḥ pratyūṣe snānamācaret /
pitṛtarpaṇasaṃyuktaṃ na dṛṣṭvā dvādaśīdinam //
2.2.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्विप्राः प्रत्यूषे स्नानमाचरेत् ।
पितृतर्पणसंयुक्तं न दृष्ट्वा द्वादशीदिनम् ॥
2.2.m: For this reason, O brāhmaṇas, one should perform bathing at daybreak / accompanied by ancestral libations, without waiting to see the day of the twelfth.

2.2.s:
mahāhānikarā hyeṣā dvādaśī laṅghitā nṛbhiḥ /
karoti dharmaharaṇamasnāteva sarasvatī //
2.2.d:
महाहानिकरा ह्येषा द्वादशी लङ्घिता नृभिः ।
करोति धर्महरणमस्नातेव सरस्वती ॥
2.2.m: For when neglected by men, this twelfth [lunar day] causes great loss; / like the Sarasvatī without bathing, it takes away all religious merit.

2.2.s:
kṣaye vāpyathavā vṛddhau saṃprāpte vā dinodaye /
upoṣyā dvādaśī puṇyā pūrvaviddhāṃ vivarjayet //
2.2.d:
क्षये वाप्यथवा वृद्धौ संप्राप्ते वा दिनोदये ।
उपोष्या द्वादशी पुण्या पूर्वविद्धां विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.2.m: Whether in decrease, increase, or upon reaching the rise of the day, / the holy twelfth is to be observed as a fast; one must avoid [an eleventh] pierced by the preceding.

2.2.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
yadā ca prāpyate sūta dvādaśyāṃ pūrvasaṃbhavā /
tadopavāso hi kathaṃ kartavyo mānavairvada //
2.2.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
यदा च प्राप्यते सूत द्वादश्यां पूर्वसंभवा ।
तदोपवासो हि कथं कर्तव्यो मानवैर्वद ॥
2.2.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / When, O Sūta, [the fast] falls upon the twelfth because the preceding [tithi] is present, / tell [us], how should the fast then be observed by men?

2.2.s:
upavāsadinaṃ viddhaṃ yadā bhavati pūrvayā /
dvitīye 'hni yadā na syātsvalpāpyekādaśī tithiḥ //
2.2.d:
उपवासदिनं विद्धं यदा भवति पूर्वया ।
द्वितीये ऽह्नि यदा न स्यात्स्वल्पाप्येकादशी तिथिः ॥
2.2.m: When the day of fasting is pierced by the preceding [tithi], / and on the second day there is not even a very short eleventh lunar day,

2.2.s:
tatropavāso vihitaḥ kathaṃ tadvada sūtaja /
sautiruvāca
yadā na prāpyate viprā dvādaśyāṃ pūrvasambhavam //
2.2.d:
तत्रोपवासो विहितः कथं तद्वद सूतज ।
सौतिरुवाच
यदा न प्राप्यते विप्रा द्वादश्यां पूर्वसम्भवम् ॥
2.2.m: How is the fast prescribed there? Tell that, O son of Sūta. / Sauti said: / When, O brāhmaṇas, [an eleventh] without overlap from the preceding is not found on the twelfth,

2.2.s:
ravicandrārkajāhaṃ tu tadopoṣyaṃ paraṃ dinam /
bahvā gamavirodheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu vivādiṣu //
2.2.d:
रविचन्द्रार्कजाहं तु तदोपोष्यं परं दिनम् ।
बह्वा गमविरोधेषु ब्राह्मणेषु विवादिषु ॥
2.2.m: On the day of the Sun, the Moon, or the son of the Sun (Saturn), the following day is then to be observed as a fast. / When many scriptures conflict, and the brāhmaṇas are in dispute,

2.2.s:
upoṣyā dvādaśī puṇyā trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam /
ekādaśyāṃ tu viddhāyāṃ saṃprāpte śravaṇe tathā //
2.2.d:
उपोष्या द्वादशी पुण्या त्रयोदश्यां तु पारणम् ।
एकादश्यां तु विद्धायां संप्राप्ते श्रवणे तथा ॥
2.2.m: The holy twelfth is to be observed as a fast, and the breaking of the fast on the thirteenth. / So too, when the eleventh is pierced and Śravaṇa has arrived,

2.2.s:
upoṣyā dvādaśī puṇyā pakṣayorubhayorapi /
eṣa vo nirṇayaḥ prokto mayā śāstravinirṇayāt //
2.2.d:
उपोष्या द्वादशी पुण्या पक्षयोरुभयोरपि ।
एष वो निर्णयः प्रोक्तो मया शास्त्रविनिर्णयात् ॥
2.2.m: The holy twelfth is to be observed as a fast in both fortnights. / This decision has been declared to you by me in accordance with the decision of the scriptures.

2.2.s:
kimanyacchrotukāmā hi tadbhavanto bruvantu me /
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
yugādīnāṃ vadavidhiṃ saute samyagyathātatham //
2.2.d:
किमन्यच्छ्रोतुकामा हि तद्भवन्तो ब्रुवन्तु मे ।
ऋषय ऊचुः
युगादीनां वदविधिं सौते सम्यग्यथातथम् ॥
2.2.m: What else do you desire to hear? Let you tell me that. / The sages said: / Declare the rules concerning the beginnings of yugas accurately as they are, O Sauti,

2.2.s:
ravisaṃkrātikādīnāṃ nāvedyaṃ vidyate tava /
sautiruvāca
dve śukle dve tathā kṛṣṇe yugādyāḥ kavayo viduḥ //
2.2.d:
रविसंक्रातिकादीनां नावेद्यं विद्यते तव ।
सौतिरुवाच
द्वे शुक्ले द्वे तथा कृष्णे युगाद्याः कवयो विदुः ॥
2.2.m: As well as the solstices, transits of the sun, and the like; there is nothing unknown to you. / Sauti said: / Two in the bright [fortnight] and two in the dark: the wise know these as the beginnings of yugas.

2.2.s:
śukle pūrvāhṇike grāhye kṛṣṇe grāhye 'parāhṇike /
ayanaṃ dinabhāgāḍhyaṃ saṃkramaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ palaḥ //
2.2.d:
शुक्ले पूर्वाह्णिके ग्राह्ये कृष्णे ग्राह्ये ऽपराह्णिके ।
अयनं दिनभागाढ्यं संक्रमः षोडशः पलः ॥
2.2.m: In the bright, [the yugādi] is to be taken in the forenoon; in the dark, it is to be taken in the afternoon. / A solstice consists of parts of a day; a solar transit is sixteen palas.

2.2.s:
pūrve tu dakṣiṇe bhāge vyatīte cottaro mataḥ /
madhyakāle tu viṣuve tvakṣayā parikīrtitā //
2.2.d:
पूर्वे तु दक्षिणे भागे व्यतीते चोत्तरो मतः ।
मध्यकाले तु विषुवे त्वक्षया परिकीर्तिता ॥
2.2.m: In the southern [solstice], the prior portion is considered, and in the northern, the subsequent; / but at the middle time of the equinox, it is proclaimed to be imperishable.

2.2.s:
jñātvā viprāstithiṃ samyaksāṃvatsarasamīritām /
kartavyo hyupavāsastu anyathā narakaṃ vrajet //
2.2.d:
ज्ञात्वा विप्रास्तिथिं सम्यक्सांवत्सरसमीरिताम् ।
कर्तव्यो ह्युपवासस्तु अन्यथा नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
2.2.m: Having accurately ascertained the lunar day declared by the astrologer, O brāhmaṇas, / the fast is indeed to be performed; otherwise one goes to hell.

2.2.s:
pūrvaviddhāṃ prakurvāṇo naro dharmaṃ nikṛntati /
saṃtatestu vināśāya saṃpadāṃ haraṇāya ca //
2.2.d:
पूर्वविद्धां प्रकुर्वाणो नरो धर्मं निकृन्तति ।
संततेस्तु विनाशाय संपदां हरणाय च ॥
2.2.m: A man who performs [the fast on a tithi] pierced by the preceding cuts away his dharma, / leading to the destruction of his lineage and the loss of his wealth.

2.2.s:
palavedhe 'pi viprendrā daśamyā varjayecchivām /
surāyā bindunā spṛṣṭa yathā gaṅgājalantyajet //
2.2.d:
पलवेधे ऽपि विप्रेन्द्रा दशम्या वर्जयेच्छिवाम् ।
सुराया बिन्दुना स्पृष्ट यथा गङ्गाजलन्त्यजेत् ॥
2.2.m: Even with a piercing of a single pala by the tenth, O foremost brāhmaṇas, one should avoid the auspicious [eleventh], / just as one would abandon Gaṅgā water touched by a drop of liquor.

2.2.s:
śvahataṃ pañcagavyaṃ ca daśamyā dūṣitāṃ tyajet /
ekādaśīṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ pakṣayorubhayorapi //
2.2.d:
श्वहतं पञ्चगव्यं च दशम्या दूषितां त्यजेत् ।
एकादशीं द्विजश्रेष्ठाः पक्षयोरुभयोरपि ॥
2.2.m: Just as one would abandon the five products of the cow defiled by a dog, so should one abandon the eleventh defiled by the tenth, / O best of twice-born, in both fortnights.

2.2.s:
pūrvaviddhā purā dattā sā tithiryadumaulinā /
dānavebhyo dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ prīṇanārthaṃ mahātmanām //
2.2.d:
पूर्वविद्धा पुरा दत्ता सा तिथिर्यदुमौलिना ।
दानवेभ्यो द्विजश्रेष्ठाः प्रीणनार्थं महात्मनाम् ॥
2.2.m: Long ago, that lunar day pierced by the preceding was given by the crown of the Yadus (Kṛṣṇa) / to the Dānavas, O best of twice-born, to propitiate those great beings.

2.2.s:
akāle yaddhanaṃ dattamapātrebhyo dvijottamāḥ /
saṃkrudvairapi yaddattaṃ yaddattaṃ cāpyasatkṛtam //
2.2.d:
अकाले यद्धनं दत्तमपात्रेभ्यो द्विजोत्तमाः ।
संक्रुद्वैरपि यद्दत्तं यद्दत्तं चाप्यसत्कृतम् ॥
2.2.m: Wealth given at an improper time, given to unworthy recipients, O best of twice-born, / or given in anger, or given without respect,

2.2.s:
pūrvaviddhatithau dattaṃ taddattamasureṣvatha /
yaducchiṣṭena dattaṃ tu yaddattaṃ patiteṣvapi //
2.2.d:
पूर्वविद्धतिथौ दत्तं तद्दत्तमसुरेष्वथ ।
यदुच्छिष्टेन दत्तं तु यद्दत्तं पतितेष्वपि ॥
2.2.m: Or given on a lunar day pierced by the preceding, that is indeed given to the Asuras. / What is given in an impure state, or what is given to the fallen,

2.2.s:
strījeteṣu ca yaddattaṃ yaddattaṃ jalavarjitam /
punaḥ kīrtanasaṃyuktaṃ taddattamasureṣu vai //
2.2.d:
स्त्रीजेतेषु च यद्दत्तं यद्दत्तं जलवर्जितम् ।
पुनः कीर्तनसंयुक्तं तद्दत्तमसुरेषु वै ॥
2.2.m: And what is given to those conquered by women, or what is given without water, / or accompanied by boasting afterwards, that is indeed given to the Asuras.

2.2.s:
tasmādviprā na kartvyā viddhāpyekādaśī tithiḥ /
yathā hantipurā puṇyaṃ śrāddhaṃ ca vṛṣalīpatiḥ //
2.2.d:
तस्माद्विप्रा न कर्त्व्या विद्धाप्येकादशी तिथिः ।
यथा हन्तिपुरा पुण्यं श्राद्धं च वृषलीपतिः ॥
2.2.m: Therefore, O brāhmaṇas, an eleventh lunar day that is pierced must not be observed, / just as a husband of a Śūdra woman formerly destroys the merit of a śrāddha.

2.2.s:
dattaṃ japtaṃ hutaṃ snātaṃ tathā pūjā kṛtā hareḥ /
tithau viddhe kṣayaṃ yāti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā //
2.2.d:
दत्तं जप्तं हुतं स्नातं तथा पूजा कृता हरेः ।
तिथौ विद्धे क्षयं याति तमः सूर्योदये यथा ॥
2.2.m: What is given, recited, offered into fire, or bathed, and likewise worship paid to Hari, / on a pierced lunar day goes to ruin, just as darkness at sunrise.

2.2.s:
jīrṇaṃ patiṃ yauvanagarvitā yathā tyajanti nāryo jhaṣaketunārditāḥ /
tathā hi vedhaṃ vibudhāstyajanti tithyantaraṃ dharmavivṛddhaye sadā //
śrībṛhannāradīyapuraṇottarabhāge tithivicāro nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.2.d:
जीर्णं पतिं यौवनगर्विता यथा त्यजन्ति नार्यो झषकेतुनार्दिताः ।
तथा हि वेधं विबुधास्त्यजन्ति तिथ्यन्तरं धर्मविवृद्धये सदा ॥
श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुरणोत्तरभागे तिथिविचारो नाम द्वितीयो ऽध्यायः
2.2.m:
Just as women proud of their youth, afflicted by the fish-bannered [god of love], abandon an aged husband, / so the wise always abandon an overlap for another lunar day to increase their dharma.

In the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, the second chapter, entitled "Deliberation on Lunar Days".

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
vistareṇa samākhyā hi viṣṇorārādhanakriyām /
yayā toṣaṃ samāyāti pradadāti samīhitam //
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
विस्तरेण समाख्या हि विष्णोराराधनक्रियाम् ।
यया तोषं समायाति प्रददाति समीहितम् ॥
2.3.m: The sages said: / Declare in full the rite of worshipping Viṣṇu, / by which he attains satisfaction and grants what is desired.

2.3.s:
lakṣmībhartājagannāthohyaśeṣāghaughanāśanaḥ /
karmaṇā kena sa prīto bhavedyaḥ sacarācaraḥ //
2.3.d:
लक्ष्मीभर्ताजगन्नाथोह्यशेषाघौघनाशनः ।
कर्मणा केन स प्रीतो भवेद्यः सचराचरः ॥
2.3.m: The Lord of Lakṣmī, the Lord of the world, who destroys the entire mass of sins— / by what deed is he pleased, he who contains the moving and the unmoving?

2.3.s:
sautiruvāca
bhaktigrāhyo hṛṣīkeśo na dhanairddharaṇīdhara /
bhaktyā saṃpūjito viṣṇuḥ pradadāti manoratham //
2.3.d:
सौतिरुवाच
भक्तिग्राह्यो हृषीकेशो न धनैर्द्धरणीधर ।
भक्त्या संपूजितो विष्णुः प्रददाति मनोरथम् ॥
2.3.m: Sauti said: / Hṛṣīkeśa is won through devotion, not by wealth, O support of the earth; / Viṣṇu, worshipped with devotion, grants one's desire.

2.3.s:
tasmādviprāḥ sadā bhaktiḥ karttavyā cakrapāṇinaḥ /
janenāpi jagannāthaḥ pūjitaḥ kleśahā bhavet //
2.3.d:
तस्माद्विप्राः सदा भक्तिः कर्त्तव्या चक्रपाणिनः ।
जनेनापि जगन्नाथः पूजितः क्लेशहा भवेत् ॥
2.3.m: Therefore, O brāhmaṇas, devotion to the wielder of the discus should always be cultivated; / even worshipped by an ordinary man, the Lord of the world removes distress.

2.3.s:
paritoṣaṃ vrajatyāśutṛṣitastu jalairyathā /
atrāpi śrūyate viprā ākhyānaṃ pāpanāśanam //
2.3.d:
परितोषं व्रजत्याशुतृषितस्तु जलैर्यथा ।
अत्रापि श्रूयते विप्रा आख्यानं पापनाशनम् ॥
2.3.m: He goes quickly to contentment, just as a thirsty man with water. / On this point too, O brāhmaṇas, a sin-destroying ancient tale is heard,

2.3.s:
rukmāṅgadasya saṃvādamṛṣiṇā gautamena hi /
āsīdgrukmāṅgado rājā sārvabhaumaḥ kṣamānvitaḥ //
2.3.d:
रुक्माङ्गदस्य संवादमृषिणा गौतमेन हि ।
आसीद्ग्रुक्माङ्गदो राजा सार्वभौमः क्षमान्वितः ॥
2.3.m: Namely, the dialogue of Rukmāṅgada with the sage Gautama. / There was a king named Rukmāṅgada, a sovereign emperor endowed with forgiveness,

2.3.s:
kṣīraśāyipriyo bhakto harivāsaratatparaḥ /
nānyaṃ paśyati deveśātpadmanābhānmahīpatiḥ //
2.3.d:
क्षीरशायिप्रियो भक्तो हरिवासरतत्परः ।
नान्यं पश्यति देवेशात्पद्मनाभान्महीपतिः ॥
2.3.m: Dear to the one who sleeps on the milk-ocean, devoted, intent upon the day of Hari; / the ruler of the earth saw none other than the lotus-navelled Lord of the gods.

2.3.s:
paṭahaṃ vāraṇe dhṛtvā vādayeddhari vāsare /
aṣṭavarṣādhiko yastu pañcāśītyūnavarṣakaḥ //
2.3.d:
पटहं वारणे धृत्वा वादयेद्धरि वासरे ।
अष्टवर्षाधिको यस्तु पञ्चाशीत्यूनवर्षकः ॥
2.3.m: Placing a drum upon an elephant, he had it sounded on the day of Hari: / 'Whoever is older than eight years and younger than eighty-five,

2.3.s:
bhunakti mānavo hyadya viṣṇorahani mandadhīḥ /
sa me daṇḍyaścaga vadhyaśca nirvāsyo nagarādbahiḥ //
2.3.d:
भुनक्ति मानवो ह्यद्य विष्णोरहनि मन्दधीः ।
स मे दण्ड्यश्चग वध्यश्च निर्वास्यो नगराद्बहिः ॥
2.3.m: If that human, foolish of mind, eats food today on the day of Viṣṇu, / he shall be punished by me, killed, and banished outside the city.

2.3.s:
pitā ca yadi vā bhrātā putro bhāryā suhṛnmama /
padmanābhadine bhoktā nigrāhyo dasyuvadbhavet //
2.3.d:
पिता च यदि वा भ्राता पुत्रो भार्या सुहृन्मम ।
पद्मनाभदिने भोक्ता निग्राह्यो दस्युवद्भवेत् ॥
2.3.m: Be he my father, or brother, son, wife, or friend, / one who eats on the day of the lotus-navelled [Lord] shall be seized like a bandit.

2.3.s:
dadaghvaṃma vipramukhyabhyo majjadhvaṃ jāhnavījale /
mameda vacanaṃ śṛtvā rājyaṃ bhuñjīta māmakam //
2.3.d:
ददघ्वंम विप्रमुख्यभ्यो मज्जध्वं जाह्नवीजले ।
ममेद वचनं शृत्वा राज्यं भुञ्जीत मामकम् ॥
2.3.m: Give to the foremost brāhmaṇas, bathe in the waters of the Jāhnavī; / having heard this word of mine, let one enjoy my kingdom.'

2.3.s:
vāsare vāsare viṣṇoḥ śuklapakṣe mahīpatiḥ /
aśukle tu viśeṣeṇa paṭahe hemasaṃpuṭe //
2.3.d:
वासरे वासरे विष्णोः शुक्लपक्षे महीपतिः ।
अशुक्ले तु विशेषेण पटहे हेमसंपुटे ॥
2.3.m: On each day of Viṣṇu in the bright fortnight, the ruler of the earth, / and especially in the non-bright (dark), with a drum in a golden case [proclaimed this].

2.3.s:
evaṃ praghuṣṭe bhūpena sarvabhūmau dvijottamāḥ /
gacchidbhiḥ saṃkulo mārgaḥ kṛto kṛto lokairharerdvijāḥ //
2.3.d:
एवं प्रघुष्टे भूपेन सर्वभूमौ द्विजोत्तमाः ।
गच्छिद्भिः संकुलो मार्गः कृतो कृतो लोकैर्हरेर्द्विजाः ॥
2.3.m: When it was thus proclaimed by the king throughout the entire earth, O best of twice-born, / the path of Hari was crowded with people going there, O twice-born.

2.3.s:
ye kecinnidhanaṃ yānti bhūpālaviṣaye narāḥ /
jñānātpramādato vāpi te yānti harimandiram //
2.3.d:
ये केचिन्निधनं यान्ति भूपालविषये नराः ।
ज्ञानात्प्रमादतो वापि ते यान्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.3.m: Whatever men met death in the territory of that king, / whether through knowledge or through negligence, they went to the abode of Hari.

2.3.s:
avaśyaṃ vaiṣṇavo lokaḥ prāpyate mānavairdvijāḥ /
vyājenāpi prakurvāṇairdvādaśīṃ pāpanāśinīm //
2.3.d:
अवश्यं वैष्णवो लोकः प्राप्यते मानवैर्द्विजाः ।
व्याजेनापि प्रकुर्वाणैर्द्वादशीं पापनाशिनीम् ॥
2.3.m: The world of Viṣṇu is inevitably attained by men, O twice-born, / who observe the sin-destroying twelfth, even under a pretext.

2.3.s:
so 'śnāti pārthivaṃ pāpaṃ yo 'śnāti harivāsare /
sa prāpnoti dharādharmaṃ yo nāśnāti harerdine //
2.3.d:
सो ऽश्नाति पार्थिवं पापं यो ऽश्नाति हरिवासरे ।
स प्राप्नोति धराधर्मं यो नाश्नाति हरेर्दिने ॥
2.3.m: He eats earthly sin who eats on the day of Hari; / he attains the righteousness of the earth who does not eat on the day of Hari.

2.3.s:
brāhmaṇo naiva hantavya ityeṣā vaidikī smṛtiḥ /
ekādaśyāṃ na bhoktavyaṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi //
2.3.d:
ब्राह्मणो नैव हन्तव्य इत्येषा वैदिकी स्मृतिः ।
एकादश्यां न भोक्तव्यं पक्षयोरुभयोरपि ॥
2.3.m: 'A brāhmaṇa must never be killed'—this is the Vedic tradition; / [likewise] one must not eat on the eleventh in both fortnights.

2.3.s:
vailakṣyamagamadrājā ravisūnurdvijottamāḥ /
lekhyakarmaṇi viśrāntaścitragupto 'bhavattadā //
2.3.d:
वैलक्ष्यमगमद्राजा रविसूनुर्द्विजोत्तमाः ।
लेख्यकर्मणि विश्रान्तश्चित्रगुप्तो ऽभवत्तदा ॥
2.3.m: The king who is the son of the Sun (Yama) fell into despondency, O best of twice-born, / and Citragupta then rested from the work of writing.

2.3.s:
saṃmārjitāni lekhyāni pūrvakarmodbhavāni ca /
gacchanti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ svadharmairmānavāḥ kṣaṇāt //
2.3.d:
संमार्जितानि लेख्यानि पूर्वकर्मोद्भवानि च ।
गच्छन्ति वैष्णवं लोकं स्वधर्मैर्मानवाः क्षणात् ॥
2.3.m: The records arising from previous actions were wiped clean; / by their own duties, human beings went in an instant to the world of Viṣṇu.

2.3.s:
śūnyā stu nirayāḥ sarve pāpaprāṇivivarjitāḥ /
bhagno yāmyo 'bhavanmārgo dvādaśādityatāpitaḥ //
2.3.d:
शून्या स्तु निरयाः सर्वे पापप्राणिविवर्जिताः ।
भग्नो याम्यो ऽभवन्मार्गो द्वादशादित्यतापितः ॥
2.3.m: All the hells became empty, deserted by sinful creatures; / the path to the realm of Yama became broken, scorched by the twelve suns.

2.3.s:
sarve hi garuḍārūḍhā janā yānti hareḥ padam /
devā nāmapi ye lokāste śūnyā hyabhavaṃstathā //
2.3.d:
सर्वे हि गरुडारूढा जना यान्ति हरेः पदम् ।
देवा नामपि ये लोकास्ते शून्या ह्यभवंस्तथा ॥
2.3.m: Mounted upon Garuḍa, all people go to Hari's abode; / and the worlds of the gods became empty in that manner.

2.3.s:
utsannāḥ pitṛdevejyāstīrthadānādisatkriyāḥ /
muktvaikāṃ dvādaśīṃ martyā nānyaṃ jānanti te vratam //
2.3.d:
उत्सन्नाः पितृदेवेज्यास्तीर्थदानादिसत्क्रियाः ।
मुक्त्वैकां द्वादशीं मर्त्या नान्यं जानन्ति ते व्रतम् ॥
2.3.m: Sacrifices to ancestors and gods, and good works such as gifts at sacred fords, were abandoned; / mortals know no other vow except the single dvādaśī.

2.3.s:
śūnye triviṣṭape jāte śūnye ca narake tathā /
nārado dharmarājānaṃ gatvā cedamuvāca ha //
2.3.d:
शून्ये त्रिविष्टपे जाते शून्ये च नरके तथा ।
नारदो धर्मराजानं गत्वा चेदमुवाच ह ॥
2.3.m: When heaven had become empty, and hell had likewise become empty, / Nārada went to the king of righteousness and said this:

2.3.s:
nārada uvāca
nākrandaḥ śrūyate rājan prāṅgaṇe narakeṣvatha /
na cāpi kriyate lekhyaṃ kiñcidduṣkṛtakarmaṇām //
2.3.d:
नारद उवाच
नाक्रन्दः श्रूयते राजन् प्राङ्गणे नरकेष्वथ ।
न चापि क्रियते लेख्यं किञ्चिद्दुष्कृतकर्मणाम् ॥
2.3.m: Nārada said: / "No lamentation is heard, O king, in your courtyard or in the hells; / nor is any writing done of the deeds of evil-doers.

2.3.s:
citragupto muniriva sthito 'yaṃ maunasaṃyutaḥ /
kāraṇaṃ kiṃ na cāyānti pāpino yena te gṛham //
2.3.d:
चित्रगुप्तो मुनिरिव स्थितो ऽयं मौनसंयुतः ।
कारणं किं न चायान्ति पापिनो येन ते गृहम् ॥
2.3.m: This Citragupta stands silent like a sage. / What is the reason that sinners do not come to your house,

2.3.s:
māyādaṃbhasamākrāntā duṣṭakarmaratāstathā /
evamukte tu vacane nāradena mahātmanā //
2.3.d:
मायादंभसमाक्रान्ता दुष्टकर्मरतास्तथा ।
एवमुक्ते तु वचने नारदेन महात्मना ॥
2.3.m: those overcome by deceit and hypocrisy, and devoted to wicked deeds?" / When these words had been spoken by the high-souled Nārada,

2.3.s:
prāha vaivasvato rājā kiñciddainyasamanvitaḥ /
yama uvāca
yo 'yaṃ nārada bhūpālaḥ pṛthivyāṃ sāṃprataṃ sthitaḥ //
2.3.d:
प्राह वैवस्वतो राजा किञ्चिद्दैन्यसमन्वितः ।
यम उवाच
यो ऽयं नारद भूपालः पृथिव्यां सांप्रतं स्थितः ॥
2.3.m: King Vaivasvata spoke, filled with a certain dejection. / Yama said: / "That king who presently lives on earth, O Nārada,

2.3.s:
sa hi bhakto hṛṣīkeśe purāṇapuruṣottame /
prabodhayati rājendraḥ sa janaṃ paṭahena hi //
2.3.d:
स हि भक्तो हृषीकेशे पुराणपुरुषोत्तमे ।
प्रबोधयति राजेन्द्रः स जनं पटहेन हि ॥
2.3.m: he is a devotee of Hṛṣīkeśa, the ancient supreme person; / that lord of kings awakens people with the drum:

2.3.s:
na bhoktavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare /
ye kecidbhuñjate martyāste me daṇḍeṣu yānti hi //
2.3.d:
न भोक्तव्यं न भोक्तव्यं संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ।
ये केचिद्भुञ्जते मर्त्यास्ते मे दण्डेषु यान्ति हि ॥
2.3.m: 'One must not eat, one must not eat when Hari's day has arrived! / Whatever mortals eat, they will go under my punishments.'

2.3.s:
tadbhayāddhi janāḥ sarve dvādaśīṃ samupāsate /
vyājenāpi munuśreṣṭha dvādaśyāṃ samupoṣitāḥ //
2.3.d:
तद्भयाद्धि जनाः सर्वे द्वादशीं समुपासते ।
व्याजेनापि मुनुश्रेष्ठ द्वादश्यां समुपोषिताः ॥
2.3.m: Out of fear of that, all people observe the dvādaśī; / having fasted on the dvādaśī even under a pretext, O best of sages,

2.3.s:
prayānti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ dāhapralayavarjitam /
dvādaśīsevanāllokāḥ prāyānti harimandiram //
2.3.d:
प्रयान्ति वैष्णवं लोकं दाहप्रलयवर्जितम् ।
द्वादशीसेवनाल्लोकाः प्रायान्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.3.m: they go to the Vaiṣṇava realm, free from burning and dissolution. / Through devotion to the dvādaśī, people go to Hari's temple.

2.3.s:
tena rājñā dvijaśreṣṭha mārgā luptā mamādhunā /
kṛta hi narakāḥ śūnyā lokāścāpi divaukasām //
2.3.d:
तेन राज्ञा द्विजश्रेष्ठ मार्गा लुप्ता ममाधुना ।
कृत हि नरकाः शून्या लोकाश्चापि दिवौकसाम् ॥
2.3.m: By that king, O best of twice-born, my paths have now been destroyed; / the hells have been made empty, and so too the realms of the gods.

2.3.s:
viśrāntaṃ lekhakerlekhyaṃ likhitaṃ mārjitaṃ janaiḥ /
ekādaśyupavāsasya māhātmyena dvijottama //
2.3.d:
विश्रान्तं लेखकेर्लेख्यं लिखितं मार्जितं जनैः ।
एकादश्युपवासस्य माहात्म्येन द्विजोत्तम ॥
2.3.m: The writing has been rested by the scribes; what was written has been erased by the people, / through the greatness of fasting on the ekādaśī, O best of twice-born.

2.3.s:
brahmahatyādipāpāni abhuktvaiva janā dvija /
samupoṣya dinaṃ viṣṇoḥ prayānti harimandiram //
2.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि अभुक्त्वैव जना द्विज ।
समुपोष्य दिनं विष्णोः प्रयान्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.3.m: Without even experiencing [the fruits of] sins such as killing a brahmin, O twice-born, / having fasted on the day of Viṣṇu, people go to Hari's temple.

2.3.s:
so 'haṃ kāṣāṭamṛgeṇaiva tulyo jāto mahāmune /
netrahīnaḥ karṇahīnaḥ saṃdhyāhīno dvijo yathā //
2.3.d:
सो ऽहं काषाटमृगेणैव तुल्यो जातो महामुने ।
नेत्रहीनः कर्णहीनः संध्याहीनो द्विजो यथा ॥
2.3.m: Such as I am, I have become equal to a wooden deer, O great sage; / like a twice-born lacking eyes, lacking ears, and lacking twilight devotion,

2.3.s:
strījito vā pumānyadvatṣaṇḍho vā pramadāpatiḥ /
tyaktakāmastvahaṃ brahmaṃllokapālatvamīdṛśam //
2.3.d:
स्त्रीजितो वा पुमान्यद्वत्षण्ढो वा प्रमदापतिः ।
त्यक्तकामस्त्वहं ब्रह्मंल्लोकपालत्वमीदृशम् ॥
2.3.m: or like a man conquered by a woman, or an impotent husband of a wife. / I have abandoned desire, O brahmin, for such guardianship of the worlds;

2.3.s:
yāsyāmi brahmaloke vai duḥkhaṃ jñāpayituṃ svakam /
nirvyāpāro niyogī tu niyoge yastu tiṣṭhati //
2.3.d:
यास्यामि ब्रह्मलोके वै दुःखं ज्ञापयितुं स्वकम् ।
निर्व्यापारो नियोगी तु नियोगे यस्तु तिष्ठति ॥
2.3.m: I shall go to the world of Brahmā to make known my sorrow. / An appointed official who stays in his post without duty,

2.3.s:
svāmivittaṃ samaśnāti sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam /
sautiruvāca
evamuktvā yamo viprā nāradena samanvitaḥ //
2.3.d:
स्वामिवित्तं समश्नाति स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ।
सौतिरुवाच
एवमुक्त्वा यमो विप्रा नारदेन समन्वितः ॥
2.3.m: yet consumes his master's wealth, surely goes to hell." / Sauti said: / Having spoken thus, O brahmins, Yama, accompanied by Nārada

2.3.s:
yayau virañcisadanaṃ citracisadanaṃ citraguptena cānvitaḥ /
sa dadarśa samāsīnaṃ mūrtāmūratajanāvṛtam //
2.3.d:
ययौ विरञ्चिसदनं चित्रचिसदनं चित्रगुप्तेन चान्वितः ।
स ददर्श समासीनं मूर्तामूरतजनावृतम् ॥
2.3.m: and accompanied by Citragupta, went to the abode of Brahmā. / He saw [Brahmā] seated, surrounded by manifest and unmanifest beings,

2.3.s:
vedāśrayaṃ jagadbījaṃ sarveṣāṃ prapitāmaham /
svabhavaṃ bhūtanilayamoṅkārākhyamakalmaṣam //
2.3.d:
वेदाश्रयं जगद्बीजं सर्वेषां प्रपितामहम् ।
स्वभवं भूतनिलयमोङ्काराख्यमकल्मषम् ॥
2.3.m: the refuge of the Vedas, the seed of the universe, the great-grandfather of all, / self-existent, the dwelling of all beings, named the syllable Om, stainless,

2.3.s:
śuciṃ śucipadaṃ haṃsaṃ brahmāṇaṃ darbhalāñchanam /
upāsyamānaṃ vividhairlokapālairdigīśvaraiḥ //
2.3.d:
शुचिं शुचिपदं हंसं ब्रह्माणं दर्भलाञ्छनम् ।
उपास्यमानं विविधैर्लोकपालैर्दिगीश्वरैः ॥
2.3.m: pure, of pure abode, the swan, Brahmā marked with darbha grass, / being worshiped by various world-guardians and lords of the quarters,

2.3.s:
itihāsapurāṇaiśca vedaurvegrahasaṃsthitaiḥ /
mūrtimadbhiḥ samudraiśya nadībhiśca sarovaraiḥ //
2.3.d:
इतिहासपुराणैश्च वेदौर्वेग्रहसंस्थितैः ।
मूर्तिमद्भिः समुद्रैश्य नदीभिश्च सरोवरैः ॥
2.3.m: and by the Itihāsas, Purāṇas, and Vedas standing embodied in the firmament, / and by embodied oceans, rivers, and lakes.

2.3.s:
dehadhṛgbhistathā vṛkṣairaśvatthādyairviśeṣataḥ /
vāpīkūpataḍāgādyairmūrtimadbhiśca parvataiḥ //
2.3.d:
देहधृग्भिस्तथा वृक्षैरश्वत्थाद्यैर्विशेषतः ।
वापीकूपतडागाद्यैर्मूर्तिमद्भिश्च पर्वतैः ॥
2.3.m: with trees bearing bodies, especially the aśvattha and others, / with step-wells, wells, ponds, and personified mountains,

2.3.s:
ahorātraistathā pakṣairmāsaiḥ saṃvatsarairdvijāḥ /
kalākāṣṭhānimeṣaiśca ṛtubhiścāyanairyugaiḥ //
2.3.d:
अहोरात्रैस्तथा पक्षैर्मासैः संवत्सरैर्द्विजाः ।
कलाकाष्ठानिमेषैश्च ऋतुभिश्चायनैर्युगैः ॥
2.3.m: with day-and-nights, fortnights, months, and years, O twice-born ones, / with kalās, kāṣṭhās, winks of the eye, seasons, solstices, and yugas,

2.3.s:
manvantaraistathā kalpairnimeṣairunmiṣairapi /
ṛkṣairyogaiśca karaṇaiḥ paurṇamāseṃdusaṃkṣayaiḥ //
2.3.d:
मन्वन्तरैस्तथा कल्पैर्निमेषैरुन्मिषैरपि ।
ऋक्षैर्योगैश्च करणैः पौर्णमासेंदुसंक्षयैः ॥
2.3.m: with manvantaras, kalpas, winkings, and open-eyed moments, / with constellations, yogas, karaṇas, full moons, and new moons,

2.3.s:
sukhairduḥkhaistathā dvandvairlābhālābhairjayājayaiḥ /
satyānṛtaiśca deveśo veṣṭito dharmapāvakaḥ //
2.3.d:
सुखैर्दुःखैस्तथा द्वन्द्वैर्लाभालाभैर्जयाजयैः ।
सत्यानृतैश्च देवेशो वेष्टितो धर्मपावकः ॥
2.3.m: with pleasures and pains, dualities, gains and losses, victories and defeats, / and with truths and untruths was the lord of gods, the fire of righteousness, surrounded.

2.3.s:
karmavidbhiśca puruṣairanupairupāsyate /
sattvena rajasā caiva tamasā ca pitāmahaḥ //
2.3.d:
कर्मविद्भिश्च पुरुषैरनुपैरुपास्यते ।
सत्त्वेन रजसा चैव तमसा च पितामहः ॥
2.3.m: The Grandfather was served by men knowledgeable in action, without peers, / and by goodness, passion, and darkness,

2.3.s:
śāntamūḍhātighoraiśca vikāraiḥ prākṛtairvibhuḥ /
vāyunā śleṣmapittābhyāṃ mūrtairātaṅkanāmabhiḥ //
2.3.d:
शान्तमूढातिघोरैश्च विकारैः प्राकृतैर्विभुः ।
वायुना श्लेष्मपित्ताभ्यां मूर्तैरातङ्कनामभिः ॥
2.3.m: and by peaceful, bewildered, and exceedingly dreadful modifications of nature, the omnipresent lord; / by wind, phlegm, and bile in embodied forms, named as afflictions,

2.3.s:
ānandena ca viśvātmā paradharmaṃ samāśritaḥ /
anuktairapi bhūtaiśca saṃvṛto lokakṛtsvayam //
2.3.d:
आनन्देन च विश्वात्मा परधर्मं समाश्रितः ।
अनुक्तैरपि भूतैश्च संवृतो लोककृत्स्वयम् ॥
2.3.m: and with bliss, the Soul of All, resting in the supreme state; / surrounded by elements, even those not mentioned, the Creator of the Worlds himself.

2.3.s:
duruktaiḥ kaṭuvākyādyairmūrtimadbhirupāsyate /
teṣāṃ madhye 'viśatsauriḥ savrīḍeva vadhūryathā //
2.3.d:
दुरुक्तैः कटुवाक्याद्यैर्मूर्तिमद्भिरुपास्यते ।
तेषां मध्ये ऽविशत्सौरिः सव्रीडेव वधूर्यथा ॥
2.3.m: He was served by harsh words, bitter speech, and the like in embodied forms. / In their midst entered the son of the Sun, like a bashful bride,

2.3.s:
vilokayannadhobhāgaṃ namravaktro vyadarśayat /
te praviṣṭaṃ yamaṃ dṛṣṭvā sakāyasthaṃ sanāradam //
2.3.d:
विलोकयन्नधोभागं नम्रवक्त्रो व्यदर्शयत् ।
ते प्रविष्टं यमं दृष्ट्वा सकायस्थं सनारदम् ॥
2.3.m: looking downwards, showing a bowed face. / Seeing Yama who had entered, accompanied by his scribe and with Nārada,

2.3.s:
vismitākṣā mithaḥ procuḥ kimayaṃ bhāskaristviha /
saṃprāpto hi lokakaraṃ draṣṭuṃ devaṃ pitāmaham //
2.3.d:
विस्मिताक्षा मिथः प्रोचुः किमयं भास्करिस्त्विह ।
संप्राप्तो हि लोककरं द्रष्टुं देवं पितामहम् ॥
2.3.m: with eyes full of astonishment, they spoke to one another: “Why has this son of the Sun / arrived here to see the god, the Grandfather, maker of the worlds?

2.3.s:
nirvyāpāraḥ kṣaṇaṃ nāsti yo 'yaṃ vyagro raveḥ sutaḥ /
so 'yamabhyāgataḥ kasmātkañcitkṣemaṃ divaukasām //
2.3.d:
निर्व्यापारः क्षणं नास्ति यो ऽयं व्यग्रो रवेः सुतः ।
सो ऽयमभ्यागतः कस्मात्कञ्चित्क्षेमं दिवौकसाम् ॥
2.3.m: He who is the son of the Sun is never idle for a moment, ever busy. / Why has he come? Is all well with the heaven-dwellers?

2.3.s:
āścaryātiśayaṃ manye yanmārjitapaṭastvayam /
lekhakaḥ samanuprāpto dainyena mahatānvitaḥ //
2.3.d:
आश्चर्यातिशयं मन्ये यन्मार्जितपटस्त्वयम् ।
लेखकः समनुप्राप्तो दैन्येन महतान्वितः ॥
2.3.m: I deem it a great wonder that this scribe, / his scroll erased, has arrived, overwhelmed with great despondency.

2.3.s:
na kenacitpaṭo hyasya mārjito 'bhūcca dharmiṇā /
yanna dṛṣṭaṃ śrunta vāpi tadihaiva pradṛśyate //
2.3.d:
न केनचित्पटो ह्यस्य मार्जितो ऽभूच्च धर्मिणा ।
यन्न दृष्टं श्रुन्त वापि तदिहैव प्रदृश्यते ॥
2.3.m: Indeed, his scroll was never erased by any righteous man! / What was never seen or even heard of is seen right here.”

2.3.s:
evamuccaratāṃ teṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ kṛtaśāsanaḥ /
nipapātāgrato viprā brahmaṇo ravinandanaḥ //
2.3.d:
एवमुच्चरतां तेषां भूतानां कृतशासनः ।
निपपाताग्रतो विप्रा ब्रह्मणो रविनन्दनः ॥
2.3.m: As those beings were saying this, the ruler who had fulfilled his command, / the son of the Sun, O brahmins, fell down before Brahmā

2.3.s:
mūlacchinno yathā śākhī trāhi trāhīti saṃrudan /
paribhūto 'smi deveśa yanmārjitapaṭaḥ kṛtaḥ //
2.3.d:
मूलच्छिन्नो यथा शाखी त्राहि त्राहीति संरुदन् ।
परिभूतो ऽस्मि देवेश यन्मार्जितपटः कृतः ॥
2.3.m: like a tree severed at its root, crying out, “Save me! Save me! / I have been humiliated, O Lord of gods, since my scroll has been wiped clean!

2.3.s:
tvayā nāthena vidhuraṃ paśyāmi kamalāsana /
evaṃ bruvansa niśceṣṭo babhūva dvijasaṃttamāḥ //
2.3.d:
त्वया नाथेन विधुरं पश्यामि कमलासन ।
एवं ब्रुवन्स निश्चेष्टो बभूव द्विजसंत्तमाः ॥
2.3.m: With you as my protector, O Lotus-seated one, I find myself helpless!” / Saying this, he became motionless, O best of the twice-born.

2.3.s:
tato halahalāśabdaḥ sabhāyāṃ samavartata /
yor'thaṃ rodayate lokānsarvānsthāvaraja gamān //
2.3.d:
ततो हलहलाशब्दः सभायां समवर्तत ।
योर्ऽथं रोदयते लोकान्सर्वान्स्थावरज गमान् ॥
2.3.m: Then an uproar arose in the assembly: / “He who makes all the worlds of moving and unmoving beings weep,

2.3.s:
so 'yaṃ roditi duḥkhārtaḥ kasmādvaivasvato yamaḥ /
athavā satyagātheyaṃ laukikī pratibhāti naḥ //
2.3.d:
सो ऽयं रोदिति दुःखार्तः कस्माद्वैवस्वतो यमः ।
अथवा सत्यगाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति नः ॥
2.3.m: why does this Yama, son of Vivasvat, weep, stricken with grief? / Or rather, this worldly saying seems true to us:

2.3.s:
janasantāpakartā yaḥ so 'cireṇopatapyate /
nahi duṣkṛtakarmā hi naraḥ prāpnoti śobhanam //
2.3.d:
जनसन्तापकर्ता यः सो ऽचिरेणोपतप्यते ।
नहि दुष्कृतकर्मा हि नरः प्राप्नोति शोभनम् ॥
2.3.m: ‘He who causes torment to people is himself tormented before long; / for a man of wicked deeds never attains good fortune.’”

2.3.s:
tato nivārayāmāsa vāyusteṣāṃ vacastadā /
lokānāṃ samacittānāṃ mataṃ jñātvā hi vedhasaḥ //
2.3.d:
ततो निवारयामास वायुस्तेषां वचस्तदा ।
लोकानां समचित्तानां मतं ज्ञात्वा हि वेधसः ॥
2.3.m: Then Vāyu silenced their words at that time, / knowing indeed the will of the Creator for the beings of even minds.

2.3.s:
nivārya śaṅkāṃ mārtaṇḍiṃ śanairutthāpayan vibhuḥ /
bhujābhyāṃ sādhupīnābhyāṃ lokamūrtirudāradhīḥ //
2.3.d:
निवार्य शङ्कां मार्तण्डिं शनैरुत्थापयन् विभुः ।
भुजाभ्यां साधुपीनाभ्यां लोकमूर्तिरुदारधीः ॥
2.3.m: Dispelling the doubt, slowly raising the son of Mārtaṇḍa / with his well-rounded arms, the all-pervading lord of noble mind, whose form is the world,

2.3.s:
vihvalaṃ taṃ palāyantamāsane saṃnyaveśayat /
sakāyasthamuvācedaṃ vyomamūrtiṃ raveḥ sutam //
2.3.d:
विह्वलं तं पलायन्तमासने संन्यवेशयत् ।
सकायस्थमुवाचेदं व्योममूर्तिं रवेः सुतम् ॥
2.3.m: seated that distraught, fleeing one upon a seat. / The one whose form is space said this to the son of the Sun, accompanied by his scribe:

2.3.s:
kena tvamabhibhūto 'si kena sthānādvivāsitaḥ /
kenāpamārjito devapaṭo lokapaṭastava //
2.3.d:
केन त्वमभिभूतो ऽसि केन स्थानाद्विवासितः ।
केनापमार्जितो देवपटो लोकपटस्तव ॥
2.3.m: “By whom have you been overcome? By whom expelled from your post? / By whom has your divine register, the scroll of the world, been wiped clean?

2.3.s:
brūhi sarvamaśeṣeṇa kuśaketurvadatvayam /
yaḥ prabhustāta sarveṣāṃ sa te kartā samunnatim /
apaneṣyati mārtaṇḍe duḥkhaṃ hṛdayasaṃsthitam //
2.3.d:
ब्रूहि सर्वमशेषेण कुशकेतुर्वदत्वयम् ।
यः प्रभुस्तात सर्वेषां स ते कर्ता समुन्नतिम् ।
अपनेष्यति मार्तण्डे दुःखं हृदयसंस्थितम् ॥
2.3.m: Tell everything in full; let this Kuśaketu speak. / He who is the master of all, dear one, he will grant your elevation / and will remove the sorrow residing in your heart, O son of Mārtaṇḍa.”

2.3.s:
sa evamuktastu prabhañjanena dineśasūnustamatho babhāṣe /
vilokya vaktraṃ kuśaketusūnoḥ sagadgadaṃ mandamudīrayanvacaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottare bhāge yamasya brahmalokagamanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.3.d:
स एवमुक्तस्तु प्रभञ्जनेन दिनेशसूनुस्तमथो बभाषे ।
विलोक्य वक्त्रं कुशकेतुसूनोः सगद्गदं मन्दमुदीरयन्वचः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरे भागे यमस्य ब्रह्मलोकगमनं नाम तृतीयो ऽध्यायः
2.3.m:
Thus addressed by the Wind, the son of the Day-lord then spoke to him, / looking at the face of the son of Brahmā, uttering words slowly with faltering voice:

Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Yama’s Journey to the World of Brahmā', in the latter part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.4.s:
yama uvāca
śṛṇu me vacanaṃ nātha pitāmaha pitāmaha /
maraṇādadhikaṃ deva yatpratāpasya khaṇḍanam //
2.4.d:
यम उवाच
शृणु मे वचनं नाथ पितामह पितामह ।
मरणादधिकं देव यत्प्रतापस्य खण्डनम् ॥
2.4.m: Yama said: / “Hear my words, O lord, O Grandfather, O Grandfather! / Worse than death, O god, is the destruction of one's authority.

2.4.s:
nispṛho nācaredyastu niyogaṃ padmasaṃbhava /
andhakūpe nipatati sa cāśu narake dhruvam //
2.4.d:
निस्पृहो नाचरेद्यस्तु नियोगं पद्मसंभव ।
अन्धकूपे निपतति स चाशु नरके ध्रुवम् ॥
2.4.m: He who, being indifferent, does not carry out his appointed duty, O Lotus-born one, / falls into a blind well and surely into hell swiftly.

2.4.s:
niyogī na niyogaṃ yaḥ karoti kamalāsana /
prabhorvittaṃ samaśnāti sa bhavetkāṣṭhakīṭakaḥ //
2.4.d:
नियोगी न नियोगं यः करोति कमलासन ।
प्रभोर्वित्तं समश्नाति स भवेत्काष्ठकीटकः ॥
2.4.m: An appointed servant who does not perform his duty, O Lotus-seated one, / and consumes his master's wealth, becomes a woodworm.

2.4.s:
yo 'śnāti lobhādvittāni prajābhyo vā mahīpateḥ /
niyogī narakaṃ yāti yāvatkalpaśatatrayam //
2.4.d:
यो ऽश्नाति लोभाद्वित्तानि प्रजाभ्यो वा महीपतेः ।
नियोगी नरकं याति यावत्कल्पशतत्रयम् ॥
2.4.m: An appointed official who greedily consumes the wealth of the king or of the subjects / goes to hell for three hundred kalpas.

2.4.s:
ātmakāryaparo yastu svāminaṃ ca viluṃpati /
bhavedveśmani mandātmā ākhuḥ kalpaśatatrayam //
2.4.d:
आत्मकार्यपरो यस्तु स्वामिनं च विलुंपति ।
भवेद्वेश्मनि मन्दात्मा आखुः कल्पशतत्रयम् ॥
2.4.m: He who is devoted to his own ends and defrauds his master, / that dull-witted soul becomes a rat in the house for three hundred kalpas.

2.4.s:
niyogī yastu vai bhūtvā ātmaveśmani bhokṣyati /
bhṛtyānvai karmakaraṇe rājño mārjāratāṃ vrajet //
2.4.d:
नियोगी यस्तु वै भूत्वा आत्मवेश्मनि भोक्ष्यति ।
भृत्यान्वै कर्मकरणे राज्ञो मार्जारतां व्रजेत् ॥
2.4.m: And he who, having become an official, eats the servants of the king / in his own house during the execution of work, becomes a cat.

2.4.s:
so 'haṃ deva tavādeśāt prajā dharmeṇa śāsayan /
puṇyena puṇyakartāraṃ pāpaṃ pāpena karmaṇā //
2.4.d:
सो ऽहं देव तवादेशात् प्रजा धर्मेण शासयन् ।
पुण्येन पुण्यकर्तारं पापं पापेन कर्मणा ॥
2.4.m: Such as I was, O god, by your command ruling the subjects according to righteousness, / [treating] the doer of merit with merit, and the sinner according to sinful deeds,

2.4.s:
samyagvicārya munibhirgharmaśāstrādibhirvibho /
kalpādau vartamānasya yāvadyāvaddinaṃ tava //
2.4.d:
सम्यग्विचार्य मुनिभिर्घर्मशास्त्रादिभिर्विभो ।
कल्पादौ वर्तमानस्य यावद्यावद्दिनं तव ॥
2.4.m: having deliberated well with the sages and the treatises on dharma, O all-pervading lord, / abiding [thus] from the beginning of the kalpa as long as your day lasts—

2.4.s:
so 'haṃ tvadīyena vibho niyogenaiva śaknuyām /
kartuṃ rukmāṅgadenādya parābhūto hi bhūbhujā //
2.4.d:
सो ऽहं त्वदीयेन विभो नियोगेनैव शक्नुयाम् ।
कर्तुं रुक्माङ्गदेनाद्य पराभूतो हि भूभुजा ॥
2.4.m: such as I am, O all-pervading lord, able only by your appointment / to act, I have been defeated today by King Rukmāṅgada!

2.4.s:
bhayādyasya jagannātha pṛthivī sāgarāṃbarā /
na bhuṅkte vāsare viṣṇoḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśane //
2.4.d:
भयाद्यस्य जगन्नाथ पृथिवी सागरांबरा ।
न भुङ्क्ते वासरे विष्णोः सर्वपापप्रणाशने ॥
2.4.m: Out of fear of him, O Lord of the universe, the earth clothed in oceans / does not eat on the day of Viṣṇu that destroys all sins.

2.4.s:
vihāya sarvadharmāṃstu vihāya pitṛpūjanam /
vihāya devapūjāṃ ca tīrthasnānādikastriyām //
2.4.d:
विहाय सर्वधर्मांस्तु विहाय पितृपूजनम् ।
विहाय देवपूजां च तीर्थस्नानादिकस्त्रियाम् ॥
2.4.m: Abandoning all religious duties, abandoning the worship of the ancestors, / abandoning the worship of gods, and the acts such as bathing at sacred fords,

2.4.s:
yogasāṃkhyāvubhau tyaktvā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca mānada /
tyaktvā svādhyāyahomāṃśca kṛtvā pāpāni bhūriśaḥ //
2.4.d:
योगसांख्यावुभौ त्यक्त्वा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च मानद ।
त्यक्त्वा स्वाध्यायहोमांश्च कृत्वा पापानि भूरिशः ॥
2.4.m: leaving behind both Yoga and Sāṃkhya, knowledge and what is to be known, O giver of honor, / leaving behind self-study and fire oblations, and having committed sins abundantly,

2.4.s:
prayānti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokamupoṣya harivāsaram /
manujāḥ pitṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ tathaiva ca pitāmahaiḥ //
2.4.d:
प्रयान्ति वैष्णवं लोकमुपोष्य हरिवासरम् ।
मनुजाः पितृभिः सार्द्धं तथैव च पितामहैः ॥
2.4.m: humans, by fasting on the day of Hari, go to the world of Viṣṇu / along with their fathers, and likewise with their grandfathers;

2.4.s:
teṣāmapīha pitaraḥ pitṝṇāṃ pitarastathā /
tathā mātāmahā yānti māturye janakādayaḥ //
2.4.d:
तेषामपीह पितरः पितॄणां पितरस्तथा ।
तथा मातामहा यान्ति मातुर्ये जनकादयः ॥
2.4.m: and even their fathers, and the fathers of their fathers, / and maternal grandfathers, the maternal relatives beginning with the mother's father,

2.4.s:
teṣāmapi janetāro janitṝṇāṃ hi pūrvajāḥ /
etadduḥkhaṃ punardeva mama marmavibhedanam //
2.4.d:
तेषामपि जनेतारो जनितॄणां हि पूर्वजाः ।
एतद्दुःखं पुनर्देव मम मर्मविभेदनम् ॥
2.4.m: and also their progenitors, the forebears of those progenitors go. / Furthermore, O god, this sorrow pierces my vital parts:

2.4.s:
priyāyāḥ pitaro yānti mārjayitvā lipiṃ mama /
pitṝṇāṃ bījato yasmāddhātryā kukṣau dhṛto yataḥ //
2.4.d:
प्रियायाः पितरो यान्ति मार्जयित्वा लिपिं मम ।
पितॄणां बीजतो यस्माद्धात्र्या कुक्षौ धृतो यतः ॥
2.4.m: the ancestors of one's beloved wife go, having wiped clean my writing! / Because of the seed of the fathers, and because one is borne in the womb of the mother,

2.4.s:
yadekaḥ kurute karma tadekenaiva bhujyate /
tato 'nyasya kṛtaṃ brahmanbījaṃ dhātrīsamudbhavam //
2.4.d:
यदेकः कुरुते कर्म तदेकेनैव भुज्यते ।
ततो ऽन्यस्य कृतं ब्रह्मन्बीजं धात्रीसमुद्भवम् ॥
2.4.m: the karma that one person performs is experienced by that one alone; / hence, O Brahmā, how can the seed produced from the mother save another?

2.4.s:
tārayetsa ubhau pakṣau yatpiṇḍo yasya vigrahaḥ /
na bhāryāyā bhavedvījaṃ na bhāryā kukṣidhāriṇī //
2.4.d:
तारयेत्स उभौ पक्षौ यत्पिण्डो यस्य विग्रहः ।
न भार्याया भवेद्वीजं न भार्या कुक्षिधारिणी ॥
2.4.m: He saves both families, whose ancestral rice-ball and whose body it is; / but the seed does not belong to the wife, nor does the wife bear [the husband's ancestral line] in her womb.

2.4.s:
kathaṃ tasyā jagannātha pakṣo yāti paraṃ padam /
jāmātuḥ puṇyamāhātmyattina me śiraso rujā //
2.4.d:
कथं तस्या जगन्नाथ पक्षो याति परं पदम् ।
जामातुः पुण्यमाहात्म्यत्तिन मे शिरसो रुजा ॥
2.4.m: How does her family go to the supreme abode, O Lord of the universe? / Because of the greatness of the son-in-law's merit—this causes me a headache!

2.4.s:
na me prayojanaṃ deva niyogenedṛśena vai /
ekādaśyupavāsī yaḥ sa māṃ tyaktvā vrajeddharim //
2.4.d:
न मे प्रयोजनं देव नियोगेनेदृशेन वै ।
एकादश्युपवासी यः स मां त्यक्त्वा व्रजेद्धरिम् ॥
2.4.m: I have no use, O god, for an appointment of this kind, / for whoever fasts on the eleventh day bypasses me and goes to Hari.

2.4.s:
kulatrayaṃ samuddhṛtya ātmanā saha padmaja /
tyaktvā tu māmakaṃ mārgaṃ prayāti harimandiram //
2.4.d:
कुलत्रयं समुद्धृत्य आत्मना सह पद्मज ।
त्यक्त्वा तु मामकं मार्गं प्रयाति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.4.m: Delivering three lineages along with himself, O Lotus-born one, / he bypasses my path and goes to the abode of Hari.”

2.4.s:
na yajñaistādṛśairdeva gatiṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ /
na tīrthairnāpi dānairvā na vratairviṣṇuvarjitaiḥ //
2.4.d:
न यज्ञैस्तादृशैर्देव गतिं प्राप्नोति मानवः ।
न तीर्थैर्नापि दानैर्वा न व्रतैर्विष्णुवर्जितैः ॥
2.4.m: A human does not attain that state through sacrifices of that kind, O lord, / nor through sacred fords, nor through gifts, nor through observances devoid of Viṣṇu.

2.4.s:
na jale pāvake vāpi mṛtaḥ prāpnoti tāṃ gatim /
yogena saṃpraṇaṣṭo vā bhṛgupātena vā vidhe //
2.4.d:
न जले पावके वापि मृतः प्राप्नोति तां गतिम् ।
योगेन संप्रणष्टो वा भृगुपातेन वा विधे ॥
2.4.m: One dying in water or in fire does not attain that state, / nor one perished through yoga, nor by falling from a cliff, O ordainer.

2.4.s:
tādṛśīṃ na gatiṃ yāti yādṛśīṃ vaiṣṇavavratī /
gatiṃ matimatāṃ śreṣṭha satyametadudīritam //
2.4.d:
तादृशीं न गतिं याति यादृशीं वैष्णवव्रती ।
गतिं मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ सत्यमेतदुदीरितम् ॥
2.4.m: One does not go to that state to which one observing the Vaiṣṇava vow goes; / this truth has been spoken, O best of the intelligent.

2.4.s:
harerdine dhātṛphalāṅgalipto vimuktavāñchārasabhojano naraḥ /
prayāti loke dharaṇīdharasya viduṣṭakarmāpi manuṣyajanmā //
2.4.d:
हरेर्दिने धातृफलाङ्गलिप्तो विमुक्तवाञ्छारसभोजनो नरः ।
प्रयाति लोके धरणीधरस्य विदुष्टकर्मापि मनुष्यजन्मा ॥
2.4.m: A man smeared with myrobalan fruit on the day of Hari, who has renounced eating pleasant delicacies, / goes to the realm of the Bearer of the Earth, even if born a mortal of wicked deeds.

2.4.s:
so 'haṃ nirāśo bhuvi hīnakarmā tavāgataḥ pādasarojayugmam /
vijñapti mātrābhayadāptikālaṃ kuruṣva sargasthitināsahetoḥ //
2.4.d:
सो ऽहं निराशो भुवि हीनकर्मा तवागतः पादसरोजयुग्मम् ।
विज्ञप्ति मात्राभयदाप्तिकालं कुरुष्व सर्गस्थितिनासहेतोः ॥
2.4.m: Such as I am, hopeless on earth, with my function ruined, I have come to your pair of lotus feet; / make it a time of attaining fearlessness merely through my plea, for the sake of creation, maintenance, and destruction.

2.4.s:
māsyustadā pāpakṛto vihīnā yanmāmakairbhūtagaṇairmanuṣyāḥ /
niyantritāḥ śṛṅkhalarajjubandhanaiḥ samīpagā me vaśagā bhaveyuḥ //
2.4.d:
मास्युस्तदा पापकृतो विहीना यन्मामकैर्भूतगणैर्मनुष्याः ।
नियन्त्रिताः शृङ्खलरज्जुबन्धनैः समीपगा मे वशगा भवेयुः ॥
2.4.m: May those sinners not be absent when men, bound by my legions of spirits / with ropes and chains, should approach me and be under my control.

2.4.s:
bhagnastu mārgo ravitāpayukto yadviṣṇusaṃghairatitīvrahastaiḥ /
vimucya kuṃbhīṃ sakalo janaughaḥ prayāti taddhāma parātparasya //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge yamavākyaṃ nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
2.4.d:
भग्नस्तु मार्गो रवितापयुक्तो यद्विष्णुसंघैरतितीव्रहस्तैः ।
विमुच्य कुंभीं सकलो जनौघः प्रयाति तद्धाम परात्परस्य ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे यमवाक्यं नाम चतुर्थो ऽध्यायः
2.4.m:
The path scorched by the sun's heat has been broken by the hosts of Viṣṇu with their very swift hands; / having abandoned the Kumbhī cauldron, the whole multitude of people proceeds to that abode of the higher than the highest.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, named "The Speech of Yama," in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.5.s:
yama uvāca
ghṛṣṭatāṃ samanuprāptaḥ panthā devasya cakriṇaḥ /
acchidrairgamyanānaiśca naraistribhuvanārcita //
2.5.d:
यम उवाच
घृष्टतां समनुप्राप्तः पन्था देवस्य चक्रिणः ।
अच्छिद्रैर्गम्यनानैश्च नरैस्त्रिभुवनार्चित ॥
2.5.m: Yama said: / The path of the Discus-bearing god has become worn smooth / by flawless men who are traveling along it, O you who are worshipped in the three worlds!

2.5.s:
apramāṇamahaṃ manye lokaṃ viṣṇorjagatpate /
yo na pūryati lokaighaiḥ sarvasatvasaroruhaiḥ //
2.5.d:
अप्रमाणमहं मन्ये लोकं विष्णोर्जगत्पते ।
यो न पूर्यति लोकैघैः सर्वसत्वसरोरुहैः ॥
2.5.m: I consider the world of Viṣṇu to be measureless, O lord of the world, / which does not become full with the floods of worlds, the lotuses of all living beings.

2.5.s:
mādhavāvasathainaiva samastena pitāmaha /
svakarmasthā vikarmasthāḥ śucayo 'śucayo 'pi vā //
2.5.d:
माधवावसथैनैव समस्तेन पितामह ।
स्वकर्मस्था विकर्मस्थाः शुचयो ऽशुचयो ऽपि वा ॥
2.5.m: By the entire abode of Mādhava alone, O grandfather, / whether abiding in their own duties or in unlawful acts, whether pure or impure,

2.5.s:
upoṣya vāsaraṃ viṣṇorlokaṃ yānti nṛpājñayā /
so 'smākaṃ hi mahān śatrurbhavatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ //
2.5.d:
उपोष्य वासरं विष्णोर्लोकं यान्ति नृपाज्ञया ।
सो ऽस्माकं हि महान् शत्रुर्भवतां च विशेषतः ॥
2.5.m: having fasted on the day of Viṣṇu by the king's order, they go to his world. / Indeed, he is a great enemy of ours, and especially of yours.

2.5.s:
nigrāhyo jagatāṃnātha bhavennāstyatra saṃśayaḥ /
tena varṣasahasreṇa śāsitaṃ kṣitimaṇḍalam //
2.5.d:
निग्राह्यो जगतांनाथ भवेन्नास्त्यत्र संशयः ।
तेन वर्षसहस्रेण शासितं क्षितिमण्डलम् ॥
2.5.m: He should be restrained, O lord of the worlds; there is no doubt about this. / By him the circle of the earth has been ruled for a thousand years.

2.5.s:
aprameyo jano nīto vaiṣṇavaṃ harivallabham /
āropayitvā garuḍe kṛtvā rūpaṃ caturbhujam //
2.5.d:
अप्रमेयो जनो नीतो वैष्णवं हरिवल्लभम् ।
आरोपयित्वा गरुडे कृत्वा रूपं चतुर्भुजम् ॥
2.5.m: Immeasurable numbers of people have been led to the Vaiṣṇava realm dear to Hari, / mounted upon Garuḍa, having assumed a four-armed form,

2.5.s:
pītavastrasusaṃvītaṃ sragviṇaṃ cārulopanam /
yadi sthāsyati deveśa mādhavyāṃ mādhavapriyaḥ //
2.5.d:
पीतवस्त्रसुसंवीतं स्रग्विणं चारुलोपनम् ।
यदि स्थास्यति देवेश माधव्यां माधवप्रियः ॥
2.5.m: dressed in fine yellow garments, wearing garlands and pleasing ointments. / If he remains thus, O lord of gods, devoted to Mādhava on the day of Mādhava,

2.5.s:
samastaṃ neṣyate lokaṃ viṣṇoḥ padamanāmayam /
eṣa daṇḍaḥ paṭo hyeṣa tava padbhyāṃ visarjitaḥ //
2.5.d:
समस्तं नेष्यते लोकं विष्णोः पदमनामयम् ।
एष दण्डः पटो ह्येष तव पद्भ्यां विसर्जितः ॥
2.5.m: he will lead the entire world to the disease-free abode of Viṣṇu. / This staff and this cloth have been cast down before your feet!

2.5.s:
lokapālatvamatulaṃ mārjita tena bhūbhujā /
rukmāṅgadena deveśa dhanyā sā sa dhṛto yayā //
2.5.d:
लोकपालत्वमतुलं मार्जित तेन भूभुजा ।
रुक्माङ्गदेन देवेश धन्या सा स धृतो यया ॥
2.5.m: Incomparable guardianship of the worlds was wiped away by that king, / Rukmāṅgada, O lord of the gods; blessed is she by whom he was carried [in the womb]!

2.5.s:
sarvaduḥkhavināśāya mātrṛjāto guṇādhikaḥ /
kimapatyena jātena mātuḥ kleśakareṇa hi //
2.5.d:
सर्वदुःखविनाशाय मात्रृजातो गुणाधिकः ।
किमपत्येन जातेन मातुः क्लेशकरेण हि ॥
2.5.m: A son born from a mother superior in virtue brings about the destruction of all suffering. / What is the use of an offspring born who only causes affliction to his mother?

2.5.s:
yo na tāpayate śatrūn jyeṣṭhe māsi yathā raviḥ /
vṛthāśūlā hi jananī jātā deva kuputriṇī //
2.5.d:
यो न तापयते शत्रून् ज्येष्ठे मासि यथा रविः ।
वृथाशूला हि जननी जाता देव कुपुत्रिणी ॥
2.5.m: He who does not scorch his enemies like the sun in the month of Jyeṣṭha— / vain were his mother's labor-pains; she has become a mother of a wicked son, O god.

2.5.s:
yasya na sphurate kīrtirghanastheva śatahradā /
yaḥ piturnoddharetpakṣaṃ vidyayā vā balena vā //
2.5.d:
यस्य न स्फुरते कीर्तिर्घनस्थेव शतह्रदा ।
यः पितुर्नोद्धरेत्पक्षं विद्यया वा बलेन वा ॥
2.5.m: He whose fame does not flash like lightning in a cloud, / who does not raise up his father's side by learning or by strength—

2.5.s:
māturjaṭharajo rogaḥ sa prasūto dharātale /
dharme cārthe ca kāme ca pratīpo yo bhavetsutaḥ //
2.5.d:
मातुर्जठरजो रोगः स प्रसूतो धरातले ।
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च प्रतीपो यो भवेत्सुतः ॥
2.5.m: he is merely a disease of the womb born to his mother on the surface of the earth. / A son who is opposed to virtue, wealth, and pleasure

2.5.s:
mātṛhā procyate sadbhirvṛthā tasyaiva jīvitam /
ekā hi vīrasūreva virañce nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.5.d:
मातृहा प्रोच्यते सद्भिर्वृथा तस्यैव जीवितम् ।
एका हि वीरसूरेव विरञ्चे नात्र संशयः ॥
2.5.m: is declared by the virtuous to be a killer of his mother; in vain is his life. / She alone is the mother of a hero, O Virañci, there is no doubt here,

2.5.s:
yayā rukmāṅgado jāto mallipemarjjanāya vai /
nedaṃ vyavasthitaṃ deva kṣitau kenāpi bhūbhujā //
2.5.d:
यया रुक्माङ्गदो जातो मल्लिपेमर्ज्जनाय वै ।
नेदं व्यवस्थितं देव क्षितौ केनापि भूभुजा ॥
2.5.m: by whom Rukmāṅgada was born to wipe away the host of wrestling champions. / Such an arrangement was never instituted by any king on earth, O god.

2.5.s:
purāṇe 'pi jagannātha na śrutaṃ paṭamārjanam /
so 'haṃ na jāṃ mi kadācidāśa dṛṣṭvā kṣirīśaṃ harisevane sthitam /
pravādamānaṃ paṭahaṃ sughoraṃ pralopamānaṃ mamaviśmamārgam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge yamavilāpanaṃ nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.5.d:
पुराणे ऽपि जगन्नाथ न श्रुतं पटमार्जनम् ।
सो ऽहं न जां मि कदाचिदाश दृष्ट्वा क्षिरीशं हरिसेवने स्थितम् ।
प्रवादमानं पटहं सुघोरं प्रलोपमानं ममविश्ममार्गम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे यमविलापनं नाम पञ्चमो ऽध्यायः
2.5.m:
Even in the Purāṇas, O lord of the world, no wiping out of the cloth has been heard of. / Such as I am, I do not know... having seen the king intent upon the worship of Hari, / beating the terrible war-drum and destroying my universal path.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, named "The Lamentation of Yama," in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.6.s:
brahmovāca
kimāścaryaṃ tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ vā khidyate bhavān /
sadguṇeṣu ca saṃtāpaḥ sa tāpo maraṇāntikaḥ //
2.6.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
किमाश्चर्यं त्वया दृष्टं कथं वा खिद्यते भवान् ।
सद्गुणेषु च संतापः स तापो मरणान्तिकः ॥
2.6.m: Brahmā said: / What wonder have you seen, or why are you grieving? / Torment felt over good virtues is a torment that ends in death.

2.6.s:
yasyoccāraṇamātreṇa prāpyate paramaṃ padam /
tamupoṣya kathaṃ saure na gacchati narastviti //
2.6.d:
यस्योच्चारणमात्रेण प्राप्यते परमं पदम् ।
तमुपोष्य कथं सौरे न गच्छति नरस्त्विति ॥
2.6.m: Through the mere utterance of whose name the supreme abode is reached— / having fasted for him, O son of the Sun, how should a mortal not go [there]?

2.6.s:
eko hi kṛṣṇasya kṛtaḥ praṇāmo daśāśvamedhāvabhṛthena tulyaḥ /
daśāśvamedhī punareti janma kaṣṇapraṇāmī na punarbhavāya //
2.6.d:
एको हि कृष्णस्य कृतः प्रणामो दशाश्वमेधावभृथेन तुल्यः ।
दशाश्वमेधी पुनरेति जन्म कष्णप्रणामी न पुनर्भवाय ॥
2.6.m: A single bow made to Kṛṣṇa is equal to the concluding bath of ten horse-sacrifices; / one who performs ten horse-sacrifices is born again, but one who bows to Kṛṣṇa is not [born] for rebirth.

2.6.s:
kurukṣetreṇa kiṃ tasya kiṃ kāśyā virajena vā /
jihvāgre vartate yasya harirityakṣaradvayam //
2.6.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रेण किं तस्य किं काश्या विरजेन वा ।
जिह्वाग्रे वर्तते यस्य हरिरित्यक्षरद्वयम् ॥
2.6.m: What need has he of Kurukṣetra, what of Kāśī, or of Viraja, / upon the tip of whose tongue rests the two syllables "Ha-ri"?

2.6.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ śvapacīṃ gacchan viśeṣeṇa rajasvalām /
annamaśnansurāpakvaṃ maraṇe yo hariṃ smaret //
2.6.d:
ब्राह्मणः श्वपचीं गच्छन् विशेषेण रजस्वलाम् ।
अन्नमश्नन्सुरापक्वं मरणे यो हरिं स्मरेत् ॥
2.6.m: A brāhmaṇa who goes with an outcaste woman, especially one in her courses, / or who eats food cooked in liquor—if at death he remembers Hari,

2.6.s:
abhakṣyāgamyayorjātaṃ vihāya pāpasaṃcayam /
sa yāti viṣṇusāyujyaṃ vimukto bhavabandhanaiḥ //
2.6.d:
अभक्ष्यागम्ययोर्जातं विहाय पापसंचयम् ।
स याति विष्णुसायुज्यं विमुक्तो भवबन्धनैः ॥
2.6.m: abandoning the heap of sins born of inedible food and forbidden women, / he goes to communion with Viṣṇu, released from worldly bonds.

2.6.s:
yannāmoccāraṇānmokṣaḥ kathaṃ na tadupoṣaṇe /
yasminsaṃgīyate so 'pi cintyate puruṣottamaḥ //
2.6.d:
यन्नामोच्चारणान्मोक्षः कथं न तदुपोषणे ।
यस्मिन्संगीयते सो ऽपि चिन्त्यते पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
2.6.m: When liberation comes from uttering his name, how could it not from fasting for him, / in which that Puruṣottama is sung and also meditated upon?

2.6.s:
līlayā coccareddevaṃ śṛṇuyācca janārdanam /
gaṅgāṃbhaḥ pūtapuṇyatve sa naraḥ samatāṃ vrajet //
2.6.d:
लीलया चोच्चरेद्देवं शृणुयाच्च जनार्दनम् ।
गङ्गांभः पूतपुण्यत्वे स नरः समतां व्रजेत् ॥
2.6.m: If one should playfully utter the god or listen to [the praises of] Janārdana, / that man attains equality [with one having] merit purified by the water of the Gaṅgā.

2.6.s:
asmākaṃ jagatāṃnātho janmadaḥ puruṣottamaḥ /
kathaṃ śāsati durmedhāstasya vāsarasevinam //
2.6.d:
अस्माकं जगतांनाथो जन्मदः पुरुषोत्तमः ।
कथं शासति दुर्मेधास्तस्य वासरसेविनम् ॥
2.6.m: Puruṣottama, the lord of the worlds, is our progenitor; / how could foolish people punish someone who observes his holy day?

2.6.s:
yastvaṃ na cūrṇitastaistu yastvaṃ baddho na tairdṛḍham /
tadasmākaṃ kṛtaṃ mānaṃ me tattvaṃ nāvabudhyase //
2.6.d:
यस्त्वं न चूर्णितस्तैस्तु यस्त्वं बद्धो न तैर्दृढम् ।
तदस्माकं कृतं मानं मे तत्त्वं नावबुध्यसे ॥
2.6.m: That you were not crushed by them, that you were not firmly bound by them— / that was respect shown to me; you do not understand my true nature.

2.6.s:
yo niyogī na jānāti nṛpabhaktānvarān kṣitau /
kṛtsnāyāsena saṃyuktaḥ sa tairnigrāhyate punaḥ //
2.6.d:
यो नियोगी न जानाति नृपभक्तान्वरान् क्षितौ ।
कृत्स्नायासेन संयुक्तः स तैर्निग्राह्यते पुनः ॥
2.6.m: An officer who does not recognize the king's foremost devotees on earth / and acts with total violence is, in turn, restrained by them.

2.6.s:
rājeṣṭā na niyoktavyāḥ sāparādhā niyoginā /
svāmiprasādātsiddhāste vininyurvvai niyoginam //
2.6.d:
राजेष्टा न नियोक्तव्याः सापराधा नियोगिना ।
स्वामिप्रसादात्सिद्धास्ते विनिन्युर्व्वै नियोगिनम् ॥
2.6.m: Those who are dear to the king, even if guilty of an offense, must not be disciplined by an officer; / perfected through the master's grace, they would discipline that officer himself.

2.6.s:
evaṃ hi pāpakartāraḥ praṇatā ye janārdane /
kathaṃ saṃyamitā teṣāṃ bālyādbhāskaranandana //
2.6.d:
एवं हि पापकर्तारः प्रणता ये जनार्दने ।
कथं संयमिता तेषां बाल्याद्भास्करनन्दन ॥
2.6.m: Thus, indeed, regarding evildoers who bow down to Janārdana: / how could there be a punisher of them, O son of Bhāskara, through childishness?

2.6.s:
śaivairbhāskarabhaktairvā madbhaktairvā divākare /
karomi tava sāhāyyaṃ haribhaktairna bhāskare //
2.6.d:
शैवैर्भास्करभक्तैर्वा मद्भक्तैर्वा दिवाकरे ।
करोमि तव साहाय्यं हरिभक्तैर्न भास्करे ॥
2.6.m: Against devotees of Śiva, devotees of the Sun, or devotees of mine, O son of the Sun, / I can render you assistance, but not against devotees of Hari, O son of Bhāskara.
For Puruṣottama is the very origin of all the gods.

2.6.s:
madhusūdanabhaktānāṃ nigraho nopapadyate /
vyājenāpi kṛtā yaistu dvādaśī pakṣayordvayoḥ //
2.6.d:
मधुसूदनभक्तानां निग्रहो नोपपद्यते ।
व्याजेनापि कृता यैस्तु द्वादशी पक्षयोर्द्वयोः ॥
2.6.m: Restraint of the devotees of Madhusūdana is not admissible; / and by those who have observed the Dvādaśī of both fortnights, even under a pretext,

2.6.s:
taiḥ kṛte avamāne tu tava nāhaṃ sahāyavān /
kṛte sahāye tava sūryasūno bhavedanītirmama dehaghātinī /
viparyayo brahmapadātsupuṇyātkṛteva mārge saha viṣṇubhaktaiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge brahmavākyaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
2.6.d:
तैः कृते अवमाने तु तव नाहं सहायवान् ।
कृते सहाये तव सूर्यसूनो भवेदनीतिर्मम देहघातिनी ।
विपर्ययो ब्रह्मपदात्सुपुण्यात्कृतेव मार्गे सह विष्णुभक्तैः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे ब्रह्मवाक्यं नाम षष्ठो ऽध्यायः
2.6.m:
if disrespect has been shown to you by them, I cannot be an ally. / If assistance were given to you, O son of the Sun, there would be unrighteousness destroying my own body, / and a fall from the highly meritorious abode of Brahmā, as it were, on a path [trodden] against the devotees of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, named "The Speech of Brahmā," in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.7.s:
prāptaṃ tāta mayā sārddhaṃ vedāṅghrinamane hitam /
nāhaṃ gacchāmi yogāntaṃ punareva jagatpate //
2.7.d:
प्राप्तं तात मया सार्द्धं वेदाङ्घ्रिनमने हितम् ।
नाहं गच्छामि योगान्तं पुनरेव जगत्पते ॥
2.7.m: Father, the good has been attained together with me by bowing at the feet of the Veda; / I will never go to the end of yoga again, O lord of the world,

2.7.s:
praśāsati mahīṃ bhūpehāṭakāṅgadasaṃjñake /
tamekaṃ devatāśreṣṭhaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare //
2.7.d:
प्रशासति महीं भूपेहाटकाङ्गदसंज्ञके ।
तमेकं देवताश्रेष्ठं संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ॥
2.7.m: while the king named Hāṭakāṅgada rules the earth. / If you shake that one foremost among deities from his steadfastness

2.7.s:
yadi cālayase dhairyāttato 'haṃ tava kiṅkaraḥ /
sa me śatrurmahāndeva tena luptaḥ paṭo mama //
2.7.d:
यदि चालयसे धैर्यात्ततो ऽहं तव किङ्करः ।
स मे शत्रुर्महान्देव तेन लुप्तः पटो मम ॥
2.7.m: when the day of Hari has arrived, then I am your servant. / He is my great enemy, O god; by him my proclamation-cloth has been destroyed.

2.7.s:
tamekaṃ bhojayitvā tu kārṣṇe 'hani mahīpatim /
kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyāmi gayāpiṇḍaprado yathā //
2.7.d:
तमेकं भोजयित्वा तु कार्ष्णे ऽहनि महीपतिम् ।
कृतकृत्यो भविष्यामि गयापिण्डप्रदो यथा ॥
2.7.m: If I can feed that one king on the day of Kṛṣṇa, / then I shall have fulfilled my task, like one offering a piṇḍa at Gayā.

2.7.s:
adya prabhṛti deveśoyairnaraiḥ saṃsmṛto hariḥ /
upoṣitaḥ stutovāpi na niyamyā mayā hi te //
2.7.d:
अद्य प्रभृति देवेशोयैर्नरैः संस्मृतो हरिः ।
उपोषितः स्तुतोवापि न नियम्या मया हि ते ॥
2.7.m: From today onward, O Lord of the gods, those men by whom Hari is remembered, / fasted for, or praised, are truly not to be restrained by me.

2.7.s:
haririti sahasā ye saṃgṛṇanticchalena jananijaṭharamārgātte vimukte vimuktā hi martyāḥ /
mama paṭavilipiṃ te no viśanti pravīṇā divicaravarasaṃghaiste namasyā bhavanti /
sautiruvāca //
2.7.d:
हरिरिति सहसा ये संगृणन्तिच्छलेन जननिजठरमार्गात्ते विमुक्ते विमुक्ता हि मर्त्याः ।
मम पटविलिपिं ते नो विशन्ति प्रवीणा दिविचरवरसंघैस्ते नमस्या भवन्ति ।
सौतिरुवाच ॥
2.7.m:
Those mortals who even once or deceitfully proclaim, 'Hari!', are liberated from the path of the mother's womb; / those skilled ones do not enter the register of my record-cloth, and they are worthy of homage by the host of supreme celestials.
Sauti said:

2.7.s:
vaivasvatasya kāryeṇa tatsammānacikīrṣayayā /
rcitayāmāsa deveśo viriñciḥ kuśalāñchanaḥ //
2.7.d:
वैवस्वतस्य कार्येण तत्सम्मानचिकीर्षयया ।
र्चितयामास देवेशो विरिञ्चिः कुशलाञ्छनः ॥
2.7.m: For the purpose of Vaivasvata, wishing to show him honor, / the Lord of gods, Viriñci, who marks welfare, reflected.

2.7.s:
cintayitvā kṣaṇaṃ devaḥ sarvabhūtaiśca bhūṣitaḥ /
bhūtatrāsanamātraṃ tu rūpaṃ sa jagṛhe vibhuḥ //
2.7.d:
चिन्तयित्वा क्षणं देवः सर्वभूतैश्च भूषितः ।
भूतत्रासनमात्रं तु रूपं स जगृहे विभुः ॥
2.7.m: Having reflected for a moment, the Lord, adorned by all beings, / the almighty one assumed a form that merely brought terror to beings.

2.7.s:
tasminnutpādayāmāsa pramadāṃ lokamohinīm /
sarvayoṣidvarā devīmanasā nirbhitā babhau //
2.7.d:
तस्मिन्नुत्पादयामास प्रमदां लोकमोहिनीम् ।
सर्वयोषिद्वरा देवीमनसा निर्भिता बभौ ॥
2.7.m: In that [form], he produced a woman who enchants the worlds; / best among all women, fashioned by his mind, the goddess shone forth.

2.7.s:
sā babhūvāgratastasya sarvālaṅkārabhīṣitā /
dṛṣṭvā pitāmahastāṃ tu rūpadraviṇasaṃyutām //
2.7.d:
सा बभूवाग्रतस्तस्य सर्वालङ्कारभीषिता ।
दृष्ट्वा पितामहस्तां तु रूपद्रविणसंयुताम् ॥
2.7.m: She stood before him, adorned with every ornament; / seeing her endowed with the treasure of beauty, the Grandfather

2.7.s:
prāhemān paśyato hyetāṃ svakānvai kāmamohitān /
pratyavāyabhayādbrahyā cakṣuṣī saṃnyamīlayat //
2.7.d:
प्राहेमान् पश्यतो ह्येतां स्वकान्वै काममोहितान् ।
प्रत्यवायभयाद्ब्रह्या चक्षुषी संन्यमीलयत् ॥
2.7.m: spoke, beholding those sons of his bewildered by passion; / out of fear of sin, Brahmā closed his eyes.

2.7.s:
sarāgeṇeha manasā sarāgeṇeha cakṣuṣā /
cintayedvīkṣayedvāpi jananīṃ vā sutāmapi //
2.7.d:
सरागेणेह मनसा सरागेणेह चक्षुषा ।
चिन्तयेद्वीक्षयेद्वापि जननीं वा सुतामपि ॥
2.7.m: Whoever, with an impassioned mind or an impassioned eye, / should contemplate or look upon a mother or a daughter,

2.7.s:
vadhūṃ vā bhrātṛjāyāṃ vā gurobhāryāṃ nṛpastriyam /
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ saṃcintya śvapacīmapi //
2.7.d:
वधूं वा भ्रातृजायां वा गुरोभार्यां नृपस्त्रियम् ।
स याति नरकं घोरं संचिन्त्य श्वपचीमपि ॥
2.7.m: or a daughter-in-law, a brother's wife, a guru's wife, or a king's woman, / goes to a dreadful hell, [even] by lusting after an outcast woman.

2.7.s:
dṛṣṭvā hi pramadā hyetā yaḥ kṣobhaṃ vrajate naraḥ /
tasya janmakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛthā bhavati nānyathā //
2.7.d:
दृष्ट्वा हि प्रमदा ह्येता यः क्षोभं व्रजते नरः ।
तस्य जन्मकृतं पुण्यं वृथा भवति नान्यथा ॥
2.7.m: The man who, seeing these women, falls into agitation, / the merit accumulated in his lifetime becomes futile, not otherwise.

2.7.s:
prasaṃge daśasāhasraṃ puṇyamāyāti saṃkṣayam /
puṇyasya saṃkṣayātpāpī pāṣāṇākhurbhaveddhruvam //
2.7.d:
प्रसंगे दशसाहस्रं पुण्यमायाति संक्षयम् ।
पुण्यस्य संक्षयात्पापी पाषाणाखुर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
2.7.m: In illicit attachment, ten thousand [units of] merit go to destruction; / through the destruction of merit, the sinner certainly becomes a rat in a stone.

2.7.s:
tasmānna cintaye tprājño hyetā rāgeṇa cakṣuṣā /
jananyā api pādau tu nādeyau dvādaśābdikaiḥ //
2.7.d:
तस्मान्न चिन्तये त्प्राज्ञो ह्येता रागेण चक्षुषा ।
जनन्या अपि पादौ तु नादेयौ द्वादशाब्दिकैः ॥
2.7.m: Therefore, a wise man should not gaze upon them with eyes of passion; / even the feet of a mother should not be massaged by [sons] twelve years old,

2.7.s:
sutaistvabhyaṅgakaraṇe punaryauvanasaṃsthitaiḥ /
ṣaṣṭyatītāṃ suto 'bhyaṅge niyuñjīta vicakṣaṇaḥ //
2.7.d:
सुतैस्त्वभ्यङ्गकरणे पुनर्यौवनसंस्थितैः ।
षष्ट्यतीतां सुतो ऽभ्यङ्गे नियुञ्जीत विचक्षणः ॥
2.7.m: nor in applying unction by sons established in their youth; / a discerning son should engage [his mother] in applying unction [only when she is] past sixty.

2.7.s:
vṛddho vāpi yuvā vāpi na pādau dhāvayedvadhūm /
ubhayoḥ patanaṃ proktaṃ raurave 'ṅgārasaṃcaye //
2.7.d:
वृद्धो वापि युवा वापि न पादौ धावयेद्वधूम् ।
उभयोः पतनं प्रोक्तं रौरवे ऽङ्गारसंचये ॥
2.7.m: Whether old or young, one should not let a daughter-in-law wash his feet; / the fall of both into the Raurava hell upon a heap of burning coals is proclaimed.

2.7.s:
yā vadhūrdarśayedaṅgaṃ vivṛtaṃ śvaśurasya hi /
pāṇipādāhatā rājan krimibhakṣyā bhavettu sā /
vadhūhastena yaḥ pāpaḥ pādaśaucaṃ karoti hi //
2.7.d:
या वधूर्दर्शयेदङ्गं विवृतं श्वशुरस्य हि ।
पाणिपादाहता राजन् क्रिमिभक्ष्या भवेत्तु सा ।
वधूहस्तेन यः पापः पादशौचं करोति हि ॥
2.7.m: A daughter-in-law who displays an uncovered limb to her father-in-law / shall be beaten hand and foot, O king, and eaten by worms; / the wicked man who has his feet washed by the hand of a daughter-in-law,

2.7.s:
snānaṃ vāpyathavābhyaṅgaṃ tasyāpyevaṃvidhā gatiḥ /
sūcīmukhaiḥ kṛṣṇavaktrorbhujyate kalpasaṃsthitim //
2.7.d:
स्नानं वाप्यथवाभ्यङ्गं तस्याप्येवंविधा गतिः ।
सूचीमुखैः कृष्णवक्त्रोर्भुज्यते कल्पसंस्थितिम् ॥
2.7.m: or a bath or unction [performed by her], meets a similar fate; / he is devoured by needle-mouthed, black-faced beings for the duration of a kalpa.

2.7.s:
tasmānna vīkṣayennārīṃ sutāṃ vāpi vadhūṃ naraḥ /
sābhilāṣeṇa manasā tatkṣaṇātpatate naraḥ //
2.7.d:
तस्मान्न वीक्षयेन्नारीं सुतां वापि वधूं नरः ।
साभिलाषेण मनसा तत्क्षणात्पतते नरः ॥
2.7.m: Therefore, a man should not look at a woman, a daughter, or a daughter-in-law / with a desiring mind; from that moment the man falls.

2.7.s:
evaṃ saṃcintayitvā ca sūkṣmāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ha /
yadidaṃ vartulaṃ vaktraṃ sonnataṃ dṛśyate śubham //
2.7.d:
एवं संचिन्तयित्वा च सूक्ष्मां दृष्टिं चकार ह ।
यदिदं वर्तुलं वक्त्रं सोन्नतं दृश्यते शुभम् ॥
2.7.m: Reflecting thus, he cast subtle insight: / 'That which is seen as this round, prominent, lovely face,

2.7.s:
asthipañjarametaddhi carmamāṃsāvṛtaṃ tviti /
vasā medo 'tha nayane sojvale strīṣu saṃsthite //
2.7.d:
अस्थिपञ्जरमेतद्धि चर्ममांसावृतं त्विति ।
वसा मेदो ऽथ नयने सोज्वले स्त्रीषु संस्थिते ॥
2.7.m: is merely a skeleton of bones covered with skin and flesh; / serum, fat, and eyes shining brightly are situated in women;

2.7.s:
atyucchritamidaṃ māṃsaṃ stanayoḥ samavasthitam /
nimnāṃśatāṃ darśayati trivalī jaṭharasthitā //
2.7.d:
अत्युच्छ्रितमिदं मांसं स्तनयोः समवस्थितम् ।
निम्नांशतां दर्शयति त्रिवली जठरस्थिता ॥
2.7.m: this highly elevated flesh is positioned upon the breasts; / the three folds on the belly show a hollow depression;

2.7.s:
punarevādhikaṃ kṣiptaṃ māṃsaṃ jaghanavatmani /
mūtradvāramidaṃ guhyaṃ yatra mugdhaṃ jagattrayam //
2.7.d:
पुनरेवाधिकं क्षिप्तं मांसं जघनवत्मनि ।
मूत्रद्वारमिदं गुह्यं यत्र मुग्धं जगत्त्रयम् ॥
2.7.m: again, more flesh is cast onto the tract of the hips; / this secret urinary orifice is where the three worlds are deluded.'

2.7.s:
apānavāyunā juṣṭaṃ sadaiva pratikutsitam /
bhastrāvargādhikaṃ kṣiptaṃ māṃsaṃ jaghanavartmani //
2.7.d:
अपानवायुना जुष्टं सदैव प्रतिकुत्सितम् ।
